discoveries.name: vortex scroll sheets (3D)
discoveries.how: vortex-phase mode=1 (radial carrier f*|z|), charge q=3, fr=14, Perlin3 sources A,B; isosurface at 0
discoveries.why: Isosurface is a tightly folded, nested sheet structure like pastry or cortical folds, continuous, with no analogue on the sheet; TPMS and gyroid-like phasor volumes are regular by comparison.

discoveries.name: radial-phasor amplitude net
discoveries.how: ripple-noise mode=2 out=1: |sum e*exp(i*2pi*f*r)| over the 3x3 sites
discoveries.why: Destructive interference between neighbouring ring emitters forms a cellular web of ridges with ring texture inside each cell, like soap film or a dried pond; softer than any CellularDistance edge and with built-in interior detail.

discoveries.name: phasor arms 3 coral
discoveries.how: phasor-noise arms=3 (unit phasor cubed before SinPhase)
discoveries.why: Triples the local frequency and turns every vortex into a 3-arm junction: a brain-coral / chevron labyrinth at two complex multiplies over the base kernel.

discoveries.name: dunes on vortex phase
discoveries.how: Stoss/slip profile and amplitude taper on arg(A+iB) plus a plane carrier: t_transverse_dunes phase=1,sf=.35,F=1,taper=.35,stoss=.8,round=.3,wind=.3; relief --hscale 25
discoveries.why: Tapered crests, Y merges and interdune flats on seeds 42, 9001 and 777, with no lattice gashes. Stock asymmetric waves give ridges but no merges or flats.

discoveries.name: vortex folded agate (3D)
discoveries.how: Replaces the prototyper's scroll params: t_vortex_phase mode=1,fr=30,q=3,boff=.37; vol at window 4
discoveries.why: Nested folded bands like agate or marble on seed 42, also seen on a second seed. Much tighter than the fr14 slabs. Check c0 7.96, range +-.997.

discoveries.name: stock agate recipe
discoveries.how: PingPong(Ping Pong Strength=9.5, Source=PowFloat(Value=Add(PowInt(Pow=2,Value=A),PowInt(Pow=2,Value=B)),Pow=0.5)), with A and B Perlin, B offset and Seed Offset 1
discoveries.why: A cheap graph that gets the same family of nested bands: 4.57 / 7.53 / 12.37 ns AVX2 for 2D/3D/4D. Bands are thicker with some polygon corners. A preset candidate that needs no new node.

discoveries.name: hex arms 2 maze
discoveries.how: Unit phasor squared on the SuperSimplex layout: t_stripes_critic kern=4,k=2,F=1.85,arms=2, window 9.73
discoveries.why: Dense curly maze with no square grid. It has some short cuts. A look raising F does not give, since F x3 goes to faceted polygons, for 2 extra multiplies. A better default than the arms 3 'coral', which is marbled zebra with hard seams.

discoveries.name: stock stained glass cells
discoveries.how: Multiply(PingPong(Ping Pong Strength=8, Source=CellularDistance F2-F1), CellularDistance F2-F1), Feature Scale 51
discoveries.why: Found while looking for an amp net rival. It is not that look: nested polygon cells with pinwheel wedges, decorative. A preset at 9.49 / 26.90 / 82.55 ns AVX2 for 2D/3D/4D.

discoveries.name: radial-phasor amplitude net (confirmed)
discoveries.how: Prototyper's discovery: t_ripple_noise mode=2,out=1,f=4,R=1,jit=1,gain=.8. Needs jitter near 1: at j.5 a rectangular grid shows, j.75 stays good.
discoveries.why: Soft polygon web with moire lines. The closest stock graph I tried gives hard polygons and pinwheels, so this is not a recipe.

discoveries.name: CausticMesh: true multi-sheet caustic as a pointwise function
discoveries.how: Tried to find out whether the real thing can be pointwise at all. A linearised ray splat gave needle artifacts, and flat triangles gave facets. Pushing a fixed window of lattice triangles through the lens, then summing 1/|det| interpolated from the vertices of every triangle that lands on the sample, removed both in the gray view.
discoveries.why: It is the only pointwise function here that draws the true cusped ribbons and bowties. Corr .955 / IoU .70 at D=1.1 on 36 vertices and 50 triangles (s=0.2, R=0.35); R=0.25 shows black gaps; s=0.1 reaches .989. It stays close at high Depth where web departs: .92 at 1.6, .85 at 2.4. Measured scalar 2272 ns = 45.6x perlin2; 3D plane form 3620 ns = 33.8x perlin3. Estimated AVX2 ~70 / ~105 ns, so it is a bake node, not a building block. Flaws: real jumps at mesh fold edges (c0ratio 1.02, max|dv| stalls at 2.07 as h shrinks), and hillshade shows polygon facets, so it is a light map, not a height. 2D and plane 3D only: a true 3D or 4D form would need a window^d of simplices, so it does not tile through GenTileable2D.

discoveries.name: Caustic depth volume: z as water depth
discoveries.how: Set lens strength D = 0.3 z under a fixed surface (w3=2), using CausticMesh. The XZ slice was the surprise.
discoveries.why: The XZ slice shows light shafts that start soft and open into sharp cusp wedges with depth, a view no slice-stable node gives. The same mode on web gives only straight vertical streaks with no wedges, so it needs the mesh. Not stationary in z by design. No truth comparison was made for the XZ view.

discoveries.name: Caustic silk: back map of a field with curl
discoveries.how: Scored fold-caustic against the histogram of its own warp, which showed open filaments rather than cells, so I applied the web back map to the free field.
discoveries.why: Open tapered silk or plasma filaments with soft fans, quite unlike the closed pool net, from the same code with Field = Free. Corr .93 at A=0.5, .79 at A=0.8 against its own truth (Perlin warp at back=3); the saved image uses Simplex. Measured scalar 492 ns with Simplex and 3 steps. Recommended as an enum on CausticWeb.

discoveries.name: Soft web by chain rule
discoveries.how: Replaced the final determinant with |det(dq_M/dy)| carried through the damped back-map steps, so there is no 1/0 and no eps. At step factor 0.5 it stays smooth.
discoveries.why: Soft pool light with no singular line core: corr .93 / IoU .62 on Simplex at D=1.1 (M=4, step factor 0.5). Possibly usable as a soft output mode, at M Hessian evals instead of M gradients plus one Hessian (estimate from eval counts). Continuity and speed were not run on this form. At step factor 0.7 or 1 it rings; see the accident below.

discoveries.name: Double-walled pipes from multi-start back map
discoveries.how: Tried to recover missing sheets with several Picard starts and a soft duplicate count. It did not reach truth (corr .82 to .84, worse than one start at .92), but the lines became doubled tubes with inner threads.
discoveries.why: A look of its own, like a net of glass pipes or vessel walls. It costs K x (M+1) evals: 2 to 8 times a single back-map run. Probably a curiosity rather than a node, kept for reference.

discoveries.name: Contour accident from undamped chain rule
discoveries.how: The chain-rule form at step factor 1, M=3, where the carried determinant crosses zero inside cells.
discoveries.why: A bright soft net overlaid with crisp black worm contours, like a contour map laid over the web. A bug-shaped accident, noted for the record; not recommended as a node.

discoveries.name: Cracked-cell light: the best real-node stand-in for caustics
discoveries.how: Built the honest graph rivals through fnlab: pow(1 - warped F2-F1, 4), the same net multiplied by a remapped Simplex with a weak Simplex floor added, and pow(warped F1/F2, 5).
discoveries.why: Shows plainly what existing nodes can and cannot do here: a crack net with crisp uniform edges, pyramid or flat cell floors and pinched bright blobs at warp folds. Useful as a preset for cracked glass or dried mud lit from below, 10.6 / 23.8 / 61.7 ns AVX2 measured for the modulated version. It is not pool light, which is the evidence the family question needed.

discoveries.name: Newton back map: higher score, worse picture
discoveries.how: Added regularised Newton and Picard-then-Newton candidates (previous version saved as t_caustic_compare.prev.cpp) and scored them against the ray truth at D=1.1 seed 42.
discoveries.why: A negative result worth keeping: Picard+Newton scored .926 / .62 against web/3 at .921 / .53 while showing speckled double edges and junction debris, pure Newton is ragged at .78, and web/4 equals web/3, so damped Picard at 3 steps is the right solver and the corr/IoU metric must not be used alone.

discoveries.name: aniso-simplex-steered
discoveries.how: fractal-slope-aligned with oct=3, aniso=4, sens=3, fo=1, gain=0.7: the first octave's gradient steers an elliptical simplex kernel for the next two octaves (t_fractal_slope_aligned.cpp, ellipSimplex2/3, frame=1)
discoveries.why: A spatially varying anisotropic noise with no window and no absolute-position dependence: palm-leaf / feather fans radiating from each coarse peak. DomainAxisScale can only stretch globally; this stretches per sample along a field direction and stays continuous (c0ratio 8.0). Usable as a steered-grain primitive (fur, feathers, wood grain following a field) beyond terrain.

discoveries.name: strata-flow-marble
discoveries.how: fractal-slope-aligned mode=1 (features compressed along the coarse slope, elongated along contours), aniso=3, sens=2, oct=5, fo=1
discoveries.why: Swirling marble-like flow bands that wrap around every hill, with the fine detail streaming along contour lines: nothing on the existing sheet has detail organised by the landform. Looks like marble, agate, or flow-banded lava; in relief it gives wavy contour ledges.

discoveries.name: coordinate-stretch-scribble (broken, recorded as a warning)
discoveries.how: fractal-slope-aligned frame=0, the catalogue's q' = M q formulation
discoveries.why: Not a node: c0ratio 1.2, maxSlope 667, scribbled swirl texture that gets worse with distance from the origin. The elliptical-kernel form is the fix.

discoveries.name: torus-angle-wrapped-lattice
discoveries.how: The 4D Gen recovers the two torus angles with atan2 from each coordinate pair, then runs the ordinary 2D triangular stripe lattice in those angles with integer wrap counts per octave and an even row count. Base gradient taken along the torus tangents. t_gully_4d.cpp mode=2.
discoveries.why: Answers the handbook's tile problem for a lattice node whose look depends on a 2D direction. Tiles exactly (no seam in the 2x2 view), c0 7.28, and keeps the 2D look, where a hypercubic 4D lattice gives a + weave. Could apply to other 2D-direction lattice nodes (phacelle, flow strokes), untested there. Scalar proof only. It assumes the torus mapping, so general 4D input gets a function of angles.

discoveries.name: wide-stencil-finite-difference
discoveries.how: Compute the source gradient by forward differences with a stencil near the feature wavelength (.2 for a .25 gully wavelength) instead of a tiny epsilon. t_gully_h fd=1,fde=0.2 with boct=5 or bmode=3.
discoveries.why: Turns a limitation into a generic steering input: the node can sit on any rough Source. Ridged4 c0 1.25 to 6.54, fbm5 c0 3.48 to 7.14, at the same 3 evaluations, and the gullied look survives in the images. Applies to any node that steers by a source gradient.

discoveries.name: cone-lattice-imprint-test
discoveries.how: Replace the base with a single cone so the direction field is exactly uniform, then render and measure angular harmonics |c4| and |c6| of the detail gradient. t_gully_h bmode=1, metrics command.
discoveries.why: A test method rather than a node. It shows anisotropy of any direction-driven kernel at a glance, and it caught the 6 fold bias a cos(4 theta) metric misses: square hist max/min 2.50, triangular 2.33 at one octave. Worth using on the other stripe and flow lattice ideas.

discoveries.name: phacelle-angle-zebra
discoveries.how: Drive the phacelle kernel from an angle field made of slow noise instead of a source gradient. t_gully_h angle=1,oct=1,out=3,sloperef=0.
discoveries.why: No critical points means no singular hairlines: c0 7.8-8.0 against 1.40-1.51 for the gradient-driven raw output. Clean zebra or labyrinth stripes. Honest limit: mean +.54, lattice rows show when the field is nearly straight, and the stripes family already holds this niche, so it does not justify a node on its own.

discoveries.name: DrainageFrame domain operator
discoveries.how: While adding local frames for fern-fold and catchment-rivers, I sampled a plain stretched Perlin fractal at (position along the trunk, distance from the trunk) instead of growing branches or computing area.
discoveries.why: Streaks run down into every trunk and the relief looks eroded, close to catchment-rivers elevation but with no walkers. Scalar 2166 ns, measured before stochastic descent, against 3236-3614 ns. Any source could be made to follow the drainage this way. 0 true jumps in the scan. Trunks are still straight and the relief is somewhat grainier than catchment.

discoveries.name: Stochastic descent
discoveries.how: To attack star-shaped sinks, a per-cell hash mask limits which neighbours a cell may drain to, falling back to all neighbours if none of those is lower.
discoveries.why: Neighbours of a minimum stop running straight into it, so spokes merge earlier and hubs mostly dissolve into confluences, with no cycles because every link stays strictly downhill. It works on every steepest-descent tree here. Judged by eye on a few seeds. The image compares sub=0/1 against Perlin and hash controls.

discoveries.name: Canyonlands carve
discoveries.how: An over-strong carve setting on dendry with a 5x5 level 0: vd=0.7, vw=6, br=0.8 on the hash valley control.
discoveries.why: Flat-topped mesas cut by steep winding canyons, a striking landform different from the intended river valleys. Some needle-like spikes appear on canyon edges.

discoveries.name: Feather contours
discoveries.how: Parallel fern-fold under a large low-frequency warp, tried to remove its bands. It did not remove them.
discoveries.why: Long flowing streamlines with tapered feathery branches, resembling a pen drawing of plumes or windswept treelines. Useless as rivers, possibly a distinct cheap line texture. Strongly anisotropic in the FFT.

discoveries.name: Strata ribbons
discoveries.how: Flow-network under warp 16 at frequency 0.03, the failure case of the family question.
discoveries.why: The strained lattice becomes thick-to-thin calligraphic ribbons like agate or brush strokes, with line width varying through the width growth. Not rivers, but an unusual look from a cheap kernel.

discoveries.name: Per-segment local width (dendry wmode=1)
discoveries.how: Level-0 width grows with the control height relative to the segment's own 3x3 min/max instead of the absolute height. The 3x3 is inside the 5x5 control window already evaluated, so it is free; the first version using the sample's 5x5 min/max seamed at cell edges and was replaced.
discoveries.why: Removes the drift-following fat/thin zones at the wide view (seed 42, 96 cells) so the tree covers the frame evenly with trunk/twig hierarchy; close view unchanged; 0 true jumps; 2743 vs 2700 ns. It equalises texture, it does not add discharge hierarchy. Keep it as the default width mode in a port.

discoveries.name: DrainageFrame domain operator (prototyper's, endorsed)
discoveries.how: Sample any source at (along trunk, distance from trunk) from the steepest-descent trunk frame, no walkers.
discoveries.why: Its relief is close to catchment elevation at lower cost and would let any user source follow drainage. FastNoise only has vector output in the DomainWarp family, so this would have to be a warp node whose offset is (u,v) minus (x,y); the per-segment fades make it seam-free in the prototype. Worth a follow-up more than catchment-rivers itself.

discoveries.name: Order-2 kite mosaic
discoveries.how: t_edge_fate_cells mode=4: value = rnd11 of the symmetric hash of (F1 hash, hash of the neighbour across the nearest bisector), both free by-products of the exact edge pass
discoveries.why: Every Voronoi cell is split into kite-shaped sectors facing each neighbour, a flat mosaic within the mosaic that no existing value mode produces, at zero extra cost once the bisector pass exists (order-2 Voronoi region id)

discoveries.name: Jointed strata (recursive-cut without a root)
discoveries.how: t_recursive_cut_noise --set root=0,f=0.7,lac=1.5,levels=6,skip=0 --window 16 (the failure mode of the idea as proposed)
discoveries.why: The global level-0 family that kills it as a shatter node gives long parallel beds crossed by shorter joints that stop at the beds, which reads as jointed sedimentary strata or columnar cliff faces; window-free and ~2.5 ns estimated in any dimension, so a Strata/Joints mode of CellularShatter with no root might be worth keeping

discoveries.name: Simplex-window Voronoi
discoveries.how: Sites on the simplex lattice, searching only the D+1 corners of the sample's simplex plus the D+1 vertices across its faces: 6 / 8 / 10 sites instead of 9 / 27 / 81. Face-opposite vertex is c_(m-1) + c_(m+1) - c_m with indices cyclic. Rings 0.28 / 0.17 / 0.14. style=1 adds plane cuts, style=2 nests levels.
discoveries.why: Could make Voronoi masks affordable in 3D and 4D. Scalar 3D 309 ns against 871 ns, 2D 269 ns against 364 ns; my estimate is about 5 / 7 / 10 ns AVX2, unported. F1 and min(e, 0.10) had 0 wrong in 1.5M / 300k / 40k samples and 0 jumps in 2M 2D and 500k 3D samples. Only clamped masks are exact: unclamped distance is wrong on 0.1-2.6% of samples at these rings. The 32-unit root view shows no lattice but more even cells than the square window; the nested 3D vol at ring 0.17 is near honeycomb, shards look fine. 4D is a geometry audit only, with no Eval4 render.

discoveries.name: T-junction cracks from existing nodes
discoveries.how: Min( Mask( L0 ), DomainOffset( Source = Mask( L1 ), Offset X = CellularValue( same cells as L0, Output +-4000 ) ) ), nested three levels. The per-parent-cell offset breaks the child network at each parent wall, and the deeper parent mask covers the jump.
discoveries.why: A shippable preset today with real hierarchical T-junctions: relief reads as cracked mud, vol as angular blocks. 35 / 106 / 345 ns AVX2, check 0 FAIL at scale 8, continuity 6.6-7.0. Parent walls stay fat with F2-F1 wedges, and the same trick over an exact edge pass removes them (t_critic2_nested style 0). Using CellularLookup of White instead fails SIMD parity, so the recipe keeps CellularValue.

discoveries.name: Site-colour merged walls (a continuous Edge Drop)
discoveries.how: Colour each site from hash bits or a terraced source. d = max( e, kd * ( F_other - F1 ) ) with F_other the nearest site of a different colour. metric=2,kd=0.8,colours=3,mode=1 for crease.
discoveries.why: Merges plates and gives parent and child walls with no vertex jumps, replacing the per-wall hash: c0 8.00 and 0 jumps above 0.2 in 3M 2D and 800k 3D samples at kd 0.2 or more, against c0 1.0 for Edge Drop. Costs one compare per stored site. Keep width / kd small enough for the window to see the other colour.

discoveries.name: Tapered-tip cracks
discoveries.how: mode=5,width=0.05,bias=0.15: m = smoothstep of a low-frequency noise at the sample; crack = m * profile( e / ( W * ( wmin + ( 1 - wmin ) * m ) ) ). In a node this is just hybrid Edge Width and Edge Depth over the exact edge distance.
discoveries.why: The best dangling-crack look in the family, with tips that narrow as they fade, and relief that reads as dried mud. C0 by construction, measured 7.66-7.93, with no per-wall state. Bias sweeps from isolated cracks to a nearly closed network.

discoveries.name: Jointed strata at low levels
discoveries.how: root=0,f=0.7,lac=1.5,levels=3,skip=0,jitter=0.5,taper=0.75,width=0.04
discoveries.why: The prototyper's strata discovery at 6 levels is hatch at low zoom; levels 3 is clean jointed slabs with no window, c0 7.98. The graph attempt gives zigzag walls, not long straight beds. Proposed as a free-angle cut mode of TileSplit.

discoveries.name: Percolation hull walls
discoveries.how: metric=2,kd=0.8,width=0.05,colours=2 at a 24-unit window
discoveries.why: With two colours the walls become long meandering polygonal curves with loops, a look nothing else in the family gives, at c0 8.0. Possibly useful for coastlines or winding seams. Only seen in 2D and a 3D slice; a curiosity, not a reason to add anything beyond the Colours parameter.

discoveries.name: TubeNetwork (min over channel pairs)
discoveries.how: Measuring connectivity showed true tubes are disconnected loops (largest air 28-50%). Taking 3 channels and the minimum distance over pairs makes the curve families meet where all three channels vanish.
discoveries.why: Restores connectivity to 90-95% while keeping round sections (aspect 1.25-1.29 vs 2.3-2.4). Should be a mode of TubeNoise, and it is the best spaghetti cave result in the family.

discoveries.name: Value-term shared lattice
discoveries.how: Predicted from kernel radius against vertex spacing that all same-lattice channels vanish at every vertex, then added a per-vertex constant from spare hash bits to each channel's contribution.
discoveries.why: Removes the common zero at vertices with no extra lattice visit. On Perlin, tube quality matches two lattices (radius CV .132 vs .130). Applies to any multi-channel gradient noise in FastNoise.

discoveries.name: TubeRope
discoveries.how: Modulating the radius by the angle in channel space, atan2(n1,n0) with 6 ribs.
discoveries.why: Ribbed strands that twist along the tube, reading as rope, cable or muscle fibre. A striking look from one extra atan2-style approximation; not explored beyond this render.

discoveries.name: TubePipe
discoveries.how: Band of the distance field around the radius, |d-R| below a wall thickness.
discoveries.why: Hollow pipes with visible ring sections, possible only because d is a real distance. Vein or hose look.

discoveries.name: World-unit rough tunnels
discoveries.how: Added 3 octaves of noise to the distance before thresholding.
discoveries.why: Because d is in world units, the roughness has the same relief everywhere on the tube, which gives believable lumpy cave or worm-coral walls. Works as a plain Add in a graph on the Distance output.

discoveries.name: Constant width canyons
discoveries.how: 2D codim 1 Distance output viewed with relief.
discoveries.why: Wandering channels of constant width and a flat plateau, which Abs of noise cannot do because its width follows the local gradient.

discoveries.name: Hash-free spaghetti and network
discoveries.how: Crossbreed: tube distance to the common zero set of two (or three) gyroids in rotated frames.
discoveries.why: Clean worm tangle with no lattice and no hash, literally from coordinates alone. No obvious repeat by eye at window 12, but its periodicity was not measured. The prototype uses finite differences at 317 ns scalar. An analytic port would be about 12 trig plus algebra, likely no cheaper than the Perlin form (estimate, not measured).

discoveries.name: Tubes on a gyroid
discoveries.how: Crossbreed: tube distance to the intersection of a warped gyroid and a Perlin field, so curves live on the minimal surface.
discoveries.why: Works and gives sparse long worms, but it does not look obviously better than plain tubes. Recorded as a curiosity, not a recommendation.

discoveries.name: Gyroid from existing nodes (graph recipe)
discoveries.how: SineWave is sin(x/S)*sin(y/S)*sin(z/S), so RemoveDimension gives two-axis products and a DomainOffset of S*pi/2 turns a sine into a cosine. Add of three such terms is the exact gyroid; verified in fnlab vol and bench.
discoveries.why: Shows the plain TPMS look is already reachable (11 nodes, 3.86/3.69/4.87 ns AVX2) and can be warped with the existing DomainWarp nodes. It frames TPMSNoise as a convenience and 2x speed node rather than a new primitive, and it is a usable preset today.

discoveries.name: RootStrands (bond-tunnels Tree mode with vertical parent bias)
discoveries.how: t_bond_tunnels.exe vol --window 8 --set inv=1,mode=1,ybias=6,rmin=0.08,rmax=0.14,warp=0.25,wfreq=1.2,warp2=0.8,wfreq2=0.25 ; the Tree link rule picks the vertical axis as parent 6x more often than the others, then a two-octave warp bends the strands
discoveries.why: The in-view disconnected forest that is a weakness for caves becomes a feature: a dense mass of hanging, wavering vertical strands with occasional side links, like roots, hair or drips, that no existing node or simple graph gives (Cellular Manhattan or axis-scaled noise does not produce separate continuous fibres). Code lives in the bond-tunnels prototype (ybias param); would be the Vertical Bias member of the BondTunnels node.

discoveries.name: RootStrands (prototyper's, verified)
discoveries.how: t_bond_tunnels.exe vol --window 8 --set inv=1,mode=1,ybias=6,rmin=0.08,rmax=0.14,warp=0.25,wfreq=1.2,warp2=0.8,wfreq2=0.25
discoveries.why: Holds on seeds 99 and 2024 and at window 14: separate, round, wavering vertical fibres. Real graph rivals I tried do not match it: a y-stretched noodle gives draped sheets and y-stretched F3-F1 gives straight needles. Niche, and it comes free with Link=Tree plus a Vertical Bias in bond-tunnels.

discoveries.name: Noodle cave from existing nodes
discoveries.how: Add(LHS=Multiply(LHS=a,RHS=a),RHS=Multiply(LHS=b,RHS=b)) with a, b = Perlin at different Seed Offset, cave where value <= iso (0.017 is about 11% void). Full text in the .txt beside the image.
discoveries.why: A graph preset, no new node. 99.99-100.00% in the core at 11% void, 99.94-99.98% at 8%, 97.88-99.21% at 5%, collapses at 2.5% (0.13-6.43%). 9.29 ns AVX2 measured, no lattice, no warp. Tube width follows the local gradient, so it has flanged webs, not constant round tubes. It is the bar any tube network node must beat above about 8% void.

discoveries.name: Curtain caves (y-stretched noodle)
discoveries.how: DomainAxisScale(Scaling Y=0.18, Source=Add(Multiply(a,a), Multiply(b,b))), Feature Scale 38, iso 0.0075 in the pipes view. Bottom row of the comparison image.
discoveries.why: An accident while hunting a root strand rival: hanging draped sheets, flowstone like, 9.17 ns AVX2 measured, existing nodes only. Connectivity not measured. A preset at most.

discoveries.name: Bedding warp: y-only warp for any layered node
discoveries.how: t_strata_caverns.exe vol --seed 7 --window 12 --set H=1,base=0.2,height=0.6,cov=0.25,gain=2,pf=0.35,oct=2,S=1.5,rs=0.22,ps=0.9,sjit=0.5,smask=1,smooth=0.05,ya=1.6,yf=0.3,dip=2.2,dipf=0.09,w3=0.1,w3f=0.8. Real nodes: DomainOffset Y fed by Perlin with Scaling X = Z = 0, then DomainWarpGradient with Amplitude Scaling X = Z = 0.
discoveries.why: A warp depending on y alone varies layer thickness and keeps floors perfectly flat; the dip then tilts the beds. It removes the periodic ruler from anything sliced in y, and turned strata into convincing sedimentary bedding. Applies to the graph recipe too.

discoveries.name: Two scale bond graph (the spine mode in the same image failed)
discoveries.how: t_bond_tunnels.exe vol --seed 99 --window 10 --set mode=0,p=0.6,rmin=0.1,rmax=0.17,chamber=0.2,hub=0.12,jit=0.12,stub=0.25,smooth=0.04,rot=1,rw=1,warp2=1.25,wfreq2=0.6,warp=0.15,wfreq=2.4,coarse=3,mf=0.15,mt=0. Graph: Min(coarse net, Max(fine net, low frequency mask)).
discoveries.why: The one thing that broke the uniform weave density the prototyper flagged: rock regions, big galleries and fine side passages, 99.45-99.71% in the core (margin 2 cells), no seam, no hybrid chance needed. Coarse tubes turn slab-like under the same warp, so the pipes view is messy; the cave view is the better one. Estimated about 24 ns from measured parts. The image also shows mode 3 spine, which looks the same as tree under warp and is not a discovery.

discoveries.name: Perpendicular pairs direction table
discoveries.how: Tried to explain why Feistel had far lower grain than golden shear chains. In 2D Feistel is a chain whose directions come in perpendicular pairs, so I gave that table to the other kernels.
discoveries.why: Same cost, and global streak drops: noise 8 grain R 0.072 to 0.018, parabola 8 at amp 1 0.093 to 0.017, stretch noise 8 0.21 to 0.075. It makes marble with no per seed grain.

discoveries.name: Rising strain removes straight bands
discoveries.how: The stretch field wide view had long straight diagonal bands. Step 1's lines stay straight in input space and later steps are bent by earlier ones, so I gave the earliest steps the least strain (gain above 1 with lacunarity above 1).
discoveries.why: The bands went away in the wide views, which is what moved lyapunov-stretch to keeper. Stretch field autocorrelation beyond 16 units at 8 steps is 0.059, and the bands were not visible at a 32 unit window.

discoveries.name: Parabolic wave kernel
discoveries.how: Measured FS::Sin in a chain at about 1 ns per step and looked for a cheaper periodic shear profile: t*(8 - 16*Abs(t)).
discoveries.why: Estimated 3.3 ns against 7.9 ns at 8 steps in 2D, with a nearly identical look on FBm. It keeps det=1, and is C1 only with no visible effect. Its period is the same, so it has the same repeat problem as sine.

discoveries.name: Stretch fur
discoveries.how: Lyapunov stretch with the golden parabola chain, lac 1.4, 12 steps, k 0.5: chain=3,steps=12,amp=0.6,form=2,bounded=1,k=0.5.
discoveries.why: Dense directional hair with clumps and partings, at an estimated 7.7/8.9/10.4 ns with no source. Strongest fur look in the family. Its wide view shows some herringbone regularity.

discoveries.name: Stretch weave
discoveries.how: The same fur with the perpendicular pairs table (spairs=1). The plaid that is a flaw elsewhere shows up on purpose.
discoveries.why: The wide view reads as woven basket cloth with hair texture inside each patch. Could be a fabric look.

discoveries.name: Stretch agate bands
discoveries.how: Pushing the golden noise chain to amp 1, 16 steps, k 0.35 at a 6 unit window.
discoveries.why: Many thin parallel flowing dark lines on white, like agate or wood grain. It aliases: c0ratio 1.5.

discoveries.name: FTLE fingerprint cells
discoveries.how: An accident of too large a step: gradient flow FTLE at eta 0.2, N 8, where descent appears to overshoot inside each basin.
discoveries.why: Each cell fills with spiral fingerprint ridges inside a bright boundary. The threshold looks like zebra thumbprints, and I have seen nothing like it elsewhere. The 3D slice at these settings shows cells without rings, so 3D is unsolved. Costs about 9x Perlin scalar, and c0ratio is 1.7. The overshoot cause is my inference, not tested.

discoveries.name: Basin foam
discoveries.how: Isosurface of 3D gradient flow FTLE at iso 0.3: field=1,eta=0.12,N=8,k=0.2,o=0.
discoveries.why: An open cell foam whose walls follow the divides of the noise basins, with cells of irregular size. Expensive at 2943 ns scalar with finite differences, 29x perlin3.

discoveries.name: Periodic shear curls
discoveries.how: Reusing the same three noises with three directions at 60 degrees: per=1,steps=21,amp=0.45,freq=1. In 3D I tried x += n0(y), y += n1(z), z += n2(x).
discoveries.why: Curling smoke with spiral eyes and a marbled paper threshold, the only curls among the warps here. c0ratio 3.6, and 21 steps is about 23 ns warp only (estimate). 9 steps already curls, at about 10 ns (estimate). Worth keeping as Direction=Periodic3.

discoveries.name: Fur graph recipe from existing nodes
discoveries.how: Built the closest thing existing nodes give to lyapunov-stretch: DomainWarpFractalProgressive(Octaves=3, Domain Warp Source=DomainWarpSimplex(Feature Scale=180, Warp Amplitude=20..40, Source=DomainAxisScale(Scaling Y=0.12, Source=FractalRidged(Octaves=3, Source=Perlin(Feature Scale=14))))), rendered with fnlab at amplitudes 1, 20, 40, 80.
discoveries.why: Amp 20 gives wavy vertical hair strands with one global direction; amp 40 gives swirled fibre bundles with ring folds. It is what a technical artist would do today for hair or brushed metal, and it shows what lyapunov-stretch adds: locally curving fibre direction with branching dark creases and no global grain. Amp 80 breaks into mush.

discoveries.name: Facet shatter warp
discoveries.how: DomainWarpSource with a Cellular F1 potential: grad F1 is the unit vector from the nearest site, so Gradient mode shears each Voronoi cell radially and Curl mode rotates each cell about its site. t_domain_warp_source.exe grid mode=0,1 --set pot=2,A=0.5 (bands) and --set pot=2,A=0.5,src=1 (fBm).
discoveries.why: Bands and fBm break into Voronoi shards with tears at the cell edges: broken glass / cut-gem / cubist facets. No existing node or graph can shift or rotate a source per Voronoi cell (CellularLookup samples one value per cell, it cannot warp a texture per cell). Comes free as a Potential choice of DomainWarpSource.

discoveries.name: Fluted cones (frost stars)
discoveries.how: Very small amplitude FD curl of a 4-octave Perlin fBm potential applied to a Worley F1 source: t_domain_warp_source.exe grid A=0.05,0.08,0.12 --set pot=1,mode=1,po=4,src=3. The finest octave dominates the gradient so the displacement is fine-grained but area preserving.
discoveries.why: The gray field shows cells turned into star-shaped frost crystals; the hillshade reads as a field of eroded volcanic cones with fluted, gullied flanks, a terrain look (cinder-cone field) that F1 cones plus any existing warp do not give because the existing warps move whole regions rather than adding incompressible fine wrinkles.

discoveries.name: Jupiter storms (jets plus storms in the potential)
discoveries.how: Flow stir of psi = stretched Perlin + bent zonal jets + sparse oval discs. t_domain_warp_flow.exe thumb --set ang=90,steps=12,L=1.2,pot=3,U=2.5,zb=.5,sx=.5,pf=1.5,bf=.5,jm=.6,sG=6,sc=.25,sd=.8
discoveries.why: Bands roll up at their edges and wrap around large spirals, so the eddies grow from the flow rather than being stamped on. Five of six seeds show a large spiral, and it holds at window 24. Scalar 2526 ns; jets without storms as a real graph are 190 nodes and 53.15 ns AVX2 at 6 steps, so only a Potential node makes this usable.

discoveries.name: Cushion plates (plain gradient descent)
discoveries.how: Few unnormalised descent steps of an analytic Perlin potential, on any source: t_domain_warp_curl.exe thumb --set kind=1,steps=5,A=-1,src=3 or kind=1,steps=8,A=-1.67,src=1
discoveries.why: Leaded-glass plates with corner fans at low steps, flat curved catchments at 12. No normalise, decay or basin output needed. Rivals differ: a gradient of F1 squared graph (13 nodes, 18.72 ns) has straight polygon edges. Plates sit in rough rows from the Perlin lattice, and relief draws comb at the cliffs, so this is a material look more than terrain.

discoveries.name: Same-seed warp chain plates with spiral eyes (recipe)
discoveries.how: Chain DomainWarpSimplex(Feature Scale=130, Warp Amplitude=14) 10-12 times with the same seed around any source. 12 links measured 21.62 / 60.92 / 132.06 ns AVX2, 13 nodes with the source.
discoveries.why: Existing nodes alone give plates with curved borders and spiral eyes, a distinct look with a ray FFT. No new node needed; worth a preset.

discoveries.name: Facet shatter (recipe, reclassified from the report)
discoveries.how: DomainOffset by Multiply of Subtract of an offset Euclidean F1, 12 nodes, 18.12 ns AVX2 on SineWave. Or a per-cell shift with two CellularValue offsets, 4 nodes, 21.10 ns, for straight fault lines. Seed 2024 panel.
discoveries.why: Pinwheel or shard facets per Voronoi cell, close to the prototype apart from wider breaks in place of thin tears. The look is real; the report's claim that no graph can make it is not.

discoveries.name: Fluted cones (recipe, reclassified from the report)
discoveries.how: Forward-difference curl of a 4-octave Perlin fBm applied to Euclidean F1, 16 nodes, 21.21 / 58.96 / 114.29 ns AVX2.
discoveries.why: Star-shaped pits with fluted flanks in relief, the same family as the prototype. Independent fractal warps give blobby cells instead, so the recipe is worth a preset for terrain.

discoveries.name: Scale beads from Min of ring taps (minor recipe)
discoveries.how: Min of a Perlin source with itself at 8-12 offsets on one or two rings, 25-55 nodes, 12.37-23.75 ns AVX2. The largest case passes fnlab check with 0 FAIL, 0 WARN.
discoveries.why: I tried this as a continuous replacement for basins and it failed: instead of flat floors it gives beads and reptile scales inside each basin. Usable as a material texture; as terrain it is rows of pimples.

discoveries.name: Penrose curve mask
discoveries.how: QuasiTile output 8: in each rhomb, arcs centred on its lowest and highest index corners, with radius taken from a 3-entry table indexed by vertex index. Each edge is crossed at a position that depends only on its index level, and a circle centred on a corner crosses that corner's edges at a right angle, so arcs join smoothly across tiles. Table r1=.1, r2=.5, r3=.9.
discoveries.why: Continuous curves over an aperiodic tiling: gear-shaped rings and long meanders, with small knots at some vertices. Mask c0ratio 7.81, so no jumps. Limits: only tested at N=5 with zero-sum gamma, where the vertex index census gives 1 and 2 only. The distance-field form (output 9) has c0ratio 1.03, so it has jumps; its relief looks good but is not clean. Only the tube mask should be trusted.

discoveries.name: Analytic lattice distance
discoveries.how: MultigridNoise mode 6 and 7: distance to the nearest Z^N point computed one family at a time, sqrt(sum min(f,1-f)^2) or the Manhattan sum. This is what DomainQuasicrystal with Cellular J=0 computes through an 81-cell search.
discoveries.why: Soft crystal rosettes with sharp FFT spots at any N, in O(N), any dimension. c0ratio 8.0. N=7 and 9 give large ring motifs; threshold shows clean rings. Normalised analytically, range about -0.86..0.79. Recommended as an output of the shipped node.

discoveries.name: Multigrid Lookup at dual vertex
discoveries.how: MultigridNoise mode 9 and 10: evaluate a source once at the region's dual vertex scaled back to grid space, the multigrid analogue of CellularLookup.
discoveries.why: A smooth source quantised into polygon plates. Threshold gives large blobs whose outlines are made of tile edges, and a low frequency structure visible in the wide view. c0ratio 7.9 when grouted. The source here is a fixed 3-octave Perlin, so a source input has not been tried. In this proto Eval3 does not have the mode, so the sheet's 3D panel is blank.

discoveries.name: Nested multigrid terrazzo
discoveries.how: Coarse multigrid regions hash to decide whether to overlay a finer rotated multigrid (nest=2 or 3, split probability .35 to .6). Fine lines end at coarse region boundaries.
discoveries.why: Reads as terrazzo or aggregate: big polygons set in fine gravel. No long lines at fine scale and a nearly blob FFT. c0ratio 7.8. Cost is a fixed loop of nest + 1 multigrids. The 2D view only; Eval3 ignores nest, so the 3D panel does not show it.

discoveries.name: Phason parity weave
discoveries.how: MultigridNoise Parity with a strong phason, J=1.6 L=5. Each line flip changes parity, so the two-colouring stays valid however far the lines bend.
discoveries.why: Bold black and white curved weave with checker patches, FFT close to a plain blob. Cheap and hard edged, c0ratio 1.0 by design. Good for masks.

discoveries.name: Fractal Penrose shards
discoveries.how: Robinson descent with hashed stop depth (D=12, minD=8, stop=.25). This requires counting the rhomb diagonal as an edge, because the two halves can stop at different depths. Hash stop also breaks the periodicity of the stop=0 tiling.
discoveries.why: Penrose triangles at many scales with 5-fold stars at each, which QuasiTile cannot do. c0ratio 7.8 grouted. It is the best argument for keeping Robinson as a kind inside SubstitutionTiling. Only the 2D form was tried.

discoveries.name: Prism3 3D substitution
discoveries.how: My own 8-child dissection of a 30-60-90 prism into half-scale copies with a 60 degree turn about z and a 90 degree turn about x. Written from my memory of the idea behind Conway and Radin's tiling, not checked against the paper.
discoveries.why: A pointwise 3D hierarchical tile with exact congruent children: 2M random points, 0 outside the child prism, each child .1246-.1252 of the volume. Its 2D slice reads as shards, while the volume is hard to read and orientations stay far from uniform at usable depth (D=8 bands .218 .005 .344 .062 .372). Useful as the 3D form of the node, not as evidence of isotropy.

discoveries.name: Penrose terraces (QuasiTile tile-centre Lookup as relief)
discoveries.how: QuasiTile out=10: a 3-octave Perlin sampled once at the rhomb centre (the CellularLookup analogue), grouted, rendered as terrain with lscale=0.25 width=0.04 best=1 N=5.
discoveries.why: Stepped rhomb plateaus following a smooth field: the most terrain-like image in the family and a look CellularLookup cannot give because every step is a Penrose rhomb. c0ratio 7.9 grouted. Only tried at N=5 with a fixed source; a Source input has not been wired.

discoveries.name: Octagonal quasicrystal ornament as a graph of existing nodes
discoveries.how: AddDimension(Source=AddDimension(Source=Checkerboard(Feature Scale=24), New Dimension Position=Gradient(Multiplier X=0.7071, Multiplier Y=0.7071)), New Dimension Position=Gradient(Multiplier X=-0.7071, Multiplier Y=0.7071)) evaluated in 2D is a linear cut of Z^4 along the 8-fold star.
discoveries.why: Reproduces DomainQuasicrystal sym=8 Checkerboard and MultigridNoise Parity N=4 with no new node, rendered on the real DLL. The same cut turns any 4D source into a 4-family quasi-pattern (CellularDistance J=0 gives the lattice-distance rosettes). Costs the 4D source; 5-fold and 7-fold are not reachable this way.

discoveries.name: stamp-k1-foam
discoveries.how: t_stamp_scatter with K=1,src=1,Rmin=0.4: the rank-subtract fade at K=1 subtracts the runner-up mask from the winner
discoveries.why: Domes of mixed size pressed together with sharp creases where the strongest mask changes hands, like a bubble raft or foam; the crease network is size-weighted so it is not plain Voronoi. Cheap (one source eval). Modest novelty: close to inverted CellularDistance F1 with size jitter, so a mode rather than a node.

discoveries.name: flow-strokes-curl
discoveries.how: t_flow_shingle with shape=1,elong=3,size=0.45,bristle=0.2,detail=0.1,flow=3,ff=0.2,jit=0.6: per-lane angle sampling bends each straight stroke into the field
discoveries.why: Tapered strokes with bristle grooves that curl into flame and swirl shapes, an illustration look nothing on the existing contact sheet approaches; it falls out of flow-shingle at high flow amplitude with no extra cost.

discoveries.name: cascade-fade
discoveries.how: t_stamp_scatter fadep=3,fc=2 (now default): w_K = min(m_K, fc*(m_K - m_(K+1))), w_j = min(m_j, fc*(m_j - m_(j+1)) + w_(j+1))
discoveries.why: Top-K selection that stays C0 yet thins a stamp only when it is itself tied with the rank below. K=2 keeps .80 of the mask mass against .63 for rank subtract at mean overlap 4.91, with the same source evals. Any node doing K-limited blending could reuse it.

discoveries.name: chisel-rubble
discoveries.how: t_grounded_scatter facet=6,fixn=1,cut=0.68,aspect=0.35,size=0.5,dens=0.9,k=0.02,sink=0.4,tilt=0: cut each stone by fixed icosahedron axes in its own rotated frame, hashed offsets only
discoveries.why: Reads as angular broken rock and scree rather than eggs, at +17% scalar. Per-stone rotated faceting is not available from a graph. 0 of 387 stones floating.

discoveries.name: pebble-max-tops
discoveries.how: t_pebble_pile rmin=0.25,layers=8,sizej=0.3,comp=1: height is the max of stone tops, not the first covering layer
discoveries.why: A continuous pebble heightfield with no cliffs, at one hash per layer and no window. It gives the Max-of-Cellular-domes look with rotated, aspect-jittered stones. Rim is sqrt so c0ratio reads 2.8-3.1, not a jump.

discoveries.name: graph-rigid-stones
discoveries.how: Real nodes: Max(terrain Gradient, r^2 - F1^2 - (y + CellularLookup(Height) + offset)^2), with RemoveDimension Y on all cellular nodes and SeedOffset 1 on the terrain Height, because CellularLookup runs its source at seed+1.
discoveries.why: Stones keep their shape instead of shearing with the hill, unlike the earlier graph that sampled Height per lane. 36.8 ns AVX2 3D measured. Spheres only, with cut faces at Voronoi edges, so a recipe for sparse boulders and not a replacement for the node.

discoveries.name: graph-quadtree-blocks
discoveries.how: Real nodes: 4 CellularValue with Grid Jitter 0 at scales 64, 32, 16, 8, nested by DomainOffset of half the cell size, chosen by 3 CellularValue masks through thresholded Fade.
discoveries.why: A hierarchical block layout and city relief from stock nodes. 72 / 227 / 743 ns AVX2 measured, so usable offline only, and it is the reason quad-stamp's case rests on cost.

discoveries.name: stamp-patchwork-k1
discoveries.how: t_stamp_scatter K=1,src=3,R=1.25,jit=0.5,Rmin=0.7,fc=8: one source eval per lane with a sharp cascade
discoveries.why: Modest novelty. Patches of differently oriented stripes with hairline seams, like woven or parquet tiles, at the cost of one source eval. Rows of the lattice show at jit .5. A setting, not a mode worth naming.

discoveries.name: NestedCracks (hierarchical crack plates)
discoveries.how: Mutated PuffyCaps so each level's lattice lives in the local frame of the cap that owns the sample: position relative to the owner, scaled by its radius, seeded by its hash. Children fade to zero at the owner's boundary. Output with crack=1 is flat plates with a groove at every level. Grooves taper naturally, since their width depends on how far apart the two sites are.
discoveries.why: This is the strongest surprise in the family. Cracks at every scale never cross a parent crack, and wedge-shaped grooves read as dried mud or cracked basalt in relief, while 3D gives a fractured rock mass. FBm of F2-F1 crosses its cracks and no simple graph I can think of could nest them, because the child needs the owner's identity. Measured c0ratio 5.25, but max slope 164 because fine grooves are very steep. Scalar 374 ns 2D. Estimated AVX2 16/52/170 ns at 4 levels, from handbook Cellular costs.

discoveries.name: NestedCaps (self-similar florets and split boulders)
discoveries.how: Same local-frame mutation with the cap dome kept as output. Small lobes carry proportionally small sub-lobes, and children vanish at creases.
discoveries.why: Height view is hierarchical cells, like a tortoise shell or leaded glass, with rounded boulders in relief. In 3D it gives split blocks of stone. Clearly unlike FBm, and a graph cannot pass the owner frame down. c0ratio 7.1 with soft=0.1, max slope 29.4. Scalar 297 ns 2D (measured before soft was added, at rmin=0.7, edge=0.15) and 586 ns 3D. Plain PuffyCaps would be its no-nesting mode.

discoveries.name: Radial parasols
discoveries.how: An accident in the first CumulusNoise code. Displacement depends only on direction from the parent centre, so the raw 2D height shows a pinwheel of pleats in every cell. Owner switches also made it jump (c0ratio 1.2 in this first version).
discoveries.why: Reads as pleated umbrellas, palm crowns or fan coral seen from above, a striking look for a canopy texture. The fixed CumulusNoise keeps a softer continuous version in its relief, which would be the place to start if it is wanted as a mode.

discoveries.name: Crater cavities
discoveries.how: Rendered CraterField's Eval3 as an isosurface at iso 0.03 instead of as a height slice.
discoveries.why: Round voids with smaller pits on their walls, like eroded limestone. It comes free with the 3D form of CraterField, so it is a use case rather than a new node.

discoveries.name: Graph sponge preset (no new node)
discoveries.how: While looking for the closest graph to BubblePack, the negated Max of 4 scaled sqrt CellularDistance layers gave a connected sponge.
discoveries.why: A strong coral or sponge volume available today from existing nodes, worth listing as a preset. Measured 21.1/57.5/181 ns AVX2 with fnlab, for the tree without the final Multiply.

discoveries.name: Rimmed sparse crater graph recipe (no new node)
discoveries.how: Fourteen existing nodes: CellularDistance Euclidean Squared with Size Jitter 0.8 scaled 0..8, bowl = Max(Min(D-1, 0), -0.6), rim = Max(0.3 - 1.5*Abs(D-1.1), 0), summed and multiplied by a 0/1 gate from Min(Max(CellularValue*1000, 0), 1) at the same scale and jitter.
discoveries.why: Gives sparse, round, flat-floored craters with thin raised rims at one scale for a measured 23.6/65/208 ns AVX2 (SSE41 32/91/288, AVX512 11/29/92). It is the honest baseline for CraterField: craters are bitten where they cross Voronoi edges, there is one size class, and no erasure, which is exactly what the node adds. Worth listing as a preset on its own.

discoveries.name: NestedCaps (hierarchical cells, split boulders)
discoveries.how: Prototyper mutation of PuffyCaps: each level's lattice lives in the owner cap's local frame, children fade at the owner boundary. Re-tested: c0ratio 7.10, max slope 29.4, scalar 348.5 ns 2D (6.8x perlin2), far coords clean.
discoveries.why: Tortoise-shell cells with rounded boulders in relief and split stone blocks in 3D; a graph cannot pass the owner frame down, and the seed 5 window 16 sheet has no lattice. The best of the discoveries; plain PuffyCaps would be its no-nesting mode. Cost is 3x3 power-distance searches per level, so a 4D port is heavy.

discoveries.name: NestedCracks (hierarchical crack plates)
discoveries.how: Same local-frame mutation with crack=1 output. Re-tested: c0ratio 5.25, max slope 164, scalar 390 ns 2D (7.8x perlin2), 3D z-continuity max 0.128.
discoveries.why: Dried-mud plates whose child cracks never cross a parent crack. Downgraded: Min of three F2-F1 layers gives a very similar height view, and the distinctive dark wedge grooves are also the steep-slope artifact. Keep as a mode of NestedCaps if that is built, not on its own.

discoveries.name: Radial parasols
discoveries.how: Prototyper accident in the first CumulusNoise code: displacement depends only on direction from the parent centre, so every cell is a pinwheel of pleats. That version jumps (c0 1.2, max slope 366); the shipped CumulusNoise 2D field keeps a continuous softer version.
discoveries.why: A striking canopy or fan-coral texture from above that nothing in the existing set gives. Only worth keeping as a 2D output mode of CumulusNoise if that ever ships, since the continuous form costs the full cumulus search.

discoveries.name: Crater cavities
discoveries.how: CraterField Eval3 rendered as an isosurface at iso 0.03.
discoveries.why: Round voids with smaller pits on their walls, eroded-limestone look. A use case of the 3D form, not a node.

discoveries.name: Graph sponge preset (no new node)
discoveries.how: Negated Max of four scaled sqrt-of-clipped-CellularDistance layers. Prototyper measured 21.1/57.5/181 ns AVX2, not re-measured by me.
discoveries.why: A connected coral or sponge volume from existing nodes, confirmed from the image. Worth a preset.

discoveries.name: nested-voronoi aniso fibre grains
discoveries.how: NestedVoronoi with aniso=3: each parent cell's child lattice is stretched along a hashed axis before the search, so the children become oriented fibre bundles per parent (the grid row aniso 3; saved by the earlier run of this task).
discoveries.why: Bark / metal-grain / felted patches with hard parent boundaries and no per-pixel shear, which neither CellularDistance nor a DomainAxisScale graph can give because the stretch axis changes per cell; it overlaps CellFrame's look at a fraction of the cost (no source evals), so it may be the cheaper route to per-grain orientation.

discoveries.name: GiniFoam trabecular scaffold
discoveries.how: t_gini_foam vol --set rel=1,jit=0.7,press=0.1,S=0.25 --iso 0.47: keep only the high participation band around cell edges and junctions.
discoveries.why: A webbed bone or coral strut network with fins at the nodes. Stock F3-F1 thresholds give straight faceted rods at both thin and thick settings. The strongest reason to have the foam mode.

discoveries.name: Hard CellFrame over a Voronoi source
discoveries.how: t_cell_frame grid src=2,3 --set blend=1,jit=0.7,width=0.001,aniso=3,sj=0.5,sf=2.5: each parent grain runs a child Voronoi in its own stretched, rotated, reseeded frame.
discoveries.why: Stretched shards and fibre cells per grain, the NestedVoronoi aniso look from a general node. It also supports dropping NestedVoronoi as its own node, since this Source slot can take another cellular node. Nesting CellFrame in itself was not rendered.

discoveries.name: CellularShape needle rods inside the 3^D window
discoveries.how: t_cellular_shape shape=3,out=0 or 1,size=0.09-0.1,len=6,sj=0.3,jit=1. The window bound is on Rmax, so thin capsules can be 14x longer than wide at Rmax 0.91 with 0 jumps in the distance output.
discoveries.why: Matchstick scatter in 2D and a rod pile with free 3D orientation in volume. The report stopped at len 0.3 for its walls output and treated long capsules as needing a sparser lattice. Min of 4 rotated F1 gives only blunt ellipses at fixed angles.

discoveries.name: GradedVoronoi pore volume
discoveries.how: t_graded_voronoi vol --set out=3,levels=9,ratio=1.41,k=1.5,base=0.5,lsf=0.1,flr=1 --iso 0: the F1 floor fix turns the output into pores whose size follows the Level source.
discoveries.why: A sponge or pumice volume with spatially varying pore size and 0 jumps on 3D slices. Before the fix this output gave a mostly solid block with two strips of cavities. No stock node varies cell density per lane.

discoveries.name: FoamBlend v2 (pairwise distance blend)
discoveries.how: Family combination while testing whether BiomeBlend width is constant. N biomes each own a field, and a label's weight comes from d_k = max_j((s_j-s_k)/|grad s_j - grad s_k|). The gradients come from 3N field evals in 2D. A max of continuous functions, with no winner test.
discoveries.why: The tightest width in the family: cv 0.05, p95/p05 1.13 over 8 seeds (BiomeBlend cv 0.20, 1.92). Median 0.78-0.88 cells over wavelengths 4 to 64. No lattice, any biome touches any other, shares 0.247-0.251 at K=4, c0ratio 7.92. Limit: small specks appear where the field difference has a saddle near a tie at short wavelength (about 2 world units here, with fade width .44), and they do not depend on the finite difference step. Scalar 1124 ns, or 1413 ns with sources. An earlier cos4t reading of +0.34 was a measurement artefact, because the mask has zero slope at its contour; a linear mask reads -0.079 to -0.101, close to the isotropic -0.067.

discoveries.name: DistFade (Fade with a world space width)
discoveries.how: Divide the control by its finite difference gradient magnitude and smoothstep the result, so the fade is set in world units. 3 control evals in 2D, 4 in 3D, and by the same formula 5 in 4D (not built).
discoveries.why: Beats BiomeBlend on a continuous control: width cv 0.14, p95/p05 1.42, no border wobble, one third of the control evals (control only 316 ns against 895 ns). Limit: N biomes on one control only touch their value neighbours, and it needs a continuous control. It can be built today as a graph of about ten nodes, so a node's value is mainly ease of use.

discoveries.name: Piecewise linear warp keeps facets flat
discoveries.how: Looking for a way to break the simplex lattice without triangle solves. Warp the position by a coarser facet vector field. A composition of piecewise linear maps is piecewise linear, so facets stay exactly flat.
discoveries.why: Crease normal peak/mean 1.37 against 5.48 at 55 ns scalar, against the jitter fan's 1.78 at 81 ns. The same code works in 2D, 3D and 4D with no search. Folded area is 0.00% up to pw .4 at pf .5 and 0.01% at pw .6. Also usable as a general domain warp for any faceted source.

discoveries.name: Foam Margin tablelands and pebbles
discoveries.how: Viewing a clamped Margin output in relief and as a volume, rather than as a crack map.
discoveries.why: The relief is flat topped plateaus split by gullies, like pack ice or mesas. The volume at iso .5 is a packing of irregular non-convex pebbles with thin gaps and no point sites. Neither is a simple graph, because a second largest value needs a sorting network.

discoveries.name: Foam plates (label plus winner relief)
discoveries.how: Output 6 in the foam proto: Label level plus the winning field's value.
discoveries.why: Stepped mesas with cliffs between labels, and each plate keeps its own surface. It needs the winner value, which no node exposes today.

discoveries.name: Foam Label over facet noise
discoveries.how: Combining two ideas in the family: ExchangeFoam with SimplexFacet as the source.
discoveries.why: Angular non-convex plates at 88 ns scalar for K=5 (1.68x perlin2), much cheaper than the 317 ns Perlin form. Facet vertices are not zero, so it needs no per field offset (0.0% ties at K=8).

discoveries.name: Gumbel weighted foam shares, tested
discoveries.how: Running the entry's untested theory with a logistic approximation of the normal CDF and only the measured source std.
discoveries.why: Targets .533 .267 .133 .067 gave .522-.529 .271-.273 .137-.142 .061-.065 across Perlin, fBm, warped and facet sources, even though their marginals differ. Rare labels become islands, as a biome map wants. It is sensitive to the std value, so it is not calibration free.

discoveries.name: exact-step divisor for far-coordinate finite differences
discoveries.how: While testing the step floor, dividing a central difference by the step the floats actually took, hx = (x+h)-(x-h), instead of 2h removed the rounding error entirely: 0.2% gradient error at 1e5 features and 2% at 1e6 with h 0.05, where the naive divisor is 45% wrong at 1e5. The floor then only needs 2 ulps.
discoveries.why: It is a free fix (one subtraction per axis) that every finite-difference node in the catalogue should use; it moves the usable range of gradient nodes from about 1e4 to about 1e6 features.

discoveries.name: stacked scarp bands (cuesta hills)
discoveries.how: Repeating the contour-scarp profile at a fixed height spacing with the band index from floor((h-L0)/spacing) and cliff+talus height equal to the spacing.
discoveries.why: Stepped hills where every riser has the same plan width regardless of slope, which Terrace cannot do; a natural Band Spacing parameter for the Scarp output.

discoveries.name: Tap-mean residual plus curvature floor from the same taps
discoveries.how: Replace the centre tap residual with the mean of all stencil taps, and the absolute gradient floor with max(g, 0.5 h (|hxx|+|hyy|)). No new source evaluations.
discoveries.why: Spread 3.28 to 2.61 at 5 octaves and 1.89 to 1.63 at 3, missed core 2.6% to 0.2% at 5 octaves, and scale free: at Feature Scale 100 it holds 2.66 at 5 octaves where the old floor collapses. Cost is 5% in the scalar proto. Price: 5 octave c0 falls to 3.27-4.02, while 3 octave c0 rises to 6.09-7.63. It is the look I would ship.

discoveries.name: One secant tap along the gradient (sec=1)
discoveries.how: Walk along the gradient by the first-order distance, clamped and at least the stencil radius, and use the slope actually seen on that walk as the denominator.
discoveries.why: Best width at one extra tap by count (6 instead of 5): spread 1.15 at 3 octaves and 1.56 at 5. Not a default because c0 is about 1.49 at 5 octaves: 77 of 490000 samples step more than 0.3, around near-zero gradients. c0 4.56-4.67 at 3 octaves, so an option for thin lines on smooth sources.

discoveries.name: Fourth-root step law for far coordinates
discoveries.how: h = hw * max(1, C * (|x| 2^-23 / hw)^(1/4)), C about 4, from balancing second-difference rounding (ulp / h^2) against truncation (h^2). It needs only Sample Distance and position, not the source frequency.
discoveries.why: Replaces both the 2 ulp and 16 ulp floors with one law. At C=4 across 3 frequencies and 2 steps, gradient error is at or under 8.6, 13.9 and 23.4% at 1e5, 3e5 and 1e6 features, against 14.8, 73.8 and 101% for 16 ulp. Tested on Perlin only, 2 seeds. Applies to every finite-difference node in the catalogue. Image compares crest lines at 1e5 features; the 16 ulp and root-4 panels look about equal there.

discoveries.name: Crest membrane: closed-form 3D ridge sheets
discoveries.how: Trig closed form for the 3x3 Hessian eigenvalues, eigenvectors from the longest cross product of (H - l I) rows, and the true middle eigenvalue instead of a trace proxy (eig=1).
discoveries.why: Fragments become connected curved membranes with windows, on seeds 42, 90210 and 7. It looks like neither the Abs pretzel nor the flat F2-F1 polyhedra, and z-continuity max improves about 12-16x. 19 taps; 9 taps alone measure 24.88 ns in 3D, so about 52 ns is an estimate. Needs a polynomial acos.

discoveries.name: Crack lines by warping outside the Hessian
discoveries.how: Domain warp the position before the probe, keeping the source at 1 octave (wa=0.12, wf=1.5). In a real graph this is a DomainWarp around the probe.
discoveries.why: Keeps the Hessian on 1 octave instead of the fragmenting 3 octave source, and the lines stop looking like smooth pipes. With absolute thresholds c0 is 7.7 in the image (8.9 in check). With the final scale-free settings c0 is 6.8, 7.8 and 3.6 over 3 seeds.

discoveries.name: Thin warped masked F2-F1 as a crack preset
discoveries.how: Remap F2-F1 near its minimum, multiply by a soft Simplex mask, wrap in DomainWarpGradient. All real nodes, saved as a DSL line.
discoveries.why: A cheap crack network with free ends and Y joints at 8.38 ns AVX2. It is the look-alike crest-lines has to beat, and it does not follow any source's ridges. FFT shows a cross from the warp.

discoveries.name: Value-only mesa and stacked terrace presets
discoveries.how: MaxSmooth of the lowered source against a clamped Remap cliff at 13.34 ns; stacked steps from Modulus + Remap at 19.40 ns; the full cliff + talus chain on a signed distance graph at 53.06 ns. No new node.
discoveries.why: Delivers the mesa country character from existing nodes today, with presets saved as DSL text beside the image. Shapes differ from the prototype and the stacked preset needs a Remap for range.

discoveries.name: Fjord blocks from stock nodes
discoveries.how: Built as the rival to the glacial Voronoi mode: warped F2-F1 CellularDistance, PowFloat, Min and a Multiply carve in two tiers. The first attempt had the edge sign inverted and carved cell centres.
discoveries.why: A real stock graph gives massifs with narrow sheer troughs and true junctions, so it can ship as a preset with no new node.

discoveries.name: Stacked strata density from two Terrace sawtooths
discoveries.how: Built as a fairer 3D rival to StrataTerrace: density + 0.22 * (saw(c,T) + saw(c,1.618T)), where saw = Subtract(q, Terrace(q)) on a tilted Gradient.
discoveries.why: Stock nodes alone give crisp uneven rock ledges, much better than the 1D Value baseline used earlier. This is a useful recipe and it lowers the bar for what a 3D strata node must add.

discoveries.name: Caprock folded cliff bands
discoveries.how: The caprock profile with a large low-frequency fold source and no dip: fold=2,ff=0.25,thick=0.4,dipx=0,dipy=0.
discoveries.why: Curved cliff bands sweep round the terrain, the most striking 2D strata image, at no extra cost beyond the fold eval.

discoveries.name: Overhanging caprock hoodoos
discoveries.how: 3D density form with alternating hard and soft layers: dens=1,altl=1,thick=0.42,ledge=0.4,oct=3,sf=0.6,hamp=2.2,y0=2.4,dipx=0.15,dipy=0.06.
discoveries.why: Mushroom-capped hoodoos with hard layers overhanging soft ones, which the stock sawtooth density did not produce. It leaves small floating fragments that would need cleaning for terrain use.

discoveries.name: Worm track valleys
discoveries.how: A flaw in glacial tiers seen from above before the climb term existed: climb=0,wratio=0.5,tscale=2.2,hang=0.4. Tier 2 and 3 contours become looping tube-like channels.
discoveries.why: Wrong for glaciers, but the top-down image reads as burrow tracks or winding channels of constant width, and might suit a texture or road-carving mask.

discoveries.name: Timber plank flooring
discoveries.how: The earlier plank form of GrowthAge, re-rendered through the new Timber remap: plank=1.6,rings=14.
discoveries.why: A stationary wood floor where every plank is its own cut through its own tree, at one-trunk cost. It removes the non-stationary limit of a single trunk.

discoveries.name: Caprock mesas from Max( Source, Terrace( Source ) )
discoveries.how: Stock graph: S = Subtract( FractalFBm( 5, Perlin 178 ), Gradient( X 0.00026, Y 0.0001 ) ); out = Add( Max( S, Terrace( S, Step Count 1.8, Smoothness 0.05 ) ), the same Gradient ). Where the source is above the staircase it keeps its slope (soft layer), where the staircase wins it is a flat cap (hard layer), and the riser is the cliff.
discoveries.why: Reproduces the whole StrataTerrace default look with four stock nodes, 13.2 / 27.5 / 51.2 ns AVX2 with the FBm evaluated twice. A larger Gradient gives cuestas and hogbacks, a Perlin in the plane gives folded cliff bands.

discoveries.name: Poster agate from a 1D CellularValue lookup
discoveries.how: AddDimension( New Dimension Position = Perlin * 100, Source = DomainAxisScale( X 0, Y 0, CellularValue( Feature Scale 12.5 ) ) ) gives flat gray bands of hashed width along the field's iso-lines; multiplied by Min( 6 * |same lookup of CellularDistance F1-F2|, 1 ) it gets thin dark seams at every band edge.
discoveries.why: A stock way to get hard-edged hashed bands with seams, like a cut and polished slab, for masks and stylised materials. Cartoony next to the StrataBands agate and expensive (49 ns AVX2 2D, two 3D cellular searches per sample), which is itself an argument for a cheap jittered band profile on Terrace.

discoveries.name: burgers_nwave_t3_entropy_root
discoveries.how: Entropy root mode (mode=5) with K=21 taps at t=3 on single-octave Perlin: pushing Time well past the breaking time while picking the Hopf-Lax minimising root instead of an arbitrary bracket root.
discoveries.why: The field becomes clean merged N-waves: long straight-ish diagonal sawtooth ridges with sharp fronts, the classic shock-merging regime of Burgers, which the bisection root turns into a hole-ridden mess. It is a distinct look (parallel asymmetric ridges, like wind-packed snow or shingle beaches) that only appears once the root is entropy-correct, saved from the earlier run and confirmed in root_modes.

discoveries.name: burgers_imbricate_scales
discoveries.how: BurgersSteepen locked root (mode=7,K=13,pol=1,t=1.5) with a Worley F1 source (src=3).
discoveries.why: Each cell becomes a rounded scale with a smooth back and a sharp overlapping lip: pine cone, armour, slate. It uses no scale-specific code and holds at window 16, but the field is fixed direction and uniform, and it is 2D only (3D not tested). Scalar measured 36.9x perlin2; ESTIMATE about 55 ns in SIMD from 14 CellularDistance evals. A striking preset rather than a building block. Overlaps flow-shingle, which has a flow field and costs less.

discoveries.name: burgers_simplex_feathers
discoveries.how: BurgersSteepen locked root (mode=7,K=13,pol=1,t=1.5) with a Simplex source (src=5).
discoveries.why: Sharper shark-tooth or feather fronts than Perlin, without the brick weave Perlin shows in the wide panel. Its spectrum has strong directional spokes along d. Suggests Simplex is the better default source for this node. Seed 90210, window 16.

discoveries.name: burgers_nwave_t3_lock_root
discoveries.how: Locked root at t=3: mode=7,K=21,pol=1. This replaces the prototyper's entropy K21 discovery at a similar scalar cost (24.8x vs 27.7x perlin2).
discoveries.why: Same merged N-wave diagonal ridges as the prototyper's entropy image, with fewer small islands (4/38 vs 49/163 on the same counter) and 0.85% wrong-root pixels vs 1.51%. K13 at t=3 also looks clean, but 6.8% of its pixels differ from the reference.

discoveries.name: burgers_viscous_soft_fronts
discoveries.how: Exact viscous integral over locked taps: mode=8,K=13,nu=0.03,t=1.5.
discoveries.why: A continuous one-sided profile, c0ratio about 8 where every other mode is 1. It has soft dune crests with no aliasing and no tap banding, which the prototyper had concluded was unavoidable. See the cole-hopf-dunes verdict.

discoveries.name: stock_modulus_scarps
discoveries.how: Stock nodes only: Add(Multiply(Modulus(Add(Gradient, Multiply(Perlin, .9)), 1.5), .5), Multiply(Perlin, .6)).
discoveries.why: A cheap one-sided scarp terrain at a measured 4.59/7.75/12.60 ns AVX2, worth including as a graph recipe for anyone who does not need shocks that end or merge. Cliffs are one height and run as long unbroken level sets. It also exposes the 'no graph can do it' claim as overstated.

discoveries.name: fault_stock_graph
discoveries.how: Six stock chains of DomainRotate, DomainOffset, Multiply, Terrace(Step Count=1), DomainAxisScale, Value over a CellularValue strata. Yaw is in radians.
discoveries.why: True cross-cutting offsets from existing nodes in 2D and 3D, at 20.33/46.71/124.57 ns AVX2 including the CellularValue strata and 9.36/14.62/18.34 ns over plain Perlin. Worth shipping as a preset even if the node also ships. It does not tile, because DomainRotate does nothing in 4D.

discoveries.name: fault_drag_tips
discoveries.how: FaultLines with zone=0.25,zres=0.5,tip=3: layers bend towards the fault and then break, and each fault dies out along strike.
discoveries.why: The most geological image in the family: normal-fault style drag on faults of finite length. The idea's Zone erases the fault, and infinite traces read as a shattered window. Holds on seeds 1337, 7, 42 and 424242. Rare tiny chips remain.

discoveries.name: plate_hierarchical_shatter
discoveries.how: PlateDrift whose Lookup source is another PlateDrift: mode=3,sub=1,sfreq=3,drift=0.2,rot=0.3,gap=0.25,subgap=0.25,subbevel=0.2.
discoveries.why: Crazed plates of plates, each large plate carrying its own rotated smaller fragments, like cracked glaze in tiles. Reachable as a graph once the node exists. Relief is too noisy, so it is for masks and textures only. Scalar measured 17.3x perlin2, c0ratio 1.0. The self-nesting is a prototype shortcut, and the port would be two nodes.

discoveries.name: Woven Worley rings
discoveries.how: Fed two offset Worley F1 fields into the Textile twill as its A and B coordinates while testing the level-set-weave idea.
discoveries.why: Concentric ribbons of constant width pass over and under each other. Nothing on the contact sheet looks like it, and true distance inputs solve the thread-width problem without any correction. It is the best argument for giving Textile optional A and B sources.

discoveries.name: Warped fan mosaic
discoveries.how: Upstream warp on TileDomain Fan with TiltedHeight output.
discoveries.why: The straight fan geometry turns into organic stained glass with leaded lines. Edge distance survives the warp well enough for clean joints, and it measured c0ratio 8.0.

discoveries.name: Patchwork quilt
discoveries.how: TileDomain Courses with Quarter rotation, using a hash-picked Textile weave (plain, twill, satin) as Source in each tile.
discoveries.why: Each patch has its own weave, direction and tone, and the node boundaries stay clean. It shows that TileDomain's per-tile frame composes with another node in the family.

discoveries.name: Brushed metal plates
discoveries.how: TileDomain Grid with Quarter rotation, using a one-layer FiberNoise as Source.
discoveries.why: Each plate has its own brushing direction and tone, a common material request that takes only two nodes.

discoveries.name: Mossy wall
discoveries.how: HeightBlend of a TileDomain Courses wall and an fbm moss, using the tile bevel as Height A.
discoveries.why: Moss occupies the mortar first and reaches brick tops last, while Fade on the same two sources only greys the wall (r=3 in the prototype). It is the clearest HeightBlend demonstration found.

discoveries.name: Combed hair lines
discoveries.how: One-layer streak path with tight spacing and a strong upstream warp.
discoveries.why: It gives long dense flowing lines with real swirl singularities at about 1x Perlin plus the warp, far cheaper than the capsule fur. It reads as combed hair or wood grain.

discoveries.name: Hook wisps
discoveries.how: Parameter extreme: capsule path with field frequency 0.5, where the catalogue warned strands hook unnaturally.
discoveries.why: The flaw becomes a look of its own, flame-like curled wisps and tendrils that are useful for smoke or ornament, though it is not hair.

discoveries.name: Nested tile
discoveries.how: TileDomain Hex whose Source is a TileDomain Herringbone in the hex's local frame.
discoveries.why: Herringbone sits inside hexes with a separate seed per hex. This shows that passing tile-local coordinates makes nesting work as designed.

discoveries.name: Draped twill kelp
discoveries.how: Upstream warp on the Textile twill at low thread count.
discoveries.why: Threads flow and bulge like woven kelp. It is a simple graph recipe rather than a new node, but it looks strong. The same warp on knit shreds the loops and looks poor.

discoveries.name: Two noise strands
discoveries.how: Level-set weave with two low frequency noises as A and B.
discoveries.why: Flowing strands like muscle or kelp, with fat and pinched bands where the gradients change. It is a good look but needs Textile's A and B inputs rather than a node of its own.

discoveries.name: Knit chain-link
discoveries.how: Textile knit with thin yarn and a wider, shorter stitch: structure=1, kw=0.17, kh=0.75, ka=1.6, fib=0.03.
discoveries.why: The knit stops reading as yarn and reads as chain-link fence or chain mail, with clean diamond holes. It is the one useful thing the knit path gives that the weave cannot.

discoveries.name: Woven Worley rings (confirmed)
discoveries.how: Textile twill with two offset Worley F1 fields as A and B coordinates (level-set-weave mode=2, src=4, prof=1).
discoveries.why: Confirmed on the as_textile sheet: constant-width concentric ribbons passing over and under, c0ratio 8.05 and range -1..1 re-measured. The strongest argument for giving Textile optional A/B sources.

discoveries.name: Warped fan mosaic (confirmed)
discoveries.how: Upstream warp on TileDomain Fan with TiltedHeight output.
discoveries.why: Confirmed from sheet_warped_fan: reads as leaded stained glass or opus mosaic, c0ratio 8.0 on the sheet, and the FFT loses the lattice cross. A strong preset for the node.

discoveries.name: Mossy wall (confirmed)
discoveries.how: HeightBlend of TileDomain Courses and an fbm, with the tile bevel as Height A; Fade on the same pair beside it.
discoveries.why: Confirmed on materials_combos: moss fills the mortar first and reaches brick tops last, while Fade only greys the wall. The clearest demonstration of a height-aware Fade weight.

discoveries.name: cascade-mesas
discoveries.how: FractalMultifractal mode=0 (p-model product) at inter=2.5 with the knee output (knee=1), 6 octaves, rendered as relief at window 5
discoveries.why: The Max(0,.) floor makes an exactly flat ground and the knee saturation flattens the tops of the surviving clumps, so the relief reads as flat-topped mesas and buttes on a plain, a look neither FBm, ridged nor the other multifractal modes give. It is a parameter extreme of the Multiplicative mode, so it costs nothing extra; a port only needs Knee exposed.

discoveries.name: self-gated-fbm
discoveries.how: Set FractalFBm Gain to a clamped Remap of a Simplex with the same seed and Feature Scale as the Source, so gain follows the fractal's own first octave. Optionally wrap it in MaxSmooth for a flat floor. Real nodes only. The local spectral slope changes with height: amplitude falls off as g(s0)^i, not as a constant slope scaled by height as in Hetero.
discoveries.why: The cleanest plains-with-rough-peaks in this family, with no new code: top/bottom roughness 19.5 against Hetero's 14.1, at 8.56 ns (9.33 with floor) against 7.23 AVX2 2D. The real check gives 0 FAIL, including tiling, with warnings only for range and the known Simplex 3D/4D jumps. Should be a shipped preset.

discoveries.name: vein-side-stagger
discoveries.how: In a tiered zero-set fractal, add side*sign(parent field) to the child field. Each side of the parent then shows a different level set of the same noise, so branches meet the parent at staggered points instead of crossing it. Output stays continuous because at the parent line the parent's value is at least the child's, so Max hides the jump. Measured c0ratio 7.28 with side .2 in the combined defaults.
discoveries.why: Costs one sign operation and turns X crossings into branches that leave one side, which was the prototyper's main stated flaw. It also applies to other gated line fractals. At side .25 and up some branches are lost, so .2 is my pick from the sweep and the look is modest rather than dramatic.

discoveries.name: pmodel-lace
discoveries.how: t_fractal_multifractal mode=0,oct=6,inter=2.5,gain=0.7,knee=1. Gain .7 lets octaves 0 to 2 reach a zero factor by the formula, unlike gain .5. I did not run the per-octave void measure at this gain.
discoveries.why: This is the only setting I tested where voids visibly appear at several scales, giving a lacy clump-and-hole mask with an attractive 3D slice, possibly useful for moss or lichen coverage. Not clean: c0ratio 3.5-4.4, max slope 330-375. It would take about a dozen real nodes (estimate, I only built a partial 3-Remap product that was not a fair match). Worth a look, not a node on this evidence.

discoveries.name: Wave direction lattice
discoveries.how: Tried steering waves by a per-lane angle: use only the K nearest of Nv fixed wave vectors, weighted by a smooth bump in angle.
discoveries.why: Wave vectors never move with position, so there is no shear, and grain length comes from Nv rather than a lattice window. Measured aspect 6.0-6.2 at K6 Nv32 and 9-12 at Nv64, against about 3 for steerable 2x2. K6 Nv32 gives bold single-wavelength bands. K6 Nv64 has real plaid patches, so measured aspect does not mean it looks good, and K8 Nv64 with one band still shows a plaid patch. Vortex input shows polygonal rings with sector seams and a singular centre (c0 1.5, attributed to the centre, not separately tested). 2D only. AVX2 kernel 8.55 ns at K=6, estimate of a node.

discoveries.name: Wave warp domains, animal coat
discoveries.how: A too-strong global slice warp on N=8 parabola waves (sw=2, swS=6), first judged a bad setting because its FFT smears into a square cloud.
discoveries.why: Rings and spots flow into long wavy stripes across the field, and with a tanh sharpen it reads as an animal coat with spot and stripe domains. AVX2 about 3.2 ns measured for the same op count at a different warp setting, so very cheap. 3D is only a ragged sponge.

discoveries.name: Downslope flutes
discoveries.how: Set the steerable direction to the gradient of a Perlin hill and added the hill back in.
discoveries.why: Ribbed flutes run straight down the slopes like a dissected volcano, far more structured than FBm from one simple rule. No branching, and less natural than the erosion-filter keeper. Needs a source gradient in a real node.

discoveries.name: Cyclic slice shear creases
discoveries.how: Over-driving the cyclic decorrelation warp at a short scale (decorA=10, decorS=5).
discoveries.why: Braided long sheared bands crossing at shallow angles, like muscle tissue, tendons or mylonite rock. Seen in 2D only.

discoveries.name: Half plane wave strata
discoveries.how: A bug: all wave vectors lay in one half plane.
