discoveries.why: Magnitude and Speckle turn into long horizontal lenses like cross-bedded strata, while Real and Ridged stay isotropic, a cheap anisotropy in the envelope alone. It is also why the wave table must alternate the sign of d.

discoveries.name: Cyclic raw knit fabric
discoveries.how: The unmodified cyclic recipe viewed at a 24 unit window across seeds.
discoveries.why: A convincing knit rib texture, vertical in 3 seeds and horizontal in 1. A flaw for noise but a usable textile pattern with very cheap maths.

discoveries.name: Wave sign parity mosaic
discoveries.how: Multiplying the sign of each wave: a 2-colouring of the line arrangement.
discoveries.why: A shattered-glass two-colour mosaic with jump discontinuities, same family as the multigrid mosaic, so likely not worth a separate mode.

discoveries.name: Steerable envelope normalisation
discoveries.how: Divide each steerable octave by sqrt( sum w_i^2 |G v_i|^2 / 2 ), its own expected std from the same per-corner terms (envn=1 in the prototype).
discoveries.why: Measured: lattice imprint cellVarMax/Min 21x -> 2.1x at one octave and 5.3x -> 1.6x at four, grain aspect unchanged (3.04-3.15), max slope 15 -> 37, kurtosis 2.9 -> 2.4. At four octaves the combed grain keeps its look with even contrast and fainter FFT rings; at one octave it becomes a constant-contrast stroke field with a bimodal histogram, a distinct look of its own. One FMA per corner plus one rsqrt per octave. Worth an option on the node, not a new default.

discoveries.name: offset-cone dune sea (graph recipe)
discoveries.how: Found while testing whether existing nodes can make barchans. Two CellularDistance F1 cones from the same seed, Feature Scale=110, Size Jitter=0.3: Max(0, 0.1 - Cell(p)) - 1.6 * Max(0, -0.3 - Cell(p offset by 40,16)), clamped at 0, the whole tree under DomainWarpGradient(Warp Amplitude=35, Feature Scale=170).
discoveries.why: In sand-lit relief it reads as a faceted dune sea with sharp crests and shaded lee faces, over 2 seeds. It uses existing nodes only, costs 12.6 ns AVX2 measured, and passes fnlab check (0 FAIL, 1 WARN on tile seam). Honest limits: circular disc-edge creases show, faces are planar, and from above it is an asymmetric Voronoi rim network, not barchans. Colour was applied by my sand renderer. A cheap recipe for a big rough erg, not a replacement for barchan-field.

discoveries.name: Knot fibre bundle
discoveries.how: Combined the Milnor map with Worley on the f plane and the Gauss-Newton tube distance on f - c, with the nearest feature searched in the same metric.
discoveries.why: Hundreds of uniform-radius wires following parallels of the knot read as field lines or combed hair. This is the strongest knot image, and it was not in the idea. Flaw: thin wires measure c0ratio 1.11 to 1.83.

discoveries.name: Hopf whirlpool of scales
discoveries.how: Rendered a 2D slice of Hopf + Worley while checking the idea's claim that 2D is dull, then swept z0.
discoveries.why: Concentric rings at z=0 become a pinwheel at z=1.2, like a whirlpool or ammonite, continuous at c0ratio 7.99. The lift costs 0.4 ns over the source in the AVX2 sketch.

discoveries.name: Hopf fold whirl wallpaper
discoveries.how: Applied the mirror fold to Hopf + Worley and looked at the 2D sheet.
discoveries.why: A baroque, carpet-like tile of whirlpools. It is decorative and obviously periodic, so not noise, but a distinct wallpaper look.

discoveries.name: Knot scatter glyphs
discoveries.how: Lowered the density of per-cell random knots to 0.5 at K=4.
discoveries.why: Separated knots read like floating calligraphy. A curiosity only: 1759 ns scalar was measured for a similar 3x3x3 scatter, and there is no clear use.

discoveries.name: Coral reef layout
discoveries.how: Moved roots onto a plane with a 3x3 window instead of the idea's 3x3x3 lattice.
discoveries.why: It uses a third of the capsules, removes the height limit, and turned floating sticks into coral and forest. This one change decides whether the idea works.

discoveries.name: Template forest
discoveries.how: Reused one prebuilt tree per node, with only a per-cell rotation about y and a scale.
discoveries.why: At the wide view it looked much the same as unique trees, and measured 1.75x to 1.79x faster in the AVX2 sketch. Close-up repetition was not assessed.

discoveries.name: Coral spacetime shards
discoveries.how: Used a 2D tree with z as age and rendered the isosurface.
discoveries.why: Angular wedge-like shards, an odd crystal look. Weak: striped render artifacts are visible and I did not pursue it.

discoveries.name: Perlin lattice stained glass
discoveries.how: This came from a flaw: without offsets, two Perlins share a root at every lattice point. Output RootDist, maxstep 1.
discoveries.why: Dark wells inside bright lacy walls, like stained-glass lead. The wide view is lattice-locked (axis 42.78), so it suits regular tiles and panels rather than natural noise. The same flaw would affect any Newton solve on seeded Perlin pairs.

discoveries.name: Newton root lattice agate cells
discoveries.how: Ran Newton on a local polynomial with hashed roots. The plain window pinned iterates to their own cell and gave square basins; a compact kernel on 1/(z-r) fixed that.
discoveries.why: Cells with nested rings and thin dark seams, like polished agate. Slices along z are wavy columns, so it is really a 2D form that morphs over z. Scalar 1709 ns at N=10 (34x perlin2), so not cheaper than the noise pair.

discoveries.name: Newton mesa plateaus
discoveries.how: Rendered the flat root value as a relief.
discoveries.why: Stepped tabletop plateaus with sheer cliffs and ornate outlines, a fantasy terrain look that needs no terrace step. The cliffs are true jumps.

discoveries.name: Hopf-link and cinquefoil fibre bundles
discoveries.how: Ran the prototyper's bundle mode with P=2,Q=2 and P=5,Q=2 instead of the trefoil.
discoveries.why: Two-lobed and five-lobed combed-hair bundles, as clean as the trefoil one, so the bundle mode generalises over torus knot types. A parameter variant, not a new mechanism; it strengthens the showcase, not the usefulness.

discoveries.name: chiral p6 vortex tiling
discoveries.how: chiral-wallpaper g=16 with Chirality pushed to 0.5 (a parameter extreme the idea warned about as non-invertible)
discoveries.why: The extra folds turn the pinwheel tiling into exactly 6-fold symmetric spiral vortices, still continuous and seamless; a striking preset rather than a failure mode, worth exposing as the upper end of the Chirality range

discoveries.name: bubble frogspawn clusters
discoveries.how: bubble-invert iter=1 cell=0.3 eps=0.2 with a cellular F1 source (src=3) instead of the fbm/stripes the idea described
discoveries.why: Each bubble becomes a tight cluster of many small glossy cells inside the big cells, like frogspawn, roe or compound eyes: a two-scale cellular material at a 1x1-window cost that no existing node or graph produces

discoveries.name: chained wallpaper ornament
discoveries.how: In t_chiral_wallpaper, chain=1 or 2 applies a second fold after a constant rotate and scale (cang, cscale, cox). Best frames: p3 with Worley source, p6, p4 at chain=2.
discoveries.why: Gives flowers, rosettes and feather lace at about one extra fold per level, still the exact group (black-box 17/17 at chain=1). Needs no new node once a wallpaper domain node exists: stack it with DomainRotate and DomainScale. It also replaces domain-kifs.

discoveries.name: post-fold crease softening
discoveries.how: After the exact fold, push the point inward from each fundamental-triangle edge by sqrt(d^2+e^2)-d (SoftFold in t_chiral_wallpaper). In a port this is 3 or 4 sqrt, about 1 ns (estimate).
discoveries.why: Removes the straight seam lines at the mirrors. Because it is a function of the fold's output it cannot change the symmetry: black-box 17/17 at soft=.04. It works on hex folds where softening each abs inside the fold is not obviously safe. Reusable by domain-kaleidoscope and any other fold node.

discoveries.name: bubble 3D sphere clusters
discoveries.how: bubble-invert in 3D with a cellular source (src=3, iter=1, eps=0.2, iso 0.1) instead of the stripes the prototyper rendered.
discoveries.why: Each sphere inversion nests a cluster of small spheres inside large ones, a coral or foam-like volume from one extra map evaluation. The 2D map costs 1.13-1.26 ns; the 3D map was not timed. The source is a 3D CellularDistance at about 12 ns.

carry.name: Simplex-window Voronoi
carry.what: 6/8/10 sites against 9/27/81. Estimated 5/7/10 ns AVX2 for edge masks. It would reprice every cell node in 3D and 4D, so test before KD3 grows further.

carry.name: NestedCaps
carry.what: Owner-frame children: hierarchical cells and split boulders a graph cannot make, because the child needs the owner's identity. c0 7.1 with soft=0.1, max slope 29.4, scalar 297 ns 2D and 586 ns 3D. The strongest node candidate not in the tournament.

carry.name: NestedCracks
carry.what: Same mechanism with crack output: cracks at every scale never cross a parent. c0 5.25, max slope 164, estimated 16/52/170 ns at 4 levels. The lobes critic found Min of three F2-F1 layers largely matches it.

eddies_jupiter_storms (jets rolling up into spirals on 5 of 6 seeds)
steerable-perlin (fluted volcano flanks following a smooth direction field)
crater-field (flat-floored rimmed craters with central peaks, fresh on old)

quasi-tile (bevelled Penrose paving at varied heights)

lyapunov-stretch (overlapping curved plates like eroded strata)

The volume (a tree of square pipes, provably acyclic) as the alternate
overrated: caustic-web look 8: at seed 42 w24 it is a uniform crack net with isotropic FFT, fine, but c0 2.08 and max slope 672 make it a texture, not a heightfield; the cracked-cell stock graph covers most shader uses.

domain-warp-flow look 8: the 8 belongs to the hand-built Jupiter potential (jets + discs, 2526 ns scalar); plain Stir and Watershed are 17.5x Perlin at c0 3.3 and the curl node does the hooks and eyes at 4 steps.
vortex-cells shipped as its own node: on bands it is stamped ovals that nothing moves between; the multi-scale cloud swirl is the one good setting and is a preset-level feature.
quad-stamp 'ship': the dome scatter is dull and the quadtree reads as a grid of squares (axis 78); the case rests only on the 72 ns stock graph being slow.
grounded-scatter useful 7: in most engines boulders are instanced meshes, not noise; it matters only for voxel/SDF worlds, and costs 9-27 Height evals per lane.
knot-field unique 9 and coral-noise unique 9: both proven, both one centred object or a 64-121x Perlin hero bake; uniqueness without a use.
cellular-facet-mesh at 3D: the Kuhn split shows as an axis-aligned grid and it costs ~12x bare simplex-facet for no better volume.
lattice-phasor clean 6 is generous: the hex kernel still shows walls from F2.5 and straight domain seams at F3.7, so only the F1.5-2 labyrinth and the steered mode are clean.
fisk-meanders look 7: the thumb is two parallel belts of goosenecks on a flat grey ground, and 220-230 ns AVX2 measured; omegas and oxbows are real but the picture is thinner than the numbers.
tile-split unique 6: the stock running-bond graph is a near match; the node's case is 2 ns vs 16 ns and AVX512 parity, which the critic conceded.
underrated: height-blend (unique 4, merged into Fade): for a terrain artist this is the most-used blend in the toolbox; the mossy-wall and pebble/sand comparisons are the clearest usability wins in the whole set. Ship it as its own node with Height A/B inputs, not a Fade enum.
surface-probe (look 4): slope and curvature masks drive every terrain material setup; the real 10-node slope graph moires at 1e5 features, so the node is not optional.

graded-voronoi (look 7, filed under voronoi): per-lane cell density is a planet LOD primitive (cells shrink toward coasts or settlements) and the pore volume with 0 jumps is a sponge/pumice tool. The grid image undersells it.
transverse-dunes (mode of vortex-phase): its relief reads as a dune field better than barchan-field at a fraction of the cost; it deserves to be the headline dune preset.

NestedCaps discovery (lobes): the relief reads as forested karst or cauliflower hills, c0 7.1, 6.8x Perlin scalar; a graph cannot pass the owner frame down. It is a better terrain candidate than three of the lobes keepers.
cellular-planes (unique 4): tilted-slab relief with soft fault ramps at ~2x Cellular is a cheap faulted-block terrain base; the 5-node graph rival costs 21 ns and cannot do the soft S range.
exchange-foam useful 7: the label map plus the FoamBlend v2 and DistFade discoveries are the missing biome-partition stack for planets; c0 1 is the point, not a flaw.
shear-flow 'not cheap': a warp that never folds or pinches (det=1) is what artists want when fractal warps make plateaus and crease knots; 6 ns 2D is fine for the quality.

jointed strata (recursive-cut without a root, levels 3): long parallel beds crossed by joints that stop at the beds, window-free at ~2.5 ns estimate, is exactly columnar cliff-face detail; it should be a TileSplit mode, not a footnote.
strata-caverns as a shipped preset: graph-recipe is the right call but it is the only cave with walkable floors and should be in the default preset list, not only on disk.
iso-distance Band output: constant-width beach and shoreline bands on 1-3 octave coasts are something every island generator needs; it was judged against the 5-octave case it was never good for.
panel.comments:
Method: I judged images first (all 23 family sheets, the discoveries sheet split into 7 strips, plus individual relief/wide/second-seed images for erosion-filter, dendry, graded-voronoi, crater-field, caustic-web, steerable-perlin, cyclic-noise, lyapunov-stretch, fisk-meanders, NestedCaps and the Jupiter storms), then read the critic prose. I measured nothing; every number here is quoted from tournament.json and is the critic's measurement or estimate as they labelled it. Where a thumbnail and the prose disagreed I went with the image (cyclic-noise diagonal shear at w32, fisk thumb thinness, graded-voronoi dull grid but clean ramp).

What the images actually show at the top: only two entries produce terrain a landscape artist would use raw: erosion-filter (branching gullies, two seeds checked) and crater-field. Steerable-perlin, domain-warp-curl, plate-drift, fault-lines and simplex-facet are strong secondary terrain tools. Tile-domain and textile are first-rate materials but not terrain. Tube-noise and strata-caverns are the cave answers; the rest of networks is structural. Many of the highest 'look' scores (knot fibre bundle, Jupiter storms, lyapunov plates, cumulus boulders, caustic web) are front-page pictures with little day-to-day use, and I ranked them accordingly.

Honest flaws in my own top 25: cellular-edge-distance, surface-probe and height-blend are chosen for function with plain images; graded-voronoi likewise. Dendry is bake-only at 54x Perlin. Caustic-web and burgers have c0 problems. NestedCaps is a discovery with one critic re-test, not a tournament entry.

Obvious holes in the set:
1. No planet operators at all: no cube-sphere/spherical domain node, no latitude utility, and 4D (tiling) is unbuilt for most keepers (crater-field, dendry, quasi-tile 3D only, fisk, flow-shingle). For planets this matters more than another crack node.
2. No deposition or slope-limiting: nothing fills valleys with sediment or caps slopes (a thermal-erosion stand-in); spill-level failed and the Min-of-ring-taps attempt gave beads. The erosion filter carves but never deposits.
3. No analytic-derivative output on the base noises: surface-probe, erosion-filter, iso-distance, crest-lines and three crossbreeds above all want grad(Perlin/Simplex) and pay 3-5 taps for it; a Gradient output enum on Perlin/Simplex would be the single biggest cost win across the set (erosion critic: 20.3 ns analytic vs 25.6 FD).
4. Rivers remain unsolved at building-block cost: dendry 54x, catchment 76-145x, fisk 220 ns; the cheap things (tube 2D constant-width channel, iso-distance band) give channels but no tree.
5. Cloud/volume noise for atmospheres got one candidate (cumulus, port 3); planets need a cheap 3D cumulus-like primitive and the set does not have one.
6. Several 'clean' numbers were measured with a probe origin that cannot see lattice seams (voronoi critic found this); c0 values for other lattice-window families may be optimistic and should be re-run with the straddling origin before anything ships.

crossbreeds.name: CraterGullies
crossbreeds.why: Crater walls in the relief are smooth; real crater rims are dissected by radial gullies. The erosion filter already proves the steer-by-gradient kernel; the crater profile is closed form so its gradient is free, no finite differences.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Per lane: evaluate CraterField levels as today but accumulate (h, dh/dx, dh/dy) analytically per level (bowl, rim and peak are polynomials of r, so grad = f'(r) * (p - c)/r, masked by the same erase rule). Slope mask m = smoothstep(s0, s1, |grad|). Then run 2 octaves of the erosion filter's 3x3 triangular stripe kernel with direction = grad/|grad| and amplitude a*m, exactly as erosion-filter does on its Perlin base, and return h - stripes. Fixed loop counts (levels, 2 octaves), one hash per lattice point, 3x3 window per octave. Cost estimate: crater (~16 ns 2D est.) + 2 x ~8 ns = ~32 ns 2D; 3D/4D by the same window rule. Tiles via the torus-angle trick the erosion family already built.

crossbreeds.name: PlateShatter
crossbreeds.why: Plate-drift gives rigid rotated plates but their surface is flat; shatter-bsp gives T-junction cracks but on a fixed Voronoi. Cracks that turn with their plate are what breaking river ice and tempered glass look like, and the hierarchical-shatter discovery shows nesting plate-drift works but was too noisy.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Per lane: plate-drift's 3x3 window finds the owning plate id k, its rotation R_k and translation t_k (hashed), and the gap distance g. Transform q = R_k^T (p - c_k - t_k). In plate space run shatter-bsp with seed = hash(k): levels L (fixed int), each level a hashed line through the sub-cell centre, distance d_l clipped at the parent cut as shatter-bsp already does; crack = min_l(d_l / w_l). Output = min(g / gapWidth, crack) for a mask, or plate TiltedHeight minus crackDepth * profile(crack). All lookups are per-lane hashes, no neighbour state; window stays 3x3 (3x3x3 in 3D). Cost estimate: plate-drift (~3x Cellular) + ~0.5 ns per level.

crossbreeds.name: SteeredTube
crossbreeds.why: Tube-noise worms are isotropic; lava tubes, roots and burrows follow a field (down-slope, down gravity, along bedding). Steerable-perlin proves an elliptical per-lane kernel costs little and needs no window.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Per lane: direction unit vector u from a hybrid Direction input (constant, source, or gradient of a source via 3 taps). Build the per-lane metric G = I + (aniso - 1) u u^T. Evaluate the two (Network: three) tube channels n_i as steerable-perlin octaves: at each of the 2^D corners the kernel offset is G (p - corner), with the per-vertex value term from tube-noise so channels do not share zeros. Distance d = sqrt(sum n_i^2) / max(|grad n|, eps) using the analytic corner gradients steerable-perlin already carries, then tube-noise's radius/network logic unchanged. Single lattice visit per channel, no window, 2D/3D/4D by the GenT path. Cost estimate: tube-noise cost x ~1.3 for the metric multiply, plus the Direction eval.

crossbreeds.name: CliffBands
crossbreeds.parents: contour-scarp x strata-terrace x surface-probe (the stacked-scarp-bands discovery, made a node)
crossbreeds.why: Terrace makes risers whose plan width varies with slope; the probes family showed a signed distance s/|grad s| gives risers of constant plan width, and strata showed stacked caprock bands read as cuesta country. Neither family shipped it as a node.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Per lane: source s and its gradient from D+1 taps (central differences with the exact-step divisor h = (x+h)-(x-h)). Band index k = floor((s - L0) / spacing) (a float per lane, no branch). Signed distance to the band's lower iso: d = (s - (L0 + k spacing)) / max(|grad s|, floor) with floor = 0.5 h (|hxx|+|hyy|) from the same taps. Height = L0 + k spacing + spacing * profile(d), profile = clamp(d / cliffWidth) blended into a talus curve over talusWidth, both in world units. Optional hybrid Hardness source modulates spacing per lane. Pointwise, 3 taps in 2D, 4 in 3D, 5 in 4D. Cost estimate: 3-5 source evals plus ~2 ns.

crossbreeds.name: ScreeShingle
crossbreeds.parents: flow-shingle x surface-probe (gradient) x grounded-scatter (chisel stamp)
crossbreeds.why: Flow-shingle stacks oriented overlapping stamps along a field; scree and talus are exactly that: angular stones imbricated down a slope. The field is the terrain gradient and the stamp is the chisel-rubble silhouette, both already prototyped.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Per lane: terrain height H(p) and gradient from 3 taps (2D) give downhill direction u and slope m. Run flow-shingle's 3x3 (3x3x3) candidate search with per-candidate frame aligned to u sampled at the candidate's cell centre (one extra H tap per candidate, 9 in 2D, or reuse the lane's u for a cheaper approximation), stamp = chisel-rubble polygon from fixed icosahedral cut axes in the candidate's hashed rotation, priority = position along u so downhill stones overlap uphill ones. Density hybrid = smoothstep of slope m so flats stay bare. Output H + stoneHeight * mask. Hard edges like flow-shingle (c0 ~1), so a material/mask, not a smooth heightfield. Cost estimate: 3 + 9 H taps + ~8 ns.

crossbreeds.name: SlabField
crossbreeds.why: Cellular-planes gives tilted plates with soft fault ramps; cell-frame gives per-cell rotated grain. Tilted sedimentary slabs whose bedding grain turns with each slab is tumbled-slate and flagstone terrain, and the two share one window pass.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Per lane: one 3x3 (3^D) pass keeping the nearest F1..F4 sites (F1..F5 in 3D) with their hashes. Per site i: lift l_i, tilt vector t_i, grain angle a_i, scale g_i from hash bits; local value v_i = l_i + dot(t_i, p - s_i) + detailAmp * Source(R(a_i) (p - s_i) * g_i, seed ^ hash_i). Blend with cell-frame's barycentric weights w_i over the stored sites (sharpness S from cellular-planes; S small = hard faulted slabs, large = soft hills). Output sum w_i v_i. Source is evaluated a fixed 4 (5 in 3D) times per lane. Cost estimate: ~1.3x CellularDistance plus 4-5 source evals.

crossbreeds.name: RippleOverlay
crossbreeds.parents: lattice-phasor (hex kernel) x surface-probe gradient x transverse-dunes profile
crossbreeds.why: Sand ripples and wind-blown snow run perpendicular to the local slope-and-wind direction; the phasor family showed steered stripes are clean on the hex kernel at 4.3 ns, and the dune profile gives the stoss/slip asymmetry. Nothing lets a graph steer stripes by its own terrain today.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Per lane: base B(p) from Source; gradient from D+1 taps (exact-step divisor); direction u = normalize(mix(windDir, grad B, slopeWeight)) with a fallback to windDir when |grad| < eps (Select, no branch). Evaluate the SuperSimplex-vertex phasor (4 kernels in 2D, 8 in 3D) with direction u and spread s to get phase phi via re*InvSqrt(re^2+im^2+eps^2); profile = dune(phi, stoss, round) from transverse-dunes. Output B + rippleAmp * mask(slope) * profile. Fixed window, hash per vertex, 2D/3D; 4D via the torus-angle trick. Cost estimate: D+1 Source taps + ~4.3 ns (measured hex kernel) + profile.

crossbreeds.name: MoonBase
crossbreeds.why: Crater relief has no ejecta; real craters are ringed by boulder fields that thin with distance from the rim. Grounded-scatter already attaches stones to a Height source; the only new part is a density that depends on the rim mask, which stamp-scatter's cascade fade keeps pop-free.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Per lane in 3D: Height = CraterField(p.xz) (the Height source). For each of the 9 (27 with tilt) stone candidates, evaluate the crater rim mask once at the candidate's cell centre c (rimMask = clamp(1 - |r - R_rim| / ejectaWidth) summed over levels, available from the same crater evaluation at c); stone exists where hash < density0 * rimMask(c) using stamp-scatter's cascade fade so appearance is continuous as the mask varies in space. Stone SDF, sink and smooth-min union exactly as grounded-scatter; output density = min(terrain SDF, stones). Fixed candidate count, no extra window. Cost estimate: grounded-scatter cost + 9 crater evals at ~16 ns each (so ~150-200 ns 3D, a bake node like its parents).

presets.name: Alpine Lakes
presets.recipe: terrain = ErosionFilter(Source=FractalFBm(Octaves=3, Source=Perlin(Feature Scale=400)), Stripe Octaves=2, Altitude Fade on, Slope Mask 0.15..0.5); rockMask = SurfaceProbe(Output=Slope, Source=terrain); shading = HeightBlend(Height A=terrain-derived rock FBm, Height B=grass FBm, weight=rockMask)
presets.what: The erosion-filter relief: smooth hills carved by branching gullies that feed valleys, with flats staying smooth and a slope mask for rock/grass. Critic harness ~20-25 ns AVX2 2D for the terrain part.

presets.name: Cratered Moon
presets.recipe: Add(CraterField(Slope=2.3, Levels=12, Base 0.05, Erase on), Multiply(FractalFBm(Octaves=4, Source=Simplex(Feature Scale=60)), 0.08)); for 3D voxel worlds use the same CraterField Eval3 at iso 0.03 for eroded-limestone cavities
presets.what: A moon or airless planet heightmap with a power law of flat-floored rimmed craters, young on old, plus fine regolith roughness. ~14x Perlin scalar for the crater part; wide view is even by eye.

presets.name: Gas Giant Bands
presets.recipe: DomainWarpFlow(Steps=12, Amplitude 1.2, Potential = Add(DomainAxisScale(Scaling Y=0.5, Perlin), Add(zonal jets: SineWave on y bent by Perlin, sparse discs: Remap(CellularDistance F1 with Size Jitter))), Source=DomainAxisScale(Scaling Y=0.1, FractalFBm Perlin)); stock fallback at 21.6 ns AVX2 2D: chain DomainWarpSimplex(Feature Scale=130, Warp Amplitude=14) 10-12 times with the same seed
presets.what: Jupiter-style bands whose edges roll up into large spirals (5 of 6 seeds in the discovery sheet). Expensive (scalar 2526 ns for the full potential) so bake it; the same-seed warp chain gives plates with spiral eyes today.

presets.name: Spaghetti Caves
presets.recipe: TubeNoise(Mode=Network, Channels=3 Perlin with value term, Radius=0.1, Feature Scale=80) carved from terrain by Min; stock fallback at 9.3 ns AVX2 3D: Add(Multiply(a,a), Multiply(b,b)) with a, b = Perlin at different Seed Offset, cave where value <= 0.017
presets.what: Round-section connected worm tunnels (90-95% connected in network mode) instead of the flanged ribbon webs the stock noodle gives. Add 3 octaves of noise to the Distance output for lumpy walls of uniform relief.

presets.name: Cave Galleries
presets.recipe: The strata-caverns graph recipe on disk: y-sliced slab voids with a Perlin plan source, dome ceilings from Max with a plan FBm, shaft mask from 4 extra plan evals, y-only bedding warp (ya=1.6, yf=0.3) and a 2.2 degree dip
presets.what: Stacked horizontal caverns with dead-flat walkable floors, domed roofs and vertical shafts linking levels, 100% connected in the core at the critic's recommended params. The only cave base with floors you can walk on.

presets.name: Mesa Country (stock)
presets.recipe: S = Subtract(FractalFBm(Octaves=5, Source=Perlin(Feature Scale=178)), Gradient(Multiplier X=0.00026, Y=0.0001)); out = Add(Max(S, Terrace(S, Step Count=1.8, Smoothness=0.05)), the same Gradient). Larger Gradient = cuestas and hogbacks; a Perlin in the Gradient slot = folded cliff bands
presets.what: Flat-capped mesas, buttes, sheer cliffs and talus slopes from four stock nodes, measured 13.2 / 27.5 / 51.2 ns AVX2 2D/3D/4D by the strata critic. Reproduces the whole StrataTerrace default.

presets.name: Plains With Rough Peaks (stock)
presets.recipe: MaxSmooth(LHS=FractalFBm(Octaves=6, Gain=Remap(From Min=-0.3, From Max=1, To Min=0, To Max=0.75, Clamp Output=True, Source=Simplex(same seed and Feature Scale as the fractal Source)), Source=Simplex), RHS=-0.3, Smoothness=0.5)
presets.what: Self-gated FBm: smooth lowland floor with roughness concentrated on the peaks, top/bottom-quintile roughness 19.5 against 14.1 for the Hetero multifractal, at 9.33 ns AVX2 2D with the floor and 0 FAIL in fnlab check including tiling.

presets.name: Ice Floes
presets.recipe: PlateDrift(Rotation=0.3, Drift=0.2, Gap=0.25, Output=TiltedHeight, Lookup=FractalFBm(Octaves=3, Simplex)) then Min with ShatterBSP(Levels=2) cracks for broken-up plates; water = Remap of the Bevel mask
presets.what: A field of rigid, rotated, tilted ice plates with wedge gaps that open and close and a few shattered plates, texture riding each plate. Reads as river ice breaking up or cracked dry mud at the tectonic sheet's scale.

presets.name: Dried Mud
presets.recipe: CellularEdge(Output=Crack, Edge Width=Multiply(0.05, Remap(Simplex(Feature Scale=300), -1..1 -> 0.3..1)), Edge Depth hybrid from the same Simplex, Tapered Tips on, Grid Jitter 0.9); stock fallback at 35 ns AVX2 2D: the nested three-level Min(Mask(L0), DomainOffset(Mask(L1), Offset X=CellularValue(L0 cells, Output +-4000))) T-junction graph
presets.what: Dangling cracks whose width and depth fade with a low-frequency field so plates merge into a near-closed network, the best dried-mud relief in the cracks family, C0 by construction (7.7-7.9 measured).

presets.name: Cobbled Street
presets.recipe: HeightBlend(Height A=TileDomain(Pattern=Fan, Output=TiltedHeight, Bevel=0.1, Mortar=0.05, Random phase on rings), Height B=FractalFBm(Octaves=4, Simplex(Feature Scale=30)) moss, bias 0.3); upstream DomainWarpGradient(amplitude small) turns the fans into leaded stained glass
presets.what: Fan-pattern cobbles with sunken and tilted stones where moss fills the joints first and reaches stone tops last, which Fade only greys. TileDomain fan measured ~61 ns 2D resolved in the materials sheet, so a material not a terrain base.

presets.name: Agate Slab (stock)
presets.recipe: PingPong(Ping Pong Strength=9.5, Source=PowFloat(Pow=0.5, Value=Add(PowInt(Pow=2, Value=A), PowInt(Pow=2, Value=B)))) with A, B Perlin, B at a DomainOffset and Seed Offset 1
presets.what: Nested folded bands like agate or marble from stock nodes at a measured 4.57 / 7.53 / 12.37 ns AVX2 2D/3D/4D; bands thicker and more polygonal than the vortex-phase node.

presets.name: Biome Map
presets.recipe: labels = ExchangeFoam(K=5, Source=Perlin(Feature Scale=900) per field with the per-field offset on, Weighted shares via the Gumbel table); blend width = FoamBlend v2 pairwise distance (s_j - s_k)/|grad s_j - grad s_k| from 3 taps per field; detail density per biome = GradedVoronoi(Level=labels)
presets.what: A planet biome partition with islands, enclaves and any-to-any borders (no 4-label pinwheels), a constant world-space blend width (cv 0.05 measured for FoamBlend v2) and cell density that follows the biome. The pieces exist; only the K-field label compare needs a node.

overrated: knot-field: Look 8, Unique 9 and a keeper badge, but it is one centred object and a constant everywhere else. A demo render, not a node I can use.
newton-basins: keeper badge, but the hero is a favourable seed. Other seeds are a speckled mosaic and the relief is broken pillars.

bond-tunnels: called ship, yet its sheet images are the dullest in the family, a pockmarked block in the vol. The case is a connectivity guarantee for gameplay. It adds nothing visual over tube-noise or the stock noodle.
multigrid-noise: called ship, with a busy gray shard mosaic and spiky relief that needs a warp to hide its long lines. quasi-tile is the aperiodic node worth having.
wave-noise-sliced: keeper badge, but the default is Perlin-like blobs at a reported 9-11x Perlin once clean. The good images (wired needles, direction lattice) are side results.
lattice-phasor: Unique 8 against vortex-phase's 5. At normal viewing its random-direction labyrinth is close to phason-waves N=7 and stamped stripes, while vortex-phase's forks are the rarer look.
crest-lines: Look 6 is generous. The thumb is scattered broken dashes and the relief is walls. Only the 3D membrane is attractive.
tpms-noise: keeper and ship, but 2D is plain blobs and the plain gyroid is an 11-node stock recipe (reported 3.86 / 3.69 / 4.87 ns). Only the warp and the speed are new.
underrated: growth-age: called showcase, Useful 4, because wood is off the terrain path. Wood is one of the most requested procedural materials, and this is the only entry with knots and cathedral arches. Fix the ring aliasing and ship it.

domain-warp-flow: Useful 5. If Angle=0 with Path Average behaves as I expect, it is Substance's Slope Blur, the node I use most. No such render exists: the one Path Average image I found shows a stirred fibrous look. Test this before sizing the node down.
ripple-noise: Useful 4, called too niche. Rain on puddles is a standard game and VFX need. It has only been judged from one frame, so test it in motion.
streak-scatter: Look 5, merged away. It reads as a scratch map, and there is no other scratch source in the set.
occlusion-stack: Useful 5. The leaf litter panel is a real forest floor.
quasi-fold: Useful 4. Crumpled foil with straight creases is a common material map and nothing else makes it. Judged as a terrain its relief looks bad, but that is the wrong test.
flow-network: dropped for not being rivers. Its one-way branching fissures may suit bark, rain channels and wall runoff. That is my reading of the image and it is untested.

nested-voronoi: called graph-recipe, but terrazzo is a staple and the reported graph is 39 / 124 / 424 ns against about 12 / 36 / 123 for a three-level node (my estimate from the critic's per-level figure).
vortex-phase: Unique 5 because 21 stock nodes can reach it. Nobody builds 21 nodes for stripes, and the 3D sheets are some of the best volumes shown.
fold-caustic: Look 6, Unique 6. The back-mapped thumb looks more like real sun on a sandy bottom than the keeper does, though it is the expensive setting and its timing was not re-run.
bubble-invert: Useful 4. Frogspawn and sphere clusters from any source, at a measured 1.13-3.6 ns over the source. A cheap domain operator should score higher than that.
stretch-ftle: Useful 4. The veined plates in 2D and basin foam in 3D suit shell, wing and biological material work, if its steep spots can be tamed.
panel.comments:
WHAT I DID. Read the handbook, the existing nodes sheet and all 24 sheets. I also opened about 15 individual images and family panels. I ran no prototype or fnlab exe, only small Python scripts to read the JSON and crop that sheet. Crossbreeds are on paper: none was built, every crossbreed look is my prediction, and every crossbreed cost is an estimate. Cost figures I call reported or measured come from tournament.json, and I did not re-measure them.

WHAT I COULD NOT JUDGE FROM IMAGES. phase-vortex and steered-band-noise have no image that I saw, so those two scores come from critic notes. For cellular-fracture I only saw the kite mosaic, not the rays. Several merged ideas have no thumb of their own, so I judged them from family panels: defect-stripes, dislocation-stripes, occlusion-stack, streak-scatter, flow-strokes, hilbert-curve-noise, boulder-field-3d. Every image I judged is a still, and each is one rendered setting.

DATA WARNINGS. Some tournament fields disagree with the critic re-tests in the same entry, and I trusted the re-tests. Examples: growth-age field c0ratio 8 against re-measured 1.71 with max slope 651; crater-field scalar 10.16x against 14.4x; ripple-noise 3.34x against 5.8-6.1x; tube-noise c0 7.85 against 7.05. The fold-caustic sheet thumb is the back-mapped form, not the as-written default the critic drops, so my 7 applies only to the back-mapped form.

OBVIOUS HOLES, plainly.
1. Nothing was judged in motion. VFX is half of my interest, and nobody knows whether these nodes boil, pop or crawl over time. Z-slice strips for caustics and the Hopf whirl are the only hints I saw. This is the biggest gap and it applies to my top picks too: caustic-web, ripple-noise, domain-warp-curl.
2. Tiling. Seamless output is the first requirement for a material artist, and it is treated as an afterthought. The stripes critic reports that the 4D torus loses constant width, cellular-facet-mesh has no 4D, and growth-age has no obvious form. A per-lattice Period option that wraps cell indices would suit materials better than the torus, and only some entries mention one. I would add a tiling pass to every shipped material node.
3. Weathering is nearly absent. There are no drips, grunge, rust blooms, edge chips or occlusion. Streak-scatter is an accidental scratch map and SurfaceProbe covers slope only. HorizonProbe and LeakStreaks above are my attempt at this, but this should have been a family.
4. Water and atmosphere. There are caustics but no water surface, cumulus lobes but no wispy cloud density, and nothing for fire. ChoppyOcean addresses only the first.
5. Organic surfaces. No bark, skin pores, leather grain or animal rosettes. Vortex-phase and cell-frame are near but not there.
6. One float per node. Nearly every proposal grows an Output enum, so getting height, ID and mask costs three evaluations, and a per-element ID cannot travel down a graph to drive later nodes. That is an architecture limit, but it shapes how usable all of this is in a material graph.

TIE-BREAKS AND BIG PICTURE. quasi-tile and grounded-scatter score 8 but miss the top 25 because they are narrower than the 8s that made it. flow-strokes (8.5) is absent only because I count it as a mode of flow-shingle, and level-set-weave likewise goes with textile. NestedCracks is listed by name because its relief is the best crack image, though the T-junction stock graph is a real rival at a reported 35 ns. The strongest pattern in the images: domain operators and modifiers that work on any source (TileDomain, ErosionFilter, StampScatter, ChiralWallpaper, flow and shear warps) give more per node than new closed generators. If only a few ship, ship those.

crossbreeds.name: ChoppyOcean
crossbreeds.parents: caustic-web (back map), burgers-steepen (root of the same Lagrangian map), wave-noise-sliced (plane-wave table)
crossbreeds.why: The set has the light under water but no water. One map gives height, whitecap mask and caustic from the same waves, so they line up, and Time is a hybrid input. Not built, look unverified.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Table built when params are set: M plane waves with k_i from a wind angle and cos^2 spread, geometric wavelengths, a_i from a spectrum, w_i = sqrt(g*|k_i|). Optional Period snaps k_i to integer multiples of 2pi/Period for exact tiling without the 4D torus. Seed hashes once to a domain offset. Gen: x0 = p. Constant loop K times: theta_i = dot(k_i, x0) + w_i*T; G = sum(-a_i*k_i*sin theta_i); x0 = p - c*Chop*G, with c the CausticWeb damping 1/(1+0.6*Chop*Hmax). One final pass at x0: h = sum(a_i*cos theta_i), Hessian H = sum(-a_i*cos theta_i*k_i*k_i^T), J = I + Chop*H, detJ. Output enum: Height = h/sum(a_i); Foam = smoothstep(f0, f1, -detJ); Caustic = (eps + |detJ|)^-gamma. No lattice, no window, one code path per lane. 2D is the base form; 3D adds z to T, so a slice is an animation frame; 4D adds w as a second phase term. Risks: the fixed point can change branch at high Chop and lose continuity; direction chains appeared at N=8 in wave-noise-sliced, so M needs about 16. Cost ESTIMATE from the reported N=16 plane-wave figure of 12.5-15 ns per pass: 25-30 ns at K=1, 50-60 ns at K=3.

crossbreeds.name: GrowingCracks
crossbreeds.why: A crack mask driven by a wear map, or animated by a moving front: parents open first, children follow, tips taper. Materials want cracks where the damage is, and VFX wants them spreading. Not built, look unverified.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Damage is a hybrid sampled once at the lane. Edge pass: exact e_0 and F1 site id from the CellularEdgeDistance window, with Grid Jitter <= 0.40 for exactness. Constant loop l=1..L: from hash(id) take cut normal n and offset; e_l = |dot(p-c,n)-off|; side = mask(dot(p-c,n) > off); id = mix(id, side). Thresholds T_0 < T_1 < ... give m_l = smoothstep(T_l, T_l+s, Damage). Widths W_l = W*decay^l. crack = Max over l of m_l*profile(e_l / (W_l*(wmin + (1-wmin)*m_l))), with profile(0) = 1. Continuity: m_l depends only on the continuous Damage at the lane, so there is no per-wall state, which is what the tapered-tip form measured as C0. Because T rises with l, a parent's term at its own wall equals m_parent, which is >= every child term, so a child discontinuity at a parent wall is covered from both sides. Free ends come from noise inside Damage. Output maps crack to [-1,1]. 2D, 3D and 4D follow the window. Cost ESTIMATE from the critic's ShatterBSP estimate: about 7 / 18 ns in 2D / 3D, edge pass alone about 50 ns in 4D, plus one Damage eval. Limit: walls never move, so growth is a reveal along a fixed net.

crossbreeds.name: ShatterLookup
crossbreeds.why: Turns any node into a broken version: cracked mirror, smashed tile, fractured marble slab. PlateDrift gives Voronoi plates, but no node gives straight BSP shards with a rigid offset per leaf. Not built, look unverified.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Same edge pass and constant BSP loop as ShatterBSP, tracking d = Min over levels of e_l/W_l, leaf id and leaf centre c. theta = MaxRot*rnd11(mix(id,1)); shift = Drift*(rnd11(mix(id,2)), rnd11(mix(id,3))). p' = c + R(theta)*(p-c) + shift. In 3D, rotate in one plane picked by id bits using Select. v = Source(p'), exactly one eval per lane. out = lerp(GapValue, v, smoothstep(0,1,d)). Source jumps between shards, but every leaf boundary has d = 0, so out equals GapValue there and the result is continuous. Optional Throw adds a hash height per leaf for stepped relief, multiplied by the same smoothstep so it stays continuous. Works in any dimension the window affords. Cost ESTIMATE: ShatterBSP about 7 / 18 ns in 2D / 3D plus Source. Risk: with a mid-gray gap, shards read as grouted tile rather than glass.

crossbreeds.name: SortedSediment
crossbreeds.parents: pebble-pile, graded-voronoi, stamp-scatter (density sampled at the centre)
crossbreeds.why: Riverbeds and scree are sorted by size, and every ground material needs that. PebblePile has size layers but no spatial sorting; GradedVoronoi has seam-free size control but makes cells rather than stones. Not built, look unverified.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Level is a hybrid source in [0,1], with 0 for boulders and 1 for sand. Constant loop over layers i=0..L-1: s_i = s0*g^i in a per-layer rotated and offset frame q. ix = floor(q/s_i); h = hash(ix, seed+i); centre c = (ix + 0.5 + jit*bits(h))*s_i; radius r = s_i*lerp(rmin, rmax, bits(h)), with jit and rmax bounded so a stone fits its own cell and no neighbour window is needed. Evaluate Level once per layer at the stone centre rotated back to world, so the map never slices a stone. keep = bump(|i/L - Level(c)|, width); r = r*keep, so stones shrink out instead of popping, and hash bits < keep decide presence. dome = sqrt(Max(0, r^2 - |p-c|^2)) or a parabola. Height = Max over layers. Output enum Height, StoneValue (Select of the winner's hash), LayerIndex. Same rim slope issue as PebblePile with sqrt; the parabola profile is smoother. Any dimension. Cost ESTIMATE from PebblePile's 1.5-2 ns per layer plus 1.1 ns for a Perlin Level: about 20-25 ns at 8 layers in 2D.

crossbreeds.name: StrainLines
crossbreeds.why: Warped line work goes fat and thin with stretch, and that is how warped cells give themselves away. Carrying the Jacobian through the warp keeps line width constant in world units: craquelure, stretched hide, even marble veins. A graph cannot do this because nodes cannot pass a Jacobian. Not built, look unverified.
crossbreeds.algorithm: M = identity. Constant loop i=1..S of shears: s = dot(n_i,p) + phi_i; p += A_i*f(s)*t_i with t_i perpendicular to n_i; M = (I + A_i*f'(s)*t_i*n_i^T)*M. This is the ShearFlow kernel, and Lyapunov already carries a tangent. Then the exact edge pass at warped p. For each neighbour k in the fixed window: n_k = unit(s_k - s_1); e_k = dot(m_k - p, n_k); D_k = e_k / Max(|M^T*n_k|, floor). D = Min over k of D_k. Output line = profile(D/W), or bevel from D. Each term is zero on its own bisector and continuous, so Min stays C0 where the unwarped edge distance is. 3D uses a 3x3 M and 3D shears; 4D only if the window budget allows. Cost ESTIMATE: shear kernel about 2-3 ns, edge pass 5.5 / 16 ns, about 6 FMAs per neighbour, so about 10 / 25 ns in 2D / 3D. Risk: first order breaks down at very high strain, so the floor needs tuning.

crossbreeds.name: HorizonProbe
crossbreeds.why: Cavity and occlusion drive dirt, moss and wear on every material. Slope and hillshade exist, occlusion does not. Spill-level's fan failed at finding lakes but is the right shape for this. Not built, look unverified.
crossbreeds.algorithm: h0 = Source(p). Fixed table of D directions, with R rings at radii rad_r and a golden-angle rotation per ring. Constant loops d=1..D, r=1..R: s_dr = Max(0, (Source(p + rad_r*dir_dr) - h0)*HeightScale/rad_r); per direction keep H_d = Max over r of s_dr. Horizon term = H_d/sqrt(1 + H_d^2), the sine of the horizon angle with no atan. Output enum Occlusion = 1 - mean over d; Cavity = occlusion minus its value at a wider radius. 3D density form: fraction of 14 fixed-direction taps inside solid, with a smooth step on each. Max, sums and products keep it continuous if Source is. Use SurfaceProbe's step floor for far coordinates. Cost: 1 + D*R Source evals, so 17 at 8x2. On a 5-octave FBm at about 5.5 ns per eval (ESTIMATE from 5 x 1.1 ns Perlin), about 95 ns, so a bake node. Risk: star artifacts around thin peaks with few directions.

crossbreeds.name: LeakStreaks
crossbreeds.why: Rain runs and rust trails below ledges are on every wall I texture, and the set has no gravity-driven weathering. Not built, look unverified.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Inputs: Height source, Up direction, Length, Taps N (int), Gain, Gamma, Breakup, Column Scale. h_0 = Height(p). Constant loop i=1..N: h_i = Height(p + Up*i*Length/N); ledge_i = saturate(Gain*(h_i - h_(i-1))), which is high where climbing the wall meets a protrusion above this point; streak = Max(streak, ledge_i*(1 - i/(N+1))^Gamma). u = dot(p, Side); c = two octaves of 1D value noise in u; a second 1D noise scales the fade so streak length varies by column. out = streak*lerp(1, c, Breakup), mapped to [-1,1]. Continuous if Height is. 3D uses 2D value noise over the plane normal to Up. 4D puts w into the column noise. Cost: N+1 Height evals plus about 2 ns (ESTIMATE); N=12 on a 5 ns tile edge output is about 65 ns. Limits: ledges thinner than Length/N are missed, so feed a soft proxy height. Up has no meaning through GenTileable2D's torus, so tiling needs a Period option.

crossbreeds.name: FlutedCave
crossbreeds.why: The erosion filter transforms terrain but nobody ran it on a volume in my images. Flutes running down cave walls and flowstone would make noise caves look geological. Not built, look unverified.
crossbreeds.algorithm: s0 = Density(p), plus D forward differences for g (4 evals in 3D). n = g*InvSqrt(dot(g,g) + eps). With gravity axis a: t = a - dot(a,n)*n; tl = |t|; b = cross(t,n)/Max(tl,eps), the across-slope axis. Constant octave loop (2): 3x3x3 cell window; for each cell, hash gives jittered point c_j; w_j = Max(0, 1 - |p-c_j|^2/R^2)^3, with R inside the window reach; psi_j = f*dot(p-c_j, b); Z += w_j*(cos psi_j, sin psi_j). stripe = Re(Z)/sqrt(|Z|^2 + eps). out = s0 + A*saturate(tl/0.3)*saturate(|g|*k)*stripe. The tl mask removes flutes on floors and ceilings, where direction is undefined. 2D reduces to the ordinary ErosionFilter path. 4D's 81 cells are not affordable, so 4D drops w and does not tile. Cost ESTIMATE from the reported stripe kernel of about 8.1 ns per octave on 9 cells: about 24 ns per octave on 27 cells, so about 50 ns plus 4 Density evals. Risk: gradient noise on rough density shreds b, so it needs a smooth input.

crossbreeds.name: HeightFoam
crossbreeds.why: Up to four ground materials competing in foam-shaped regions, with borders that follow the stones and cracks instead of fading across them. ExchangeFoam has the regions and HeightBlend has the border, but the graph needs many nested nodes. Not built, look unverified.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Four fixed GeneratorSource members H_0..H_3 and one Field source. Constant loop k=0..3: F_k = Field(p, seed + k*Stride); v_k = H_k(p); score_k = F_k + HeightLock*v_k + Weight_k. best = Max of score. w_k = Exp((score_k - best)/tau), normalised by their sum, with tau > 0; the subtraction stops overflow. Output enum Value = sum(w_k*v_k), Label (argmax, jumps by design), Margin (best minus second best). Continuous for tau > 0. All 8 evals always run, as the execution model requires. Same code for 2D, 3D and 4D if the sources tile. Cost ESTIMATE: 4 Perlin fields about 4.4 ns, 4 FS::Exp about 1 ns, plus the four materials. Honest rival: nested HeightBlends with a foam Margin as Control. Ship this only if that graph's borders look wrong.

presets.name: Caprock Mesas (stock today)
presets.recipe: S = Subtract(FractalFBm(Octaves=5, Source=Perlin(Feature Scale=178)), Gradient(X=0.00026, Y=0.0001)); Add(Max(S, Terrace(S, Step Count=1.8, Smoothness=0.05)), same Gradient)
presets.what: Flat caps, cliffs and soft slopes from four stock node types. The family report gives 13.2 / 27.5 / 51.2 ns AVX2.

presets.name: Agate Slab (stock today)
presets.recipe: PingPong(Ping Pong Strength=9.5, Source=PowFloat(Pow=0.5, Value=Add(PowInt(Pow=2, Value=A), PowInt(Pow=2, Value=B)))) with A, B = Perlin, B offset with Seed Offset 1
presets.what: Nested polished bands for marble and agate. Report gives 4.57 / 7.53 / 12.37 ns AVX2. Bands are thicker with some polygon corners compared with vortex-phase.

presets.name: Cracked Mud (stock today)
presets.recipe: Min(Mask(L0), DomainOffset(Source=Mask(L1), Offset X=CellularValue(same cells as L0, Output +-4000))), nested three levels.
presets.what: Hierarchical T-junction cracks reading as dried mud in relief and angular blocks in 3D. Report gives 35 / 106 / 345 ns AVX2.

presets.name: Dune Sea (stock today)
presets.recipe: DomainWarpGradient(Warp Amplitude=35, Feature Scale=170, Source=Max(0, Subtract(Max(0, 0.1 - Cell(p)), 1.6*Max(0, -0.3 - Cell(p offset by 40,16))))) with Cell = CellularDistance F1, Feature Scale=110, Size Jitter=0.3.
presets.what: Faceted sand sea with sharp crests and shaded lee faces. Report gives 12.6 ns AVX2. It needs a sand-coloured relief render to read properly.

presets.name: Noodle Caves (stock today)
presets.recipe: Add(LHS=Multiply(a, a), RHS=Multiply(b, b)) with a, b = Perlin at different Seed Offset; cave where value <= 0.017
presets.what: Connected worm caves at about 11% void, per the report. 9.29 ns AVX2 reported. Tube width varies, which is what TubeNoise fixes.

presets.name: Mossy Wall
presets.recipe: HeightBlend(A=TileDomain(Pattern=Courses, Output=TiltedHeight, Bevel=0.1, Mortar=0.05), B=FractalFBm(Octaves=5, Source=Simplex), Control=Remap(Source=FractalFBm(Octaves=3, Source=Perlin)), Height A=tile bevel output, Depth=0.1)
presets.what: Moss fills mortar first and reaches brick tops last. This look was rendered and confirmed in the family. The exact parameters here are my transcription into proposed node names.

presets.name: Leaded Glass and Opus Mosaic
presets.recipe: DomainWarpGradient(low amplitude, Source=TileDomain(Pattern=Fan, Output=TiltedHeight, Mortar=0.03, Bevel=0.12))
presets.what: The warped fan mosaic: stained glass or Roman paving. Rendered in the family at c0ratio 8.0. Cost not measured by me; the fan pattern is the slowest pattern in TileDomain.

presets.name: Slate Roof
presets.recipe: FlowShingle(Angle=1.57, Flow=0.12, Size=0.82, Elongation=1.3, Jitter=0.12, Priority Jitter=0.05, Rim=0.6, Detail=0.12, Tone=0.2, Interior=FractalFBm)
presets.what: Overlapping roof courses, using the parameters behind the roof_tiles image. Rows and courses are visible by design. A warp plus a Slope mask for moss would finish it (untested).

presets.name: Old Eroded Planet
presets.recipe: ErosionFilter(Forward Difference on, Octaves=2, Source=Add(FractalFBm(Octaves=5, Source=Perlin), Multiply(0.5, CraterField(Octaves=12, Lacunarity=1.45, Frequency Slope=2.2, Replay Octaves=4))))
presets.what: Mars-like craters with gullies cut into their rims. UNTESTED graph of two proposed nodes. Crater rims may produce gradient spikes in forward-difference mode.

presets.name: Faulted Cliff Face
presets.recipe: ErosionFilter(Forward Difference on, Source=FaultLines(Fault Count=5, Slip=0.25, Throw=0.15, Zone Width=0.2, Spacing=1.5, Source=Add(Max(S, Terrace(S, Step Count=1.8, Smoothness=0.05)), Gradient)))
presets.what: Layered caprock cut by faults with rills running down the scarps. UNTESTED. Nonzero Zone Width is there to keep scarps from swamping the gradient taps.

presets.name: Calacatta Marble
presets.recipe: DomainWarpShear(Steps=6, Warp Amplitude=0.6, Lacunarity=1.3, Source=Max(Multiply(0.5, FractalFBm(Octaves=4, Source=Perlin)), RootVein(default)))
presets.what: Soft warped body with thin branching veins carried through the same warp. UNTESTED. Line width will vary with stretch, which StrainLines would fix.

presets.name: Snowline Rock
presets.recipe: R = FractalFBm(Octaves=4, Source=SimplexFacet(Output=Lerp, Warp Amplitude=0.5)); HeightBlend(A=R, B=Constant(0.9), Control=Remap(Source=SurfaceProbe(Output=Slope, Source=R), low slope to 1, high slope to 0), Depth=0.1)
presets.what: Faceted rock with snow on flats and bare steep faces. UNTESTED. SurfaceProbe re-evaluates R per tap, so cost is several times the rock.

presets.name: Forest Floor
presets.recipe: HeightBlend(A=PebblePile(Shape=Leaf, Layers=8, Shadow Strength=0.5, Edge Softness=0.03), B=PebblePile(Shape=Pebble, Radius Min=0.25, Layers=6), Control=FractalFBm(Octaves=3, Source=Perlin), Depth=0.1)
presets.what: Leaf litter drifting over stones, with stones poking through. UNTESTED as a blend; both inputs were rendered individually and look right.

presets.name: Pool Floor
presets.recipe: DomainWarpGradient(low amplitude, Source=Multiply(TileDomain(Pattern=Grid, Output=TileValue, Mortar=0.03), Remap(To Min=0.35, To Max=1.6, Source=CausticWeb(Depth=1.1, Steps=3))))
presets.what: Tiled pool with light dancing on it, with tile and caustic wobbling together under one warp. UNTESTED. The warp field is not the caustic's height, so it is an approximation.

overrated: chiral-wallpaper (unique 9, ship): exact and cheap, but it is ornament. Critic's own note says relief is a lattice of repeated craters, and 3D is only a prism. Fine, but below any of the world-gen nodes.
knot-field (look 8, unique 9, status keeper): one centred object, constant -1 elsewhere. Showcase call is right; keeper status should go.
newton-basins (status keeper with call drop): the fronds cover a minority of area on other seeds. The status is simply inconsistent.
domain-warp-flow (look 8, ship): the look is real but is mostly the jets-plus-storms potential, and est 53 ns 3D at 6 steps makes it a bake tool.
quasi-tile (look 8, unique 9): gorgeous in 2D, but 100-200 ns est in 3D and no 4D, so no voxel density and no tiling.
burgers-steepen (ship): stock Modulus scarps look close in relief at 4.59/7.75/12.60 ns measured; exact mode is about 15 source evals.
fiber-noise (ship): fur is the expensive path, and the cheap path looks like pick-up-sticks with a star FFT.
lyapunov-stretch (ship): plaid basket at wide view, blurry 3D. Good material, wrong priority.
textile (ship): lovely weave, near no use for a voxel world, and knit is weak.
tile-split as its own node: it should be a mode of tile-domain; the tile-domain entry already suggests its splits as an option.
spanning-maze port 9: rates simple code, not cost. 3D est 40-60 ns and 4D est 250 ns. The score I give is for the look and proof.
lattice-phasor unique 8: at 3D it is a sheet sponge that TPMS gets at far less cost by estimate, and walls show in steered 2D on all kernels.
underrated: tube-noise clean 5: flakes are real, but cave_bases_s42 is the clearest win in the whole tournament for a voxel world.
cellular-edge-distance look 6: scoring look on a foundation misses the point. Clean mortar in 3D unlocks a whole family.
fault-lines unique 5: a 36-node stock chain is not a usable alternative, it has no 4D, and its 3D dip test came out as tilted chunks.
simplex-facet look 6: bare 3D vol is cut crystal at est 1.7 ns.
height-blend unique 4: every material border in a world uses this, and it halves measured cost compared with the graph (10.0 vs 21.4 ns 2D, two 4-octave fractals; graph re-evaluates sources).
surface-probe look 4: a daily tool should not be judged on its image.
grounded-scatter port 5: the only entry that replaces a placement pass.
strata-caverns unique 4: the node call is right, but it is still the only walkable cave.
quad-stamp unique 5: est 4-6 ns in any dimension against 227 ns 3D measured for the graph, for block and city masks.
bubble-invert (showcase): about 1.2 ns map cost measured and 3D sphere clusters look superb.
self-gated-fbm (discovery): zero new code, 8.56 ns, should ship now.
Simplex-window Voronoi (discovery): 6/8/10 sites against 9/27/81 could reprice every cell node in 3D and 4D. Scalar 309 vs 871 ns 3D; AVX2 unported. Clamped masks only.
exact-step divisor (discovery): one subtraction per axis moves FD gradients from about 1e4 to about 1e6 features.
Value-term shared lattice (discovery): applies to any multi-channel gradient noise at one lattice visit.
panel.comments:
How I judged: I viewed all 23 family sheets and the discoveries sheet, plus about 15 full images. I ran no exes and measured nothing: every ns, c0 and connectivity figure above is quoted from tournament.json, except where labelled as my estimate. Crossbreed and preset costs are my estimates, and no crossbreed has been built.

Ten ids have no thumb on their sheet. occlusion-stack, dislocation-stripes, defect-stripes, steered-band-noise and flow-strokes were judged from other images showing the look. boulder-field-3d was judged from chisel images under grounded-scatter. radial-phasor was judged from its discovery image. phase-vortex and cellular-fracture were judged from prose only, so weight those low.

Warnings on the evidence:
1. Cost is provisional. I saw no entry whose ns comes from a real FastSIMD node. Measured figures are hand-written AVX2 kernels or graphs of existing nodes via fnlab; most others are op-count or scalar-ratio estimates. There is no SSE41, AVX512 or NEON parity evidence for any new idea. A stock brick graph already failed AVX512 parity on 27% of samples.
2. The c0ratio test is blind to integer lattice seams. I read ContinuityProbe in lab_proto.h: default origin (0.37, 0.61), sample spacing 0.01, steps of at most 8e-3, so no sample pair crosses an integer line, which confirms the Voronoi critic's finding. That critic moved the origin and saw GiniFoam go 7.93 to 1.00. It re-tested only its own family. So treat c0 near 8 on any unit-lattice node elsewhere as unverified until re-run with a straddling origin. lab_proto.h is still unchanged.
3. Licence: steerable-perlin is reported as not clean-room (shader-derived catalogue and dem_steer were read before the paper). Write that port fresh from the paper and its supplemental. Dendry's reference code is GPL; the notes say it was not fetched, so keep it that way.

Obvious holes in the set:
A. No shared gradient path. Erosion, slope, curl, flow, steerable direction, iso-distance, crest, caustic, root-vein and others each pay FD taps or carry a private derivative Perlin. Nobody prototyped a value-plus-gradient Gen on Perlin, Simplex and fractals. I think this is the highest-leverage work in the project, above any single node. Surface-probe's 57.88 ns 3D graph at 5 octaves should collapse to about one FBm plus overhead (my estimate). Related: outputs such as winner value, id and frame have no route except modes, and DrainageFrame is stuck for lack of vector output.
B. No real 3D terrain. Erosion is a heightfield, catchment is laminae, dendry is rods, and fractal-derivative's vol is lumps. For a voxel world with overhangs, this is the largest content gap. SurfaceFlutes above is my attempt.
C. No column awareness. A 2D height subtree inside a 3D graph is re-evaluated per voxel. GeneratorCache does not rescue this (21.9 vs 21.4 ns measured, single slot), and grounded-scatter pays 9 height evals per voxel. Engines will have to split graphs by hand unless the graph can run dependency-aware 2D prepasses on grid generation. Since many top picks here are 2D-only, this decides their real price.
D. No LOD. Hard-edged outputs (labels, tiles, mosaics) alias at distance, fine lines dash at low resolution (root-vein at 32 px, erosion dashes in wide views), and octave counts cannot vary per lane. Nothing offers a footprint or fractional-octave input, which a world at scale needs for distant chunks.
E. Weak tiling and 4D. QuasiTile, dendry, catchment, fisk and erosion's lattice lack ordinary 4D. Stripes lose width on the torus, and bond is dots through it. Torus-angle wrapping works for erosion in a scalar proof only.
F. Placement output. Stamps fill density, but nothing returns a stable feature id or per-feature parameters for placing trees or structures, beyond cell hash values.

Top-25 note: dendry-noise (6.5) ranks above higher-scored pebble-pile, caustic-web and tile-split because nothing else makes a river tree; tile-split is excluded as a mode of tile-domain. strata-caverns and self-gated-fbm are graph presets, not node requests.

crossbreeds.name: WalkableWorms
crossbreeds.why: Tube-noise has the best cave section here and strata-caverns has the only floors you can walk on. A round worm tangle is a fall-through hazard in a voxel game. TubeNoise already computes the offset vector to the axis, so a flat floor costs almost nothing. Not built or rendered: untested idea.
crossbreeds.algorithm: One Perlin lattice visit as in TubeNoise: channels n0,n1,n2 with gradients g0,g1,g2 and the per-vertex value term. Apply a fixed Y squash sy (about 0.4) to the input, and multiply g.y by sy by chain rule so results are in world units. For each of the 3 fixed channel pairs: A = J J^T + Damping*I (2x2), lambda = A^-1 n, r = J^T lambda, the first-order vector from curve to sample. Keep the r with min |r| using Select. sd = SmoothMax( |r| - R, -r.y - F*R, k ), giving a round roof and a flat floor F*R below the axis. Steep axes have r perpendicular to the axis, so r.y stays near 0 and the floor does not cut: shafts stay round. Output Clamp( sd / R ). No window, no per-lane control flow. 4D uses the same algebra with a 4 component r. Cost estimate: network 5-7.5 ns 3D (tournament estimate) plus about 0.3 ns. Inherits the flat lens flakes.

crossbreeds.name: SurfaceFlutes (3D erosion)
crossbreeds.parents: erosion-filter + steerable-perlin (Sheets) + surface-probe + wide-stencil FD discovery
crossbreeds.why: The biggest hole for a voxel world: every terrain winner is a heightfield, and raw erosion in 3D is vertical extrusion. This puts downhill flutes on any isosurface, including overhangs and cave walls. Not built or rendered: untested idea.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Density S, solid above 0. Tetra jet: 4 Source taps at stencil h near the flute wavelength, exact-step divisor. g = grad S, n = g*InvSqrt(g.g), t = down - n*dot(n,down), L = |t|, surface distance s = S*InvSqrt(g.g). Thin direction b = normalize(cross(n,t)). Fixed loop over O octaves (default 2): run one steerable-perlin octave in Sheets topology with d = b, using G v = e1 v + (e0-e1)(d.v)d per corner; sign of d does not matter because d appears twice. Take a ridged value and analytic gradient from the same corner sum. Add that gradient to g scaled by the octave amplitude, then recompute t and b for the next octave: that is the erosion filter's branching rule. Output S + Strength * smoothstep(Band,0,|s|) * smoothstep(0.1,0.4,L) * sum(gain^i * v_i). The L term fades flat tops and ceilings, where t is undefined, so it stays C0 there. Cost estimate: 4*Source + 2*2.89 ns (hand kernel, 3D) + about 1 ns; about 30 ns on a 3-octave Perlin density. No per-lane early out, so the engine should run it only in surface-band chunks. 4D steerable has a timing kernel only. Risk: 3D sheet aspect is about 3.3, so flutes may read short.

crossbreeds.name: CellDomain
crossbreeds.parents: cellular-edge-distance + plate-drift + nested-voronoi + tile-domain per-tile frame + NestedCracks + facet shatter
crossbreeds.why: Half the striking discoveries are the same thing: evaluate a child in the frame of the owning cell, hide the jump in a grout line. NestedCracks, terrazzo, facet shatter and plate-of-plates each got their own code or a large graph. One node makes them all short graphs. It does not reproduce plate-drift's wedge gaps, because cell outlines do not rotate. Not built: untested idea.
crossbreeds.algorithm: 3^D window pass keeping rel[i], hash[i], F1 site and hash h. Bisector pass as cellular-edge-distance: e = min over j of dot(.5*(rel[j]+rel1), n)*InvSqrt(n.n), with Grid Jitter capped at the audited value. Frame q = R(h)*(p - site)*Scale + Offset(h), with R a table rotation in 2D or a hash-derived Householder in 3D/4D, no trig. v = Source.Gen( seed ^ h, q ), one eval with a per-lane seed. Optional tilt: v += dot(tilt(h), rel1). Output Lerp( Grout, v, smoothstep(0,W,e) ), with W a hybrid. At e = 0 both sides return Grout, so it is C0 whatever v does. Nesting is a Source that is another CellDomain; child jumps vanish under the parent grout. Cost estimate: 5.5/16/50 ns plus one Source per level (edge pass figure from the tournament), any dimension.

crossbreeds.name: QuickShatter
crossbreeds.parents: Simplex-window Voronoi discovery + simplex-facet PL warp + shatter-bsp
crossbreeds.why: The 3D and 4D price of cracks is the main barrier for shatter in volumes. Simplex-window uses 6/8/10 sites against 9/27/81, but its cells drift toward honeycomb in 3D. A PL warp breaks that regularity with no search. Not built or rendered: untested combination.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Step 1: simplex lattice at frequency fw, hash D+1 corners to vectors, barycentric interpolate, p2 = p + A*v (piecewise linear). Step 2: at p2, search the D+1 simplex corners plus the D+1 face-opposite vertices, c_(m-1)+c_(m+1)-c_m, at jitter rings .28/.17/.14; keep F1 site, rel and hash. Step 3: bisector pass over those same sites, then e = Min(e, 0.10), since only clamped masks were exact in the audit. Step 4: fixed L=3 BSP levels: plane from hash(F1, path), side bit updates path, e = Min(e, taper^l * |dot(rel,n)-o|). Step 5: output a Lerp of leaf hash value toward Grout by smoothstep(e/W). Cost estimate: about 7/12/18 ns against the shatter-bsp estimate of 7/18/52 ns, so the win is 3D and 4D only. Limits: width varies with warp Jacobian, no wide bevels, and walls kink at PL creases.

crossbreeds.name: JointBlocks
crossbreeds.parents: fault-lines + multigrid-noise + cellular-planes + jointed strata discovery
crossbreeds.why: Real cliff faces are blocks bounded by long joint sets with small offsets. Fault-lines gives offsets with no grout, Multigrid gives cheap regions and exact plane distance, neither gives blocks. No window, cost flat in dimension, and a 4D form that survives tiling better than graphs using DomainRotate. Not built: untested idea.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Fixed loop over N families (3-6) with golden-angle or table normals n_i and spacing s_i: u = dot(p,n_i)/s_i + phi_i, k = Floor(u), f = u - k; e = Min(e, s_i*Min(f,1-f)); id = id ^ (k*Prime_i); off += slipdir_i * rnd11(hash(k,i)) * Slip * s_i. After the loop: v = Source.Gen( seed, p + off ) + dot(tilt(id), p - Round(p)) omitted by default because it jumps; use only under grout. Output Lerp( -Depth, v, smoothstep(0,W,e) ): at a joint e = 0 on both sides, so the block jump is hidden and it is C0. Optional per-family tip mask from a low frequency hybrid, as in fault_drag_tips. Cost estimate: about 1-1.5 ns per family (fault-lines figure), so 8 ns plus Source at N=6. Risk: long straight runs, measured at 86.8 units on Multigrid N=7; a Perlin warp cut that to 10.8 units.

crossbreeds.name: FoamWalls
crossbreeds.why: Cracks around non-convex organic plates with constant world-space width. Voronoi cannot do non-convex; Foam Margin blurs where the top two fields run parallel. Analytic gradients avoid FoamBlend's 3N evaluations. Not built: untested idea.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Fixed loop k<K (default 5): (s_k, g_k) = Perlin value + analytic gradient at p + offset_k with seed + k*stride. Masked update of winner value s1, its gradient g1 and label. Second fixed loop over j<K: d = (s1 - s_j) * InvSqrt( |g1 - g_j|^2 + eps ); e = Min( e, Select( j==label, +large, d ) ). This is a min over all fields rather than a rank-2 pick, so there is no jump when rank 2 changes, and e reaches 0 from both sides at a winner change. Outputs: Wall smoothstep(e/W), Plate rnd11(hash(label)) lifted by bevel(e), Winner value under grout, all C0 except raw Label. Cost estimate: K * about 1.3x Perlin + K InvSqrt: about 8 / 16 / 30 ns (2D/3D/4D) at K=5, against 3N source taps for FD. Keep the per-field offset, since Perlin ties at vertices. Risk: specks where a field difference has a saddle near a tie, as FoamBlend v2 showed.

crossbreeds.name: GroundedCrystals
crossbreeds.parents: grounded-scatter + chisel-rubble + cellular-shape needle rods + simplex-facet look
crossbreeds.why: Faceted crystal outcrops rooted on terrain, with no placement pass. Crystal clusters are a staple voxel request and no graph can rotate per-instance prisms. Not built: untested idea.
crossbreeds.algorithm: XZ column lattice, fixed 3x3 window; column hash ignores y. For each column: site from hash, H = Height.Gen(site.xz) (9 evals), base b = (site.x, H - Sink, site.z). For M fixed crystals per column (M=2): axis a = normalize(up + Tilt*hashDir), frame u,v from hash bits by fixed cross products; q = p - b; along = dot(q,a); r_hex = Max(|q.u|*.866 + |q.v|*.5, |q.v|); sd = Max( r_hex - w, along - L + Tip*r_hex, -along ). Union by Min over 18 prisms, then Max with terrain density if Output = Union. Window rule: L*|a.xz| + w <= 1 - jitter/2, same reach bound as CellularShape, or seams appear. Cost estimate: about 10 ns + 9*Height + 18 prisms at about 0.7 ns: about 60-65 ns with a 2-octave Perlin height. Surface-band chunks only. No 4D form proposed.

crossbreeds.name: GeodeField
crossbreeds.why: True spheres are exact distance fields, so banded shells get constant thickness. Each geode needs its own band sequence, which a Terrace on a distance output cannot give. Own-cell kernel means no window. Not built: untested idea.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Fixed level loop as BubblePack (own cell, one hash per cell per level, L(L+1)/2 lookups): q in cell frame, centre c(hash), radius r(hash); d = |q-c| - r in world units. Masked update of min d, its h and r. Density output: Max( d, -(Thick*r + d) ) inverted so the shell is solid with an air core. Bands output: b = Floor( -d / T ); value = rnd11( hash(h, b) ), hard by design, or a smoothed jitter profile from strata-bands. Density is a min of continuous functions, so C0; Bands is a material id with jumps. Evaluate Bands only on solid voxels. Cost estimate: 15 ns 3D at L=7 (BubblePack estimate) + about 1 ns. Inherits top-level lattice and occasional overlaps.

crossbreeds.name: SupplyDunes
crossbreeds.why: Barchan is one stamped dune at 20-22 ns measured and never merges; vortex dunes merge but are only transverse. A sand supply hybrid could run one field from isolated dunes to continuous ridges at a quarter of the cost. Whether horns form is unknown, so test this before believing it.
crossbreeds.algorithm: A,B = Perlin sources, B offset. Unit phasor z = (A+iB)*InvSqrt(A^2+B^2+eps^2). phase = arg(z) by polynomial atan2 + 2pi*f*dot(w,p); t = Fract(phase/2pi). Stoss and slip profile: h0 = Min( t/Stoss, smoothstep( 1, Stoss, t ) ). Amplitude taper a = smoothstep( 0, Core, Sqrt(A^2+B^2) ), which narrows crests towards vortex cores. Output Max( 0, a*h0 - (1 - Supply) ), Supply a hybrid. No window, dimension via sources; heightfield in use, so per column. Cost estimate: 5-6 ns 2D. Risk: clipping likely gives lens shapes rather than true crescents without crest curvature from a low-frequency warp.

presets.name: Plains And Peaks (existing nodes)
presets.recipe: MaxSmooth(LHS=FractalFBm(Octaves=6, Gain=Remap(From Min=-0.3, From Max=1, To Min=0, To Max=0.75, Clamp Output=True, Source=Simplex), Source=Simplex), RHS=-0.3, Smoothness=0.5)
presets.what: Flat lowlands with rough peaks and no new code. Measured in the tournament at 9.33 ns AVX2 2D, 0 FAIL in check. Should be the default terrain preset today.

presets.name: Eroded Highlands
presets.recipe: ErosionFilter(Octaves=2, Strength=0.15, Stripe Frequency=0.6, Branching=0.3, Output=Height, altitude fade on, FD stencil=0.2, Source=Plains And Peaks)
presets.what: Gullied mountains over plains. Critic measured 25.6 ns for 2-octave erosion on its own base in a hand AVX2 harness; on this 3-tap source about 40 ns per column (my estimate). Not rendered on this exact base. Evaluate per column.

presets.name: Noodle Caves (existing nodes)
presets.recipe: Add(LHS=Multiply(LHS=a,RHS=a), RHS=Multiply(LHS=b,RHS=b)), a and b = Perlin at different Seed Offset, cave where value <= 0.017
presets.what: Connected caves with no new node: 9.29 ns AVX2 measured, 99.99-100.00% core connection at 11% void. Flanged webs, not round. The bar TubeNoise must beat.

presets.name: Worm Caves
presets.recipe: Min(Terrain Density, Subtract(Add(TubeNoise(Mode=Network, Output=Distance, Feature Scale=F), Multiply(FractalFBm(Octaves=3, Source=Perlin), 0.05*F)), Radius))
presets.what: Round tunnels with world-unit rough walls, as in tube_rough_network. TubeNoise est 5-7.5 ns 3D plus 3 octaves. Terrain composition not rendered.

presets.name: Walkable Caverns (existing nodes)
presets.recipe: The graph recipe
presets.what: Flat floors, domes, per-layer plans, shafts, with y warp and dip. 33.92 ns AVX2 3D measured; 100.00% core connection on 3 seeds at recommended parameters per the critic. Connectivity numbers for the graph itself were not stated separately.

presets.name: Bone Caves
presets.recipe: DomainWarpGradient(two octaves, a=6.6 equivalent amplitude, Source=TPMSNoise(Family=Gyroid)), iso about 0.887 at period 1.5, or today the graph recipe under the same warp
presets.what: Foam skeleton with three-way junctions, the best connected-cave image in the tube family. Gyroid graph 3.69 ns 3D measured; warp adds cost. Amplitude does not transfer directly from prototype Perlin to real warp node, so tune it.

presets.name: Faulted Rock Layers
presets.recipe: FaultLines(Fault Count=6, Spacing=1.5, Slip=0.3, Density=0.8, Zone Width=0.25, Source=StrataBands(Source=Add(Gradient(Y), Multiply(Perlin, 0.25))))
presets.what: Rock material field with displaced beds. Evaluate only on solid voxels. Est about 15 ns 3D. The stock fallback measured 46.71 ns 3D.

presets.name: Banded Stone (existing nodes)
presets.recipe: PingPong(Ping Pong Strength=9.5, Source=PowFloat(Value=Add(PowInt(Pow=2,Value=A),PowInt(Pow=2,Value=B)),Pow=0.5)), A and B Perlin, B offset and Seed Offset 1
presets.what: Nested agate bands for stone colour and veins: 4.57 / 7.53 / 12.37 ns AVX2 measured.

presets.name: Biome Map
presets.recipe: ExchangeFoam(Phases=5, Output=Label, Weight Ratio set for rarity, Source=DomainWarpGradient(Source=Perlin)), paired with same seed Output=Margin for border width
presets.what: Non-convex biome regions with any-to-any contact and islands for rare labels. Per column; est 6.5 ns plus warp. Gumbel shares measured within about .01 of target but sensitive to source std.

presets.name: Boulder Scree
presets.recipe: GroundedScatter(Height=shared 2-octave terrain height, Density=Remap(SurfaceProbe(Output=Slope, Source=Height)), Facet=6, Cut=0.68, Aspect=0.35, Sink=0.4, Output=UnionDensity)
presets.what: Angular rocks resting on the ground, denser on slopes. Est about 55 ns plus probe; not rendered with the slope density. Fallback: spheres, 36.8 ns measured.

presets.name: Mossy Ruin Wall
presets.recipe: HeightBlend(A=TileDomain(Pattern=Courses, Tile Width=2, Tile Height=0.9, Mortar=0.05, Bevel=0.12, Output=TiltedHeight), B=FractalFBm(Source=Perlin), Control=FractalFBm(Source=Perlin), Height A=tile bevel)
presets.what: Moss takes the mortar first, brick tops last, as rendered in materials_mossy_wall_heightblend. In 3D set Z Length for real blocks. Native HeightBlend costs sources plus under 1 ns by estimate.

presets.name: Crystal Vein Rock
presets.recipe: Fade(A=Rock, B=SimplexFacet(Lattice=Simplex, Output=Flat, PL Warp=0.5), Fade=Remap(TubeNoise(Mode=Tube, Output=Distance, Radius=0.05)))
presets.what: Cut-crystal facets along thin vein tubes. SimplexFacet est 1.7-3.5 ns 3D, tube est 4.5-6.5 ns. Composition not rendered.

presets.name: Moon Ground
presets.recipe: CraterField(Octaves=12, Lacunarity=1.45, Replay Octaves=4, Density=1, Base Source=FractalFBm(Octaves=4, Source=Perlin))
presets.what: Flat floors, rims, fresh craters on old ones. Est 9-18 ns plus base. Same node at iso 0.03 in 3D gives limestone pits. Stock one-scale fallback 65 ns 3D measured, clipped at Voronoi edges.

overrated: knot-field (look 8, unique 9): the fibre bundle is the prettiest image in the tournament and it is still a single centred object that is -1 everywhere else; it has no business in the node list.
dendry-noise (ship): 2700 ns scalar, 60-250 ns estimated, no 4D, port 4. The only real river tree, but as a FastNoise node it is a support problem; showcase or external bake.
cumulus-noise (keeper): port 3 and 40-120 ns estimated for one 3D look.
tile-split (keeper, ship): a duplicate of TileDomain's Courses/Running/Basket/Herringbone patterns; two nodes for one look.
burgers-steepen (ship): c0 1.01 by design, pinholes at 5 evals, 17 evals for the clean form, and a stock Modulus sawtooth gets the one-sided cliffs at 4.6 ns measured.
fault-lines (keeper): a 36-node stock chain gives the cross-cut look at 9-18 ns measured; the node only saves node count.
strata-caverns (look 7, keeper): the critic's own call is graph-recipe; the flat-floored galleries are slab maths over a plan source.
grounded-scatter (ship): 55-140 ns estimated, 3D only, and Max(Gradient, CellularLookup sphere) gets most of it.
flow-strokes (look 8): discontinuous by design with ink-black gaps; a mode of a niche stamp.
vortex-cells (ship as own swirl node): stamped ovals on straight bands, an ornament, not a flow.
tpms-noise (keeper): the gyroid is three SineWave terms from stock; the seven-surface enum is exactly the enum sprawl to avoid.
coral-noise (unique 9, keeper): 125-225 ns estimated and 3-7 microseconds scalar; a bake object.

The critics' 'unique' scores in general: unique was repeatedly awarded before the stock-graph rival was built, and in six families the rival then matched the node (puffy-caps, strata-terrace, fractal-multifractal, cellular-planes, domain-quasicrystal, contour-scarp).
underrated: height-blend (look 6, unique 4): the highest utility per line of code in the tournament; under 1 ns over the sources, port 9, and the mossy-wall image makes the case in one glance.
