bubble-invert (showcase): a 1-3 ns measured domain modifier with a proven Lipschitz bound and looks (frogspawn, nested sphere clusters) that no existing node makes; it should be a ship as DomainInvert.

cellular-edge-distance (look 6): judged as a correction rather than a look, but it fixes every cellular crack picture and the critic rated the dramatic shatter-bsp above it; the foundation deserves the top mark.

stamp-scatter (look 6): a plain thumbnail hides that it is an instancing framework; craters, bubbles, pebbles and rosettes all run through it, and the no-pop proof with a positive control is the best verification in the set.
simplex-facet (look 6): the cheapest new primitive (0.56x Perlin scalar) with the best low-poly 3D volume; the 2D quilt complaint goes away with the PL warp.
tube-noise (clean 5): measured c0 7.85 and range -1..0.993 across 2D/3D/4D; cleaner than its score, and the most valuable 3D result here for the library's main audience.
truchet-noise (promising, ship-as-mode): ~1.2 ns estimated, classic look, 3D tube tangle; its cave failure was a static-init bug in the harness, not the node.
growth-age (showcase): wood is among the most requested materials and the Timber remap reads as a planed board at ~5 ns estimated; worth more than most showcases.
multigrid-noise (look 6): a 0.5-1 ns estimated aperiodic arrangement node in 2D/3D/4D with a working torus map; with the phason breaker on by default it is a cheap new partition.

the Simplex-window Voronoi discovery (cracks): 6/8/10 sites instead of 9/27/81 is the only finding that changes the cost of the whole cellular family in 3D/4D, and it sits unranked in a discovery list.
the exact-step divisor and fourth-root step law (probes): unglamorous, but they fix finite differences at far coordinates for every derivative-using node in the tournament.
panel.comments:
Method and honesty. I read all 24 sheets and 13 individual images, then the critics' notes. I ran nothing; every nanosecond and every c0ratio above is the critics' number, and I kept their estimate/measured labels. Scores are from a maintainer's seat (small coherent set, few enums, no duplicates, predictable range, low burden), so a beautiful hero object scores below a plain cheap primitive.

What I would actually ship from this tournament, as nodes: CellularEdge (exact inset, with Levels=ShatterBSP, hybrid Edge Width/Depth, site colours; shatter-bsp, edge-fate, crease, fracture, crystal all collapse into it), GradedVoronoi (or a Level hybrid on the Cellular nodes), one OwnCellStamp node (crater-field, bubble-pack, pebble-pile, quad-stamp as Shape, stamp-scatter's cascade fade as the overlap rule), DomainWarpCurl with Steps, DomainWarpFlow as its heavy sibling, SteerablePerlin, TubeNoise (Network default), HeightBlend, ExchangeFoam, SurfaceProbe (Slope/Laplacian/SignedDistance outputs), LatticePhasor (hex layout, Direction hybrid, Arms int), TileDomain cut down to Pattern/Bevel/Mortar/Rotation/Source, Textile, QuasiTile (2D/3D, documented as non-tiling), SpanningMaze, ChiralWallpaper, SimplexFacet (with CellularFacetMesh as a 2D mode), DomainInvert (bubble-invert), ErosionFilter at 2 octaves if the derivative work below is done, CausticWeb. That is about 20 nodes; everything else in the 121 is a mode of one of these, a preset of stock nodes, or a showcase.

Range: most winners do not natively hit [-1,1] (crater -0.76..0.47, caustic-web -0.772..1, strata-terrace -1.15..1.28, newton unnormalised). Each shipped node needs a measured ScaleOutput constant and a VariableRange mixin; the critics only flagged this for some.

The obvious hole is architectural, not a missing look. Seven of the strongest results (steerable-perlin, erosion-filter, surface-probe, crest-lines, fractal-derivative, root-vein, domain-warp-curl, tube-noise's Jacobian estimate) all want the gradient of a source, and each prototype solved it its own way (analytic Perlin derivative, forward differences, central stencils, tetra jets). FastNoise has no analytic-gradient kernel and no derivative interface. One decision, a GenGrad path on Perlin/Simplex plus a finite-difference fallback with the exact-step divisor and fourth-root step law from the probes family, unlocks half the tournament at once and should be done before any of those nodes.

Second hole: 4D. QuasiTile, dendry, grounded-scatter, cellular-facet-mesh, flow-shingle (81 candidates), quad-stamp 3D graphs and several others either skip 4D or explode in it, and GenTileable2D silently breaks for them. Nodes that cannot do 4D should say so in metadata rather than fall back to dropping w.

Third hole: nothing new for animated or volumetric clouds (cumulus is 40-120 ns and port 3, wave-noise failed), and no cheap connected-cave guarantee outside bond-tunnels' lattice plumbing; TubeNoise Network is the practical answer but connectivity is empirical. Nothing addresses hex-lattice variants of the coherent noises either, which is a long-standing request that TileDomain Hex only half answers.

Duplicates to collapse before anything ships: tile-split into TileDomain; the five crack entries into CellularEdge; five stamp entries into one stamp node; shear-flow / domain-warp-sine / feistel / lyapunov into one shear warp (and I would still question that one against DomainWarpFractalProgressive); domain-warp-source and scatter-warp into Curl/Flow; phasor-noise / dislocation / defect / radial / phase-vortex into LatticePhasor and vortex-phase; tpms into the gyroid recipe.

crossbreeds.name: CellularScaffold
crossbreeds.parents: cellular-edge-distance x tube-noise x gini-foam (trabecular iso discovery)
crossbreeds.why: The gini-foam trabecular vol and the tube-noise worms show that struts along Voronoi edges are a wanted 3D look (bone, coral rock, Plateau borders) and that round sections beat ribbons. Nothing gives distance to the Voronoi edge skeleton; the exact bisector pass already has everything needed.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Standard 3^D cellular search keeping the three (3D: four) nearest sites s1..s3 and distances F1..F3. From the bisector pass compute exact inset to each neighbour: d1j = (Fj^2 - F1^2) / (2 |sj - s1|) for j = 2,3. Edge distance e = sqrt(d12^2 + d13^2) (3D: distance to the line where three cells meet; 2D: distance to the Voronoi vertex, so expose Mode {Edges, Vertices}). Output = 1 - Min(e / Radius, 1) scaled to [-1,1]; hybrid Radius. All terms are continuous functions of continuous F's, fixed loop, no extra hashes; cost about 1.4x CellularDistance by the critic's per-site op count (estimate). Threshold at 0 gives a connected strut network; Radius from a Level source gives bone that thins with height.

crossbreeds.name: GradedStamp
crossbreeds.parents: graded-voronoi x stamp-scatter x crater-field / bubble-pack
crossbreeds.why: graded-voronoi proved that grading feature size by a hybrid Level across space works without seams; crater-field and bubble-pack are own-cell multi-level stamps with a fixed size spectrum. Breeding them gives craters, vesicles or texture islands whose size follows a map (big craters on highlands, pumice that gets finer towards a rim) in one node.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Sample Level L(p) once at the lane position. For k = 0..Levels-1 (fixed int loop): scale s_k = ratio^k; cell c_k = Floor(p * s_k); h = hash(seed + k, c_k); centre = (c_k + 0.5 + jitter(h) * 0.5 * (1 - 2 r_k)) / s_k with radius r_k = rmin + bits(h) * (rmax - rmin) so the stamp never leaves its own cell (one hash per level, no window). Profile f = Shape(|p - centre| * s_k / r_k) from {Crater, Dome, Disc, Source sampled in the stamp frame}. Level weight a_k = SmoothStep(L(p) - (k - Levels/2) * Spacing, Width) * density gate from spare bits. Compose with the cascade fade from stamp-scatter: out = Lerp(out, f, inside_k * a_k) in youngest-last order (Erase) or Max or Sum via a 3-value enum. Because a_k depends on L(p) at the sample and not at the cell, a stamp fades in as a whole across its own footprint: no pop. Cost about 1 hash + 1 profile per level + 1 Level eval, dimension agnostic (estimate).

crossbreeds.name: FlowCellular
crossbreeds.why: steerable-perlin showed that a per-lane hybrid direction turns an isotropic primitive into a flow-aligned one at modest cost, and cell-frame showed per-grain streaks are wanted but cost 3-4 source evals. Stretching the cellular metric by one direction eval gives elongated flow-aligned cells (wood rays, muscle fibre, flowstone, ice) with F1 / F2-F1 / exact edge outputs for about one extra source eval.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Evaluate hybrid Direction once at the lane position: angle theta (2D) or unit vector u (3D, from a vector-valued hybrid or a DomainWarp-style triple). Build M = R diag(1, 1/Aspect, 1/Aspect) R^T once per lane (Aspect >= 1, contraction only, so the 3^D window bound of the unchanged jitter lattice still holds). Run the ordinary cellular window search with d = |M (p - site)| for every candidate; keep the bisector pass for the exact inset under the same metric (d1j = (Fj^2 - F1^2) / (2 |M (sj - s1)|)). Outputs F1, F2-F1, EdgeDistance, CellValue. Since M is the same for all candidates in a lane and theta is continuous, F1 and F2 remain continuous; discontinuity in Direction is the user's. Cost = CellularDistance + 1 Direction eval + D^2 multiply-adds per candidate (estimate 1.2x Cellular plus the direction source).

crossbreeds.name: InvertedStamp (Apollonian craters)
crossbreeds.why: bubble-invert is a 1-3 ns domain modifier with a proven Lipschitz bound, and its frogspawn image shows inversion turns any cellular source into nested clusters. Fed with craters or bubbles it gives craters inside craters and vesicle clusters inside vesicles, a nesting look the own-cell stamps cannot make with a fixed size ladder.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Level-0 own-cell sphere per lane: c = cell centre + jitter, radius r, confined to its cell. q = p - c, rho2 = Max(q.q, (eps r)^2). If rho2 < r^2: p' = c + q * r^2 / rho2 (inversion), else p' = p (identity outside the sphere; continuous at the rim since the map is identity there). Repeat for Iterations (fixed int, 1 or 2) with the next finer own-cell lattice. Evaluate the stamp family (GradedStamp or any Source) at p'. The map's Lipschitz constant is 1/eps^Iterations as bubble-invert measured, so the output stays continuous with a known slope bound. Cost 1-3 ns per iteration plus the stamp (estimate from the bubble-invert AVX2 port).

crossbreeds.name: ShatterPlates
crossbreeds.parents: plate-drift x cellular-edge-distance (Levels) x cellular-planes x height-blend
crossbreeds.why: plate-drift's tilted rigid plates were its strong image and its bevel mask the weak one; CellularEdge with Levels gives exact T-junction shards; height-blend fills gaps with a second material so features interlock. Together: broken flagstone / tumbled slate with soil in the cracks, in one pass.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Run CellularEdge with Levels = ShatterBSP cuts to get shard id h, shard anchor a (site, or parent site plus cut index) and exact inset e. Per shard from h: lift l in [-1,1], tilt vector t with |t| <= Tilt, so plate height H = l + Dot(t, p - a), clamped to the shard by the inset band: H_plate = Lerp(soil, H, SmoothStep(e / Bevel)). Then HeightBlend(H_plate, Soil(p), HeightA = H_plate + Bias, HeightB = Soil(p), Softness) where Soil is any Source: soil fills where it is higher than the plate top, plate corners poke through. All pointwise: one cellular edge pass, one source eval, no sort. Cost about 1.5x CellularDistance + Source (estimate).

crossbreeds.name: BeddingTubes
crossbreeds.parents: tube-noise x strata-caverns x bedding warp (networks discovery)
crossbreeds.why: tube-noise gives round worm tunnels but no stratigraphy; strata-caverns gives flat-floored galleries but is a graph recipe. Tubes constrained to bedding planes give limestone-style galleries that run laterally along layers and connect through short cross-cuts, which is the actual look of karst.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Two channels as in tube-noise Network mode: n0 = Perlin(seed, x, y, z) and n1 = Saw(y' / Thickness) - 0.5 where y' = y + Dip.x * x + Dip.y * z + Fold * Perlin(seed+1, x * ff, z * ff) (the bedding warp) and Saw is a sawtooth with hashed per-layer thickness from Floor(y'/Thickness). Tube distance d = sqrt(n0^2 + n1^2) / sqrt(|grad n0|^2 |grad n1|^2 - (grad n0 . grad n1)^2)^(1/2) exactly as tube-noise estimates distance to the intersection curve, with the gradients from the derivative Perlin kernel and the analytic saw gradient. Output 1 - d / Radius. Add a third channel n2 = Perlin(seed+2) and take the Min over pairs (tube-noise Network rule) for cross-cuts between layers. Cost about tube-noise Network plus one cheap analytic channel (estimate 5-8 ns 3D).

crossbreeds.name: FoamBlend
crossbreeds.parents: exchange-foam x height-blend x FoamBlend v2 (regions discovery)
crossbreeds.why: exchange-foam gives the best region labels, height-blend gives the best material transition, and biome-blend failed because its borders were cell-scale scallops. Combining label margin with height-driven blending gives biome transitions where pebbles stay whole and sand fills first, from the K evals already paid.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Evaluate K control fields c_k (K fixed int, one Source at K seed offsets, or K sources). a = argmax c_k, b = second, margin m = c_a - c_b >= 0 (continuous, zero on the border). Evaluate the two winning material sources S_a, S_b only (2 evals, selected per lane by masks over a fixed loop of the N materials: everything costs its worst case, so N materials = N evals in SIMD; document that). Blend w = SmoothStep((H_a + m * Gain) - H_b, Softness) with H the materials' own heights (their value, or a Height input); out = Lerp(S_b, S_a, w). Away from the border m is large and the winner dominates; on the border the height difference decides, so the seam follows the features. Discontinuity only where argmax changes, where m = 0 and w is decided by heights alone, which is continuous in H. Cost K + N source evals + a few ops (estimate).

presets.name: Mossy stone wall
presets.recipe: HeightBlend( A = TileDomain( Pattern=Courses, Bevel=0.1, Mortar=0.05, Rotation=Random, Source=FractalFBm( Octaves=3, Source=Perlin( Feature Scale=18 ) ) ), B = FractalFBm( Octaves=5, Source=Simplex( Feature Scale=40 ) ), Height A = the TileDomain bevel output, Height B = B, Softness=0.1 )
presets.what: The mossy_wall_heightblend image: a random-course stone wall with moss filling the joints and low stones first, both materials crisp. Replaces the usual see-through Fade.

presets.name: Alpine ridges with gullies
presets.recipe: Add( ErosionFilter( Stripe Octaves=2, Altitude Fade=0.6, Source=FractalFBm( Octaves=3, Source=Perlin( Feature Scale=600 ) ) ), Multiply( FractalRidged( Octaves=4, Source=Simplex( Feature Scale=120 ) ), 0.12 ) )
presets.what: The erosion-filter relief: smooth hills whose flanks carry branching V gullies feeding valleys, with ridged crests on top. The 2-octave form is the one the critic costed at 25 ns 2D.

presets.name: Cratered moon
presets.recipe: Add( GradedStamp( Shape=Crater, Levels=12, Ratio=1.41, Compose=Erase, Level=Constant 0 ), Multiply( FractalFBm( Octaves=4, Source=Simplex( Feature Scale=30 ) ), 0.04 ) ) with Output Min/Max set from the measured -0.76..0.47 range
presets.what: The crater-field relief: flat-floored rimmed craters with central peaks over a power law of smaller ones, fine regolith roughness. Fourteen stock nodes only reach rimless overlapping bowls.

presets.name: Spaghetti caves
presets.recipe: Min( TubeNoise( Mode=Network, Radius=0.12, Channel Source=Perlin( Feature Scale=70 ) ), Subtract( Multiply( FractalFBm( Octaves=3, Source=Simplex( Feature Scale=25 ) ), 0.15 ), Constant 0.85 ) ); carve where value < 0
presets.what: Round-section worm tunnels that meet in a network (the tube-noise vol) with wall roughness, for a voxel world. The classic abs+abs recipe beside it gives flanged ribbon sheets.

presets.name: Steered fingerprint / tiger stripes
presets.recipe: LatticePhasor( Frequency=1.5, Spread=0.15, Direction = DomainWarpSimplex( Warp Amplitude=40, Source=Gradient( Multiplier X=0.002 ) ) wrapped as an angle, or Direction = SteerablePerlin angle field ), Feature Scale=12
presets.what: Constant-contrast stripes with isolated Y forks following a smooth direction field; fingerprints, zebra, tiger. The cleanest stripe image of the stripes family.

presets.name: Stock agate (no new nodes)
presets.recipe: PingPong( Ping Pong Strength=9.5, Source=PowFloat( Pow=0.5, Value=Add( PowInt( Pow=2, Value=Perlin( Feature Scale=80 ) ), PowInt( Pow=2, Value=SeedOffset( Seed Offset=1, Source=DomainOffset( Offset X=37, Source=Perlin( Feature Scale=80 ) ) ) ) ) ) )
presets.what: Nested agate bands around the zero set of a 2-vector field; in 3D the isosurface is folded sheets. Entirely existing nodes, found while rivalling vortex-phase.

presets.name: Self-gated FBm plains with rough peaks (no new nodes)
presets.recipe: MaxSmooth( LHS=FractalFBm( Octaves=6, Gain=Remap( From Min=-0.3, From Max=1, To Min=0, To Max=0.75, Clamp Output=True, Source=Simplex( Feature Scale=S, same seed ) ), Source=Simplex( Feature Scale=S ) ), RHS=Constant -0.4, Smoothness=0.1 )
presets.what: Flat smooth lowland with roughness proportional to height, which is what FractalMultifractal promised; the Gain hybrid already does it, so the node is unnecessary.

presets.name: Gyroid sponge (no new nodes)
presets.recipe: Add( Add( T(x,y), T(y,z) ), T(z,x) ) where each T is SineWave( Feature Scale=S ) with RemoveDimension on the third axis and a DomainOffset of S*pi/2 on one axis to turn one sine into a cosine; optionally wrap in DomainWarpSimplex( Warp Amplitude=0.3*S )
presets.what: The exact gyroid, verified by the tubes critic through fnlab; warped it is the organic sponge that tpms-noise ships. Saves the seven-family TPMS enum.

presets.name: Penrose pavers
presets.recipe: QuasiTile( N=5, Output=Lookup at tile centre, Lookup=FractalFBm( Octaves=3, Source=Perlin( Feature Scale=200 ) ), Grout=0.04, Bevel=0.1 ), Feature Scale=40
presets.what: The quasi-tile relief: tumbled thick-and-thin rhomb blocks each at its own height, no straight runs, aperiodic. 2D/3D only; GenTileable2D will not tile it.

presets.name: Breaking river ice
presets.recipe: ShatterPlates( Levels=2, Tilt=0.3, Bevel=0.05, Soil=Multiply( Simplex( Feature Scale=60 ), 0.2 ) ) or, until that exists, HeightBlend( PlateDrift( Rotation=0.3, Drift=0.2, Gap=0.25 ), water Constant -0.2 )
presets.what: Rigid plates rotated against each other with opening wedge gaps and dark water showing in the cracks; the plate-drift thumbnail with the weak bevel replaced by a blend.

overrated: tile-domain unique 9: brick, herringbone, hex and fan paving are the standard tile-generator patterns of every material authoring tool; its value is usefulness and continuity, not novelty
cellular-edge-distance useful 8 / clean 9: exact Voronoi edge distance is a known technique (iq's Voronoi edges); the audit is good work but this is a correction of F2-F1, not a capability

chiral-wallpaper unique 9: domain folding into a fundamental region is the kaleidoscope trick; the exact chiral 17-group enumeration is the only new part, and outside p3/p31m/p6 the images are streaky brocade
dendry-noise unique 8: it is the published Dendry algorithm, and at 54x Perlin it is a bake node, not a FastNoise building block
crater-field look 8: it reads at once, but multiscale own-cell crater stamps are a standard planet-generator recipe and the single top size class shows
light-cone-ca clean 7 and the whole exactness effort: an impressive proof wrapped around an image available at a tenth of the cost
surface-probe useful 8: a slope mask is useful, but scoring a finite-difference utility beside look nodes inflates it; its best outputs are the step-law findings
coral-noise unique 9: capsule-union trees from a hashed lattice are a known SDF trick; the reef layout rescues it as a hero object only
quad-stamp port 9 and domain-warp-curl port 8: neither was ported or measured as a real node; port scores rest on estimates
stamp-scatter useful 8: honest as infrastructure, but on its own the images are dull and every stamp source still has to be written
underrated: lyapunov-stretch (look 7, clean 4): the overlapping-plate relief and combed-hair field are top-five images of the tournament and the stretch field of a shear chain is genuinely new maths for texture at 2.9x Perlin
stretch-ftle (port 3 sank it): curl-flow FTLE brain coral, the FTLE fingerprint cells and the basin-foam volume are among the strangest results here; expensive, but a showcase that deserves a 3D form
flow-strokes (merged into flow-shingle as shape=1): the strongest image in stamps and one of the ten best overall; it should headline the node
vortex-phase 3D (look 7, unique 5): the scroll/agate sheet volumes have no analogue on the existing sheet and the node is about 4 ns; the critics judged it on its zebra stripes
ripple-noise / radial-phasor amplitude net (showcase): the soft polygon interference web is the most unusual 2D cellular look in the set at an estimated 12 ns, cheaper than many keepers

NestedCaps (a discovery, never scored as an idea): owner-frame children at every level is a new mechanism that no graph can pass down; it beats the puffy-caps entry it mutated from and should be a node candidate
bubble-invert useful 4: a two-scale cellular (frogspawn, 3D sphere clusters) at 1.2 ns over the source is a bargain nobody else has
cellular-shape unique 6: per-cell rotated primitives and 14:1 needle rods inside the 3^D window fill a real gap; stock cellular is axis-locked
cumulus-noise port 3: the only lobes-on-a-parent-surface volume; the cost is real but the look is unreachable otherwise
cell-frame (promising): per-grain frames with a seam-free barycentric blend generalise nested-voronoi and the brushed-plate presets; rated below what the images show
fractal-slope-aligned Strata mode: detail organised along contours (flow marble wrapping hills) at 1.2x FBm is a new idea buried under a failed gullies mode
panel.comments:
Method: I read tournament.json in full (all 23 families, 117 idea ids, 180-odd discoveries), every family sheet and the discoveries sheet, plus 30 individual images where thumbnails were unclear. Images judged first, prose second. All numbers quoted are the prototypers' or critics' measurements from the JSON; I ran nothing and measured nothing.

What the set actually delivers: three or four things nobody else ships and that obey the execution model cleanly (erosion-filter's branching drainage, steerable per-lane grain, pointwise exact Penrose, pointwise caustic nets, a provably perfect maze, Hopf-Lax shocks), a dozen solid material and cellular nodes whose value is usability rather than novelty (tile-domain, graded-voronoi, grounded-scatter, stamp-scatter, tube-noise, crater-field, plate-drift, exchange-foam), and a long tail that is known tricks in new clothes. The known-trick list, to be scored on usability not novelty: lattice-phasor (Tricard phasor noise), wave-noise (Tricard wave noise), cyclic-noise (nimitz shadertoy), fractal-derivative (de Carpentier swiss/jordan, iq), tpms (gyroid), truchet, newton-basins, bubble-invert (sphere inversion), dendry (Gaillard), height-blend, pebble-pile (dead leaves), fault-lines (offset bands), fractal-multifractal (Musgrave), strata-terrace (Max(s,Terrace(s))), domain-warp-curl (Bridson), light-cone-ca.

Critics were right more often than prototypers; the recurring pattern is a prototyper claiming no graph can do it and a critic building the graph in 10-40 nodes at a fraction of the cost (strata-terrace, puffy-caps, nested-voronoi, cellular-planes, fault-lines, tpms, burgers stock scarps, contour-scarp). The stock recipes they produced are a real output of the tournament and several are presets above.

Obvious holes in the set: (1) No node exposes a derivative. Half the keepers (erosion, steerable, caustics, probes, iso-distance, crest, FoamBlend, DistFade) pay 3-5 source evaluations for finite differences; an analytic-gradient output on Perlin/Simplex, or a GradientSource interface, would halve the cost of the best results and is a bigger win than any single new node. (2) No filtering. Every hard-edged winner (pebble-pile, flow-shingle, plate-drift, tile-split, caustic lines, root-vein, crest-lines) aliases, and nothing takes a filter footprint; a hybrid Filter Width that box-filters the step/profile would make these shippable for real-time use. (3) Single-float output forces duplicate evaluation wherever a frame or winner value is wanted (DrainageFrame, foam winner plates, tile-local frames); the DomainWarp vector interface should be reusable by non-warp nodes. (4) 4D and tiling are missing from most direction-dependent keepers (steerable, erosion, flow-shingle, fisk, dendry), so GenTileable2D breaks; the torus-angle-wrapped lattice was tested once and should be a shared utility. (5) Nothing hydrological at scale: lakes and flat water fill failed (spill-level), rivers do not connect to the erosion gullies, and no node handles a drainage basin larger than its window. (6) No per-lane anisotropic cellular: cellular-shape rotates per cell and cell-frame per grain, but a Voronoi with a per-lane metric tensor (cells stretched along a field) is absent and is the natural companion to steerable-perlin. (7) Nobody treated the fourth dimension as time: only vortex-phase and ripple rain considered animation, yet looping noise is one of the most requested features in practice.

crossbreeds.name: PenroseShatter
crossbreeds.why: Shatter-bsp needs a Voronoi root only to be isotropic; a Penrose rhomb root is already isotropic, has exactly two tile shapes, and gives an aperiodic shattered paving (cracked Penrose floor, aperiodic broken glass) that neither parent makes. Also removes shatter-bsp's 3x3 Voronoi cost in 2D.
crossbreeds.algorithm: 1) Locate the rhomb containing p with the quasi-tile de Bruijn candidate loop (fixed count, N=5 default): get its integer index 5-tuple K, its two edge directions e_a, e_b and its lowest corner c. 2) h = hash(seed, K). 3) Express p in rhomb-local coords (u,v) = inverse of the 2x2 [e_a e_b] applied to p - c, so the rhomb is the unit square. 4) For level L = 1..Levels (int member): pick a cut line from bits of hash(h, L): a point q_L inside the current sub-cell and a direction with angle from the same hash; sub-cell for the next level = the side of q_L that p is on (bitmask select), tracked as an axis-aligned box in (u,v) exactly as shatter-bsp tracks its sub-cell centre. Cut distance d_L = |(p_uv - q_L) . n_L| masked by whether p projects inside the sub-cell segment. 5) Edge distance d_e = min(u, 1-u, v, 1-v) scaled by the rhomb heights (|e_a x e_b|) to world units. 6) Output: Crack = min(d_e, min over L of d_L * childWidthScale^L), LeafValue = rnd11(hash of final sub-cell id), TileType = thick/thin. All loops have a fixed count; no neighbour lookup beyond the quasi-tile candidate set. 3D: same with the rhombohedron candidate set and plane cuts.

crossbreeds.name: CurlSteeredGrain
crossbreeds.why: Steerable's per-lane angle is its whole value, and the downslope-flutes discovery already showed a gradient-of-Perlin direction works. Taking the direction from the curl of an analytic Perlin potential gives grain that follows closed streamlines (eddies, whorls, smoke) without any Euler stepping, at the price of one perlin-with-gradient evaluation. Different from warping steerable: the kernel stays undistorted so contrast stays even.
crossbreeds.algorithm: 1) psi, g = perlin gradient at p * PotentialScale (analytic derivative, as perlin2h provides). 2) direction d = (-g.y, g.x) normalised with a floor: d = (-g.y, g.x) * InvSqrt(|g|^2 + eps^2); where |g| is tiny the kernel falls back to the isotropic case automatically because the steerable kernel's anisotropy matrix is G = I + (Aspect-1) d d^T weighted by |g|/sqrt(|g|^2+eps^2). 3) Evaluate the steerable lattice kernel (2x2 corners in 2D, 2^D generally) with per-lane G exactly as steerable-perlin does, Octaves times with lacunarity; direction field shared across octaves. 4) Optional Steps int: before step 1, advance p by Steps small curl steps (the DomainWarpCurl loop) so the grain also folds; Steps=0 default. 5) Envelope normalise per octave (envn=1 discovery). 3D: d = curl of a 3-component Perlin potential, kernel anisotropy about the unit curl vector. Cost estimate: one perlin gradient (about 1.5x Perlin) plus steerable octaves; not measured.

crossbreeds.name: QuasiWeave
crossbreeds.why: Textile's weave is locked to two axis families and the level-set-weave discovery showed arbitrary A/B coordinates work. Multigrid already yields N line families with integer indices and fractional phases pointwise, so a 5- or 7-family over/under weave (quasiperiodic basketry, Penrose-like lattice work, kagome at N=3) falls out with no new search and no square repeat.
crossbreeds.algorithm: 1) For each family j in 0..N-1 (N an int member, fixed loop): t_j = e_j . p + gamma_j; k_j = Floor(t_j); f_j = t_j - k_j (phase across the strip). 2) Thread profile per family: s_j = ThreadProfile(|f_j - 0.5| / ThreadWidth) (round or smooth, as Textile). 3) Over/under rule: parity P_j = (sum over i != j of k_i + j) mod 2, computed with integer adds and an AND; height h_j = s_j * (P_j ? +1 : -1) * Select(s_j > 0). 4) At a crossing several threads overlap; output = thread with the largest (h_j + s_j*Bias) by a fixed max over the N families, which keeps the winner's own profile (no blending, same discontinuity class as Textile's weave). Soft output: smooth-max with Smoothness. 5) Tone output: hash(j, k_j) for per-thread colour. 3D: Textile's extrusion rule on the two nearest families only. Cost: O(N) adds and one profile each, no window; estimate under 2x Perlin at N=5 (unmeasured).

crossbreeds.name: FlowShockScales
crossbreeds.parents: burgers-steepen x flow-shingle (per-lane direction) x cellular F1 source
crossbreeds.why: The imbricate-scales discovery (Burgers on a Worley source) is the best scale texture in the set but has one fixed direction for the whole field. Flow-shingle's per-lane angle field is exactly the missing ingredient: scales whose sharp lips face downstream of a flow (fish skin round a body, pine cone spirals, roof tiles round a dome).
crossbreeds.algorithm: 1) theta = Angle hybrid source at p (constant or node), d = (cos theta, sin theta). 2) Hopf-Lax with locked root over K taps (K=13 int member) along d: for i in -K/2..K/2, q_i = p - d * (i * Time * TapSpacing), evaluate source u_i = CellularDistance F1 (or any Source) at q_i, candidate cost c_i = |q_i - p|^2 / (2 Time) + U_i where U_i is the trapezoid-integrated potential along the taps as the prototype does; pick the minimising i with the locked-root rule (prototype mode=7), all taps evaluated for every lane. 3) Output the source value at the chosen root, scaled; Viscous mode (mode=8) for a continuous version. 4) Because d varies per lane the tap line bends slightly between neighbours; keep Angle sources smooth (the same caveat flow-shingle already carries) and clamp Time so the shock reach stays under the Angle field's wavelength. 2D and 3D (d from a 3D angle pair). Cost: K source evaluations, so about 13x Cellular at K=13: a material node, flagged expensive.

crossbreeds.name: GradedCraters
crossbreeds.why: The crater field's one honest flaw is that the top level is one size class evenly spaced, and crater density on real bodies varies (maria versus highlands). Graded-voronoi's idea of a per-lane Level that fades whole lattice levels in and out transfers directly, because crater-field already loops over fixed levels with erasure ordering.
crossbreeds.algorithm: 1) lev = Level hybrid source at p (0..MaxLevels float). 2) For L = 0..MaxLevels-1 (fixed int loop, coarsest first): cell size s_L = Base * Ratio^-L; own-cell crater stamp exactly as crater-field (one hash per cell, occupancy bit, radius, bowl, rim, peak, confined to the cell). 3) Level weight w_L = smoothstep(lev - L + 1) * (1 - smoothstep(lev - L - Fade)) is NOT used to fade height (that would show as soft ghost craters); instead it scales the occupancy threshold per lane: a crater at level L exists if hashOcc < Occupancy * w_L, and to keep C0 the crater depth is multiplied by smoothstep((Occupancy * w_L - hashOcc) / Soft) so craters shrink to nothing as the local level passes them. 4) Erasure: young floors overwrite older ones by the same priority rule as crater-field (later level inside an earlier floor replaces height within the floor radius). 5) Output height in [-1,1] by the measured table. 3D: same with 3x3x3 own cells (crater cavities volume with graded pore size). Cost: same as crater-field plus one Level eval.

crossbreeds.name: NestedCraters
crossbreeds.why: NestedCaps was the strongest surprise in lobes: children living in the owner's frame never cross a parent boundary and scale with it. Applied to craters it gives small craters that sit on a big floor and scale with that floor, ejecta rays in the owner frame, and terraced walls, none of which the absolute-lattice crater field can do.
crossbreeds.algorithm: 1) Level 0: 3x3 own-cell crater search as crater-field; keep the owning crater's centre c0, radius r0, hash h0 (or no owner). 2) Transform p into owner frame: q = (p - c0) / r0 rotated by an angle from h0; seed1 = h0. 3) Level 1: run the own-cell crater stamp on q with cell size ChildScale (0.2..0.4) and seed1; child depth multiplied by a fade smoothstep((1 - |q|) / Rim) so children vanish at the parent rim, which keeps continuity across owner switches exactly as NestedCaps does. Lanes with no owner evaluate level 1 on the base lattice instead (Select). 4) Repeat for Levels (fixed int), each child becoming the owner for the next. 5) Combine: parent height + child height * ChildDepth^L; rays: optional term in the owner frame, Abs(sin(k * atan-approx(q))) * falloff(|q|), continuous because it is a function of q only. 6) Output range by measured table. 3D: own-cell in 3x3x3, child frame = scaled translation only. Cost about Levels x crater-field.

crossbreeds.name: BurgersFoldStrata
crossbreeds.why: Fault-lines gives offsets along straight traces; Burgers gives smooth ramps ending in sharp fronts. Applying the shock to a strata depth coordinate turns symmetric sinusoidal folds into asymmetric chevron and overturned folds with sharp limbs, the look of thrust belts in cross-section, which no node in the tectonic family produced.
crossbreeds.algorithm: 1) Depth coordinate u(p) = p.y + FoldAmp * B(p) where B is burgers-steepen on a 1-octave Perlin or Simplex source with direction d along x and Time t (locked root, K taps); t below breaking gives steepening limbs, above it sharp overturned fronts. 2) Layer index k = Floor(u / Thickness), fraction f = u/Thickness - k. 3) Output modes: Layers = rnd11(hash(seed, k)); Bands = Terrace-like profile of f; Hardness = per-layer hash gating a Burgers viscous mode (mode=8) so soft layers get soft fronts and hard layers sharp ones, by lerping between the viscous and locked outputs with the layer's hardness. 4) Optionally feed through fault-lines afterwards (position updated family by family) for faulted folds. 3D: d in the xz plane, u = y + FoldAmp * B(x,z). Cost: Burgers (K source evals) plus a hash; use K=9 for the strata case since the source is one octave.

crossbreeds.name: GrainedRegions
crossbreeds.why: Cell-frame gives per-grain brushed direction but with Voronoi grains; exchange-foam gives blob regions of varied size with enclaves. Steering the grain by the region's hashed angle, blended at borders by the pairwise distance weights from FoamBlend v2, gives metal grains, mineral thin-sections and brushed patchwork with soft isotropic borders, all region shapes instead of polygons.
crossbreeds.algorithm: 1) Evaluate K label fields s_k (exchange-foam, with the per-field offset so no lattice ties), K a fixed int. 2) Winner w = argmax s_k and runner-up by a fixed max network; border weights per label from FoamBlend v2: d_k = max_j (s_j - s_k) / |grad s_j - grad s_k| using the fields' analytic or 3-tap gradients, weight a_k = smoothstep(1 - d_k / Width). 3) Direction vector v = normalise(sum_k a_k * (cos th_k, sin th_k)) with th_k = hash angle of label k; where |sum| is near zero (opposite angles) fall back to isotropic by the same |v|-weighted anisotropy as CurlSteeredGrain. 4) Evaluate steerable-perlin octaves with direction v and Aspect; output grain, or Label, or grain + label tone. 5) Vector-blending angles means grain rotates smoothly through borders instead of popping. 3D: angle pairs per label, same blend. Cost: K label fields (about K x Perlin, with gradients K x 1.5) plus steerable octaves; K=4 default.

presets.name: Mossy brick wall
presets.recipe: HeightBlend(Source A = TileDomain(Pattern=Courses, Bevel=0.1, Profile=Smooth, Rotation=Random, Mortar=0.05) with its bevel as Height A, Source B = FractalFBm(Octaves=4, Source=Simplex(Feature Scale=18)) as moss with its own value as Height B, Depth=0.3)
presets.what: Moss fills the mortar first and reaches the brick tops last; Fade on the same pair only greys the wall. Verified side by side on the materials_combos sheet, c0ratio 7.3.

presets.name: Stained-glass fan mosaic
presets.recipe: DomainWarpSimplex(Feature Scale=140, Warp Amplitude=12, Source = TileDomain(Pattern=Fan, Output=TiltedHeight, Bevel=0.08, Mortar=0.04, Rotation=Random))
presets.what: Fan paving turns into leaded organic mosaic; edge distance survives the warp, c0ratio 8.0 measured, FFT loses the lattice cross. The best single material image from the tile node.

presets.name: Plains with rough peaks (no new node)
presets.recipe: MaxSmooth(LHS=FractalFBm(Octaves=6, Source=Simplex(Feature Scale=200), Gain=Remap(Source=Simplex(same seed, Feature Scale=200), From Min=-0.3, From Max=1, To Min=0, To Max=0.75, Clamp Output=True), Weighted Strength=0), RHS=-0.3, Smoothness=0.5)
presets.what: Gain follows the fractal's own first octave: flat smooth lowland floor with sharp rough peaks, top/bottom roughness 19.5 against Hetero's 14.1, 9.33 ns AVX2 2D, fnlab check 0 FAIL including tiling. Replaces FractalMultifractal entirely.

presets.name: Caprock mesas (no new node)
presets.recipe: S = Subtract(FractalFBm(Octaves=5, Source=Perlin(Feature Scale=178)), Gradient(Multiplier X=0.00026, Multiplier Y=0.0001)); Out = Add(Max(S, Terrace(Source=S, Step Count=1.8, Smoothness=0.05)), the same Gradient). Replace the Gradient with Perlin(Feature Scale=600)*0.5 for folded cliff bands.
presets.what: Flat-capped mesas, sheer cliffs, talus slopes and cliff-walled basins, identical in kind to the StrataTerrace default, 13.2 / 27.5 / 51.2 ns AVX2. Bigger Gradient gives cuestas and hogbacks.

presets.name: Spaghetti cave
presets.recipe: Threshold at 0 of Add(TubeNoise(Mode=Network, Channels=Perlin + value term, Radius=0.12, Output=Distance, Feature Scale=60), Multiply(FractalFBm(Octaves=3, Source=Simplex(Feature Scale=12)), 0.03))
presets.what: Round constant-section tunnel tangle, 90-95% connected, with lumpy walls of the same relief everywhere because the distance is in world units. The stock abs+abs noodle is flanged ribbons by comparison; the noodle graph Add(a*a, b*b) at iso 0.017 is the 9.3 ns fallback if TubeNoise is not built.

presets.name: Penrose terrace country
presets.recipe: Add(QuasiTile(N=5, Output=LookupCentre, Lookup Source=FractalFBm(Octaves=3, Source=Perlin(Feature Scale=400)), Grout=0.04, Bevel=0.05, Feature Scale=70), Multiply(FractalFBm(Octaves=4, Source=Simplex(Feature Scale=30)), 0.05))
presets.what: Stepped rhomb plateaus following a smooth field, every step a Penrose rhomb, with fine surface detail; c0ratio 7.9 grouted in the prototype. The most terrain-like image in the aperiodic family and impossible with CellularLookup.

presets.name: Jupiter bands
presets.recipe: DomainWarpFlow(Mode=Stir (angle 90), Steps=12, Amplitude=1.2, Potential = Add(DomainAxisScale(Scaling X=0.5, Scaling Y=2.5, Source=Perlin(Feature Scale=150)), Add(zonal jets = SineWave on Y via RemoveDimension(DomainOffset(Offset Y=Perlin*bend)), storms = Multiply(0.6, clamped Remap of CellularDistance(F1, Size Jitter=0.8, Feature Scale=300)))), Source = Gradient on Y with band tone)
presets.what: Bands roll up at their edges and wrap large spirals grown by the flow rather than stamped; large spiral on 5 of 6 seeds, holds at window 24. Needs the Flow node with a graph Potential; jets alone from stock nodes are 190 nodes at 53 ns.

presets.name: Combed hair / brushed metal
presets.recipe: SteerablePerlin(Octaves=4, Aspect=3, Angle = Multiply(Perlin(Feature Scale=500), 3.14159), Feature Scale=12) wrapped in FractalRidged for white strands; or the cheap version FiberNoise(Path=Streak, Layers=1, Spacing tight) inside DomainWarpFractalProgressive(Octaves=3, Warp Amplitude=40)
presets.what: Even combed grain with whorls and no lattice (c0ratio 7.99, 7.1x Perlin scalar at 4 octaves); the streak-plus-warp variant gives long dense flowing lines with swirl singularities at about 1x Perlin plus the warp. DomainRotate + DomainAxisScale + FBm only matches at one constant angle.

presets.name: Cracked mud with T-junctions
presets.recipe: CellularEdge(Levels=3, Edge Width = Multiply(0.05, smoothstep Remap of Simplex(Feature Scale=200)), Edge Depth=1, Colours=3, Feature Scale=40) with the tapered-tip hybrid width; stock fallback: Min(Mask(L0), DomainOffset(Source=Mask(L1), Offset X=CellularValue(same cells as L0, Output +-4000))) nested three levels
presets.what: Hierarchical cracks whose children stop at parents, tips that narrow as they fade, relief reads as dried mud; c0 by construction with hybrid width (measured 7.66-7.93). The stock T-junction graph ships today at 35 / 106 / 345 ns with fat F2-F1 wedges at parent walls.

presets.name: Agate from stock nodes
presets.recipe: PingPong(Ping Pong Strength=9.5, Source=PowFloat(Pow=0.5, Value=Add(PowInt(Pow=2, Value=A), PowInt(Pow=2, Value=B)))) with A = Perlin(Feature Scale=120), B = DomainOffset(Offset X=37, Source=SeedOffset(1, Perlin(Feature Scale=120)))
presets.what: Nested folded bands like agate in 2D and 3D at 4.57 / 7.53 / 12.37 ns AVX2, the stock cousin of the vortex-phase scroll sheets; bands are thicker with a few polygon corners. Swap A and B for two offset CellularDistance F1 fields into a Textile with A/B sources to get the woven Worley rings.

presets.name: Trabecular bone scaffold
presets.recipe: GiniFoam(Relative=1, Grid Jitter=0.7, Pressure=0.1, Smoothness=0.25, Output=Participation) isosurface at 0.47 (fnlab vol --iso 0.47); for a sponge today: negated Max of four scaled SignedSquareRoot(Max(CellularDistance Euclidean Squared, 0)) layers, 21 / 57 / 181 ns
presets.what: Webbed strut network with fins at the nodes that stock F3-F1 cannot give (it yields straight faceted rods). The strongest argument for the foam mode and a ready-made bone, coral or sponge volume.

presets.name: Dune sea from stock nodes
presets.recipe: Two CellularDistance F1 cones from the same seed, Feature Scale=110, Size Jitter=0.3: Max(0, 0.1 - Cell(p)) - 1.6 * Max(0, -0.3 - Cell(p offset)), lit as sand in relief (tree)
presets.what: A faceted dune sea with sharp crests and shaded lee faces over 2 seeds, 12.6 ns AVX2, fnlab check 0 FAIL. Honest limits: circular disc creases and planar faces; the barchan node is the showcase version at 20 ns.

overrated: bond-tunnels: keeper and ship, but the volume is a nearly solid cube with pinholes and the 2D is a smudge. Its connectivity numbers are real, but they do not make a picture.
tpms-noise: keeper, ship. 2D is blobs, and the 3D is a warped gyroid close to a stock graph the tubes critic verified.
lattice-phasor: unique 8. By eye it is a kinked worm labyrinth that vortex-phase beats for less work. Constant width is real, but it is not a thrilling result.
multigrid-noise: keeper, ship. Next to quasi-tile it is a noisy triangle mosaic with a spiky repetitive relief. Valuable mainly if it really is cheap, and its speed is unported.
fractal-derivative: keeper, ship. A decent look that the erosion filter overtakes.
wave-noise-sliced: keeper. Egg-crate blobs.
simplex-facet: unique 7 is high for a 60-degree quilt in 2D. The 3D cut crystal is the real asset, and cellular-facet-mesh has the better 2D.
underrated: coral-noise: look 6 for literal coral branching off a plate. Should be near the top on look, cost aside.
growth-age: look 6 for real wood with knots and a stunning block volume.
fisk-meanders: look 7. Its port score is fair, but the map-like image is among the best here.
barchan-field: look 7. The sand render is nearly photographic at a glance.
glacial-troughs: unique 3 and look 6, but its relief is one of the most believable landscapes in the set. Keep at least as a preset.
fern-fold: look 5 for the best frost-fern thumb in the rivers family.
fractal-slope-aligned: look 5.5, though the feathered hills are unforgettable.
radial-phasor: useful 4 and buried as a mode. The amplitude net is a top-tier 2D image.
level-set-weave: buried as a mode, yet woven Worley rings are the best image in materials after the fan mosaic.
quad-stamp: look 6, but the 3D block cascade is excellent.
domain-warp-sine: unique 3 is right, but look 6 is low; I cannot separate it from shear-flow by eye.
eikonal-stripes: clean 2 is fair because it jumps, but as a hard zebra map it looks great.
panel.comments:
Coverage. I read all 24 sheets. The sheets contain 11 ideas with no image of their own (their folders hold only critic files): dislocation-stripes, defect-stripes, steered-band-noise, radial-phasor, phase-vortex, cellular-fracture, boulder-field-3d, occlusion-stack, flow-strokes, hilbert-curve-noise, streak-scatter. For radial-phasor, flow-strokes, defect-stripes, boulder-field-3d, cellular-fracture and streak-scatter I judged the related discovery image. For steered-band-noise, phase-vortex, hilbert-curve-noise and occlusion-stack the score rests on critic text only, and dislocation-stripes rests on the vortex-phase thumb, so treat all five as weak. eikonal-stripes and phacelle-noise are also absent from the sheets; I judged them from folder and discovery images.

What is verified and what is not. None of the 9 crossbreeds was built, so their looks are predictions and their costs are estimates. Among the presets, I rendered only Breccia and Fibrous Bark, on base.dll, and benched only Breccia. Caprock and Dune Sea use stock trees rendered by critics. The other six use unbuilt nodes with proposed parameter names; Mars and Hoodoo Caves have never been rendered in any form. Other ns and ratio figures come from the tournament data and I did not re-measure them. Almost every new node is a scalar prototype, so most AVX2 figures are estimates, as the data marks them. I judged scalar prototype images, not shipping nodes.

Taste calls. My front page puts knot-field and coral-noise high on look, but both are objects rather than fields, and coral is 63x Perlin scalar. Their place in my must-have list is a creative coder's bias, so a library maintainer should discount it. Runners-up for the front page: spanning-maze vol, strata-terrace vol, vortex agate vol, gini-foam trabecular, crater-field relief, warped fan mosaic.

Best breeding stock. tile-domain, stamp-scatter, cellular-edge-distance and any steering hybrid. The most useful finding from this pass, though unproven in code, is that a shear chain's J*v0 is a direction field with no singular points, which could feed every steered node.

Obvious holes.
1. There is no shared direction or gradient channel. Erosion, steerable, flow-shingle, fiber, surface-probe and warp-flow each solve gradients or direction privately, because node output is one float. This is the largest structural gap, and it should come before many of these nodes.
2. Tiling and animation are barely served. Several entries have no 4D form or a costly one, the stripes critic says stripes lose constant width on the 4D torus, and nothing in the set was designed for z or w as time apart from caustic depth and barchan.
3. Water surfaces are missing. The set has pool-floor light but no sharp-crested ocean height.
4. Missing looks: spotted coats and rosettes, wispy rather than cauliflower cloud volumes, and affordable 3D branching (only coral, at 63x).
5. Thin-line nodes have no footprint-aware width. Caustics, crests, dendry and growth rings show spikes or aliasing in relief and fine detail. I cannot always separate renderer stepping from the field in the moire patches seen in some volumes.

Data caution. The voronoi critic showed that ContinuityProbe at its default origin cannot see seams on integer lattice lines, and suspects this affects other families. It tested only its own family. So a c0ratio of 8 in tournament.json is not proof of no seams for lattice nodes outside that family. Also, status and call disagree in places, such as newton-basins and fractal-multifractal, which are keepers with a drop or graph-recipe call. Read the call, not the status.

crossbreeds.name: ShearFrame + InkStrokes
crossbreeds.parents: lyapunov-stretch x flow-strokes x steerable-perlin / fiber-noise
crossbreeds.why: Lyapunov streaks and the flow-strokes curl are the two best 2D images, and every steered node needs a direction field. Gradient fields have cores. Each shear has det J = 1, so J*v0 can never vanish: this direction field has no singular points in any dimension. Limit: it cannot make whorls, only bends. Not built; the look is a prediction.
crossbreeds.algorithm: p = pos; v = v0 (fixed per seed). For k in 0..N-1 (int member, same for all lanes): s = dot(p, d[k]) * f[k] + off[k]; n, dn = 1D noise and derivative at s; p += a[k] * n * perp[k]; v += a[k] * f[k] * dn * dot(v, d[k]) * perp[k]; v *= InvSqrt(dot(v, v)). perp[k] must be orthogonal to d[k], using the perpendicular pairs table. Output A: Angle, from fastAtan2 of v; the wrap is harmless to consumers that take sin and cos. Output B: strokes at the original pos in the flow-shingle window (16 candidates in 2D, 27 in 3D). For each candidate r = pos - site; u = dot(r, v); w2 = dot(r, r) - u*u; capsule mask from u and w2, so 3D needs no full frame; bristles from sin of w * B; keep the highest hashed priority with Select. 4D: Angle output only, since 81 candidates is too much. Estimated AVX2 2D: 17-19 ns (critic estimates: about 10 for 8 chain steps, 7-9 for the stroke window).

crossbreeds.name: ContourEngrave
crossbreeds.parents: iso-distance x strata-bands x surface-probe x lattice-phasor Pulse output
crossbreeds.why: strata-bands has crowded contours and iso-distance has constant width only at one level. This gives constant world-width lines at every level, with width driven by hillshade: banknote engraving of any field. Cheap, no window, no hash. Not built; the look is a prediction.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Tap Source at pos and pos + h*e_i (D+1 taps): H, g = forward difference gradient. m = Sqrt(dot(g,g) + k*k), k a floor for flats. t = H * Levels + Offset. tri = Abs(t - Round(t)), a continuous triangle wave. d = tri / (Levels * m), the first-order world distance to the nearest contour. tone = sat(0.5 + 0.5 * dot(normalize(-g, 1), Light)) from the same taps. w = WidthMin + (WidthMax - WidthMin) * (1 - tone). out = 1 - 2 * smoothstep(w, w + Soft, d). Works unchanged in 2D, 3D (onion shells) and 4D (5 taps, tiles if Source does). Estimated cost: (D+1) * Source + about 1 ns, so about 19 ns AVX2 2D on a 5 octave FBm (estimate).

crossbreeds.name: QuasiDomain (Penrose parquet)
crossbreeds.why: The nested hex herringbone discovery shows tiles-inside-tiles working, and quasi-tile has the best layout in the set. Exposing each rhomb's local coordinates lets twill, boards or strokes run along its edges: a Penrose parquet floor. Not built; the look is a prediction.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Locate the rhomb exactly as QuasiTile does: N=5 gives 10 family pairs x 4 candidates = 40 fixed tests, all evaluated, selected with masks. Winner has pair (j,k) and integer indices. Solve pos = o + u*e_j + v*e_k with a precomputed 2x2 inverse per pair, giving (u,v) in [0,1]. edge = min(u, 1-u, v, 1-v) * edgeScale[j,k]. val = Source.Gen(seed ^ tilehash * PerTile, u*S, v*S) once per lane, with S from a per-pair table. out = lerp(Mortar, val, smoothstep(0, Bevel, edge)), so the jump between rhombs is hidden under mortar and output stays continuous. 3D: 6 families with a 3x3 inverse table per triple; the candidate count grows, so it is hero only there. Cost: critic measured 433 ns scalar (8.2x perlin2) for the locate alone. AVX2 unknown; no port exists.

crossbreeds.name: GrainStripes
crossbreeds.parents: exchange-foam x vortex-phase / lattice-phasor x cell-frame
crossbreeds.why: lattice-phasor shows square cuts where orientation changes, and exchange-foam has beautiful curved walls with no lattice. Giving each foam region its own stripe direction should give a polycrystal zebra with curved grain boundaries. Not built; the look is a prediction.
crossbreeds.algorithm: For k in 0..K-1 (fixed int): v[k] = Source.Gen(seed + k*Stride, pos). Track top1, top2 and label idx with Max and Select. dir = table[idx], phi = table2[idx], both per node arrays computed when a param is set. Stripe mode: c = cos(tau * f * dot(dir, pos) + phi + W * top1); W bends stripes along the region's own field. Contour mode: c = cos(tau * f * G * top1 + phi), which uses no raw coordinates, so it can tile through 4D if Source does. g = smoothstep(0, Gap, top1 - top2). out = c * g. Output is 0 on both sides of every wall, so it is continuous by construction. Estimated AVX2 with K=5 Perlin: about 8 / 14 / 26 ns (critic estimate for the foam plus about 1.5 ns, unverified).

crossbreeds.name: Thunderegg
crossbreeds.parents: cellular-edge-distance x strata-bands x simplex-facet, with the poster agate discovery
crossbreeds.why: Poster agate bands follow noise; real agate bands follow the cavity wall. CellularEdge gives exact wall distance cheaply, so bands should wrap each cell with a crystal core. My stock breccia preset is the neighbour, and it costs far more. Not built; the look is a prediction.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Run the CellularEdge pass in the 3x3 / 3x3x3 / 3x3x3x3 window (Grid Jitter <= 0.40 for exactness): e = exact wall distance, h1 = winner hash. q = e * BandFreq + Wobble * Perlin(pos) + rnd(mix(h1,1)). i = Floor(q), fr = q - i. tone = hash of (i ^ h1) via bit fields. seam = smoothstep(0, SeamW, min(fr, 1-fr)). band = tone * seam. core = smoothstep(Rc, Rc + Eps, e). crystal = SimplexFacet Flat(pos) seeded with h1. out = lerp(band, crystal, core) * smoothstep(0, Grout, e), so grout hides the cell jump. Band labels are hard inside a cell, softened only by the seam. 3D slices give nested shells for free. Estimated AVX2: 8 / 19 / 56 ns, against measured 62 / 196 / 293 for the breccia graph.

crossbreeds.name: GlassCaustic
crossbreeds.why: The caustic back-map is only used on smooth noise. Fed a bevelled tile height it should give light through glass bricks or a Penrose skylight: rounded bright rims and cusps per tile. Not built; the look is a prediction, and tile joints may need a softer profile.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Height is any GeneratorSource, TileDomain with Output Bevel and Smooth profile as the default. y = pos. For s in 0..Steps-1 (fixed, 2-3): g = forward difference gradient of Source at y (D+1 taps); y += Lambda * (pos - Depth * g - y). Then Hessian H of Source at y by fixed stencil (6 taps in 2D, 10 in 3D, 15 in 4D). b = 1 / (Eps + Abs(det(I - Depth * H))). out = ScaleOutput(b ^ Gamma). The FD step h sets line softness on tile joints. Total taps at Steps=2: 12 / 18 / 25. Depth is hybrid, so a z-driven Depth animates the light. Estimated AVX2 on TileDomain: about 15 ns 2D. On QuasiTile the 433 ns scalar locate x 12 taps is about 5 us: bake only.

crossbreeds.name: AndamentoMosaic
crossbreeds.parents: flow-shingle x cellular-edge-distance x tile-domain Fan
crossbreeds.why: The warped fan mosaic is gorgeous, but warping changes tile sizes. A per-lane metric keeps tile size constant and aligns tiles to a field. Honest limit: sites are jittered, so expect flow-aligned pebbles rather than true coursed rows, since rows need a stream function a pointwise node cannot integrate. Not built; the look is a prediction.
crossbreeds.algorithm: theta = Angle.Gen(seed, pos), one eval per lane. c, s from sincos. M(pos) = diag(1/a, 1/b) * R(theta), aspect a/b capped at 2. For each of 4x4 candidates (2D): site = cell + jitter(hash); y[i] = M * (site - pos); d2[i] = dot(y[i], y[i]); keep nearest y1, h1 via Select. Second loop over the same stored y[i]: n = y[i] - y1; e = 0.5 * (d2[i] - d2_1) * InvSqrt(dot(n,n)); edge = min(edge, e) excluding the winner by mask. out = rnd(h1) * smoothstep(Grout, Grout + Bevel, edge). M is continuous in pos when Angle is, so F1 and edge stay continuous and the walls stay closed. 3D: stretch only along the field vector, y = r - (1 - 1/a) * dot(r,v) * v, 27 candidates. Window seams at max aspect must be tested with the critic's bisection scan. Estimated AVX2 2D: 10-12 ns.

crossbreeds.name: SandSea
crossbreeds.parents: barchan-field x dunes on vortex phase x steerable-perlin per-lane direction
crossbreeds.why: Critics list one stamped profile and straight ripples as barchan tells. The vortex-phase dunes discovery has clean Y forks, and a wind hybrid lets the whole field bend together. Not built; the look is a prediction.
crossbreeds.algorithm: theta = Wind.Gen(seed, pos), low frequency, per lane. w = (cos, sin). For 3x3 cells: centre = cell + jitter, r = lerp(rmin, rmax, hash), gated by a density hash. u = dot(pos - centre, w); v = dot(pos - centre, perp(w)); u2 = u + Horn * v*v / r. h = barchan profile(u2, v, r) with the existing stoss and slip kernel. Hash also jitters Horn and stoss per dune to break the stamped look. H = smooth union over the fixed 9 candidates. Ripple: phase = tau * f * dot(pos, w) + q * arg(A + iB) with A, B two Perlins and polynomial atan2. rip = RipAmp * (0.5 + 0.5*cos(phase)) * (1 - sat(H / H0)). out = Base + H + rip. 3D as density: y - out. Critic measured 20-22 ns AVX2 for barchan with its own ripple; this adds 3 Perlin and one sincos: about 25-27 ns (estimate).

crossbreeds.name: MeanderDelta
crossbreeds.why: Dendry trees are straight-limbed and Fisk has meanders but no tributaries. Width-preserving Kinoshita offsets per segment give a sinuous tree where big rivers wander and twigs stay straight. Honest limit: a function graph cannot double back, so no omega loops or oxbows; only Fisk gets those. Not built; the look is a prediction. Bake node.
crossbreeds.algorithm: Inside Dendry's fixed-window segment loop, per level and candidate segment (a,b): t = clamp(dot(pos-a, b-a) / L2); n = signed perpendicular distance; s = t * L. y = A[level] * (sin(k*s + ph) + J * sin(3*k*s + ph3)) * Sqrt(sin(pi*t)), taking phases from the segment hash. The taper is 0 at both ends, so joints stay connected. dy = derivative of y with respect to s. d = Abs(n - y) * InvSqrt(1 + dy*dy), first-order width correction. Feed d into the existing min and width logic in place of the segment distance. A[level] grows with river order. Adds one or two sincos per candidate. Critic estimate for Dendry is 60-100 ns AVX2 2D at 4 levels; expect 10-30 ns more (estimate).

presets.name: Breccia (stock nodes, usable today)
presets.recipe: Multiply(LHS=DomainOffset(Source=Subtract(LHS=Multiply(LHS=Add(LHS=AddDimension(New Dimension Position=Multiply(LHS=Perlin(Feature Scale=170), RHS=100), Source=DomainAxisScale(Scaling X=0, Scaling Y=0, Source=CellularValue(Feature Scale=12.5))), RHS=1.2), RHS=Min(LHS=Multiply(LHS=Abs(Source=AddDimension(New Dimension Position=Multiply(LHS=Perlin(Feature Scale=170), RHS=100), Source=DomainAxisScale(Scaling X=0, Scaling Y=0, Source=CellularDistance(Feature Scale=12.5, Distance Index 0=0, Distance Index 1=1, Return Type=Index0Sub1)))), RHS=6), RHS=1)), RHS=1.2), Offset X=CellularValue(Feature Scale=70, Grid Jitter=0.9, Output Min=-900, Output Max=900)), RHS=Remap(Source=CellularDistance(Feature Scale=70, Grid Jitter=0.9, Distance Index 0=1, Distance Index 1=0, Return Type=Index0Sub1, Output Min=0, Output Max=1), From Min=0, From Max=0.05, To Min=0, To Max=1, Clamp Output=True))
