round2.intro:
# Round 2 seeds

The panel proposed 50 crossbreeds and 71 presets. Merging proposals that use the same mechanism leaves 38 crossbreeds and 35 presets (10 of them work today from stock nodes).

**No crossbreed has been built.** Every crossbreed look is a panel prediction and every crossbreed cost is an estimate. Preset status says what has really been rendered. Full `why` and `algorithm` text for each proposal is in `panel.json` under its lens.

The crossbreeds assume the planned nodes exist, but each smallest test below runs on scalar prototypes and needs no port.

crossbreeds.text:
**GradedStamp** (maintainer, parents: graded-voronoi x stamp-scatter x crater-field / bubble-pack). graded-voronoi proved that grading feature size by a hybrid Level across space works without seams; crater-field and bubble-pack are own-cell multi-level stamps with a fixed size spectrum. Breeding them gives craters, vesicles or texture islands whose size follows a map (big craters on highlands, pumice that gets finer towards a rim) in one node.

Algorithm: Sample Level L(p) once at the lane position. For k = 0..Levels-1 (fixed int loop): scale s_k = ratio^k; cell c_k = Floor(p * s_k); h = hash(seed + k, c_k); centre = (c_k + 0.5 + jitter(h) * 0.5 * (1 - 2 r_k)) / s_k with radius r_k = rmin + bits(h) * (rmax - rmin) so the stamp never leaves its own cell (one hash per level, no window). Profile f = Shape(|p - centre| * s_k / r_k) from {Crater, Dome, Disc, Source sampled in the stamp frame}. Level weight a_k = SmoothStep(L(p) - (k - Levels/2) * Spacing, Width) * density gate from spare bits. Compose with the cascade fade from stamp-scatter: out = Lerp(out, f, inside_k * a_k) in youngest-last order (Erase) or Max or Sum via a 3-value enum. Because a_k depends on L(p) at the sample and not at the cell, a stamp fades in as a whole across its own footprint: no pop. Cost about 1 hash + 1 profile per level + 1 Level eval, dimension agnostic (estimate).

**GradedCraters** (researcher, parents: crater-field x graded-voronoi (per-lane Level)). The crater field's one honest flaw is that the top level is one size class evenly spaced, and crater density on real bodies varies (maria versus highlands). Graded-voronoi's idea of a per-lane Level that fades whole lattice levels in and out transfers directly, because crater-field already loops over fixed levels with erasure ordering.

Algorithm: 1) lev = Level hybrid source at p (0..MaxLevels float). 2) For L = 0..MaxLevels-1 (fixed int loop, coarsest first): cell size s_L = Base * Ratio^-L; own-cell crater stamp exactly as crater-field (one hash per cell, occupancy bit, radius, bowl, rim, peak, confined to the cell). 3) Level weight w_L = smoothstep(lev - L + 1) * (1 - smoothstep(lev - L - Fade)) is NOT used to fade height (that would show as soft ghost craters); instead it scales the occupancy threshold per lane: a crater at level L exists if hashOcc < Occupancy * w_L, and to keep C0 the crater depth is multiplied by smoothstep((Occupancy * w_L - hashOcc) / Soft) so craters shrink to nothing as the local level passes them. 4) Erasure: young floors overwrite older ones by the same priority rule as crater-field (later level inside an earlier floor replaces height within the floor radius). 5) Output height in [-1,1] by the measured table. 3D: same with 3x3x3 own cells (crater cavities volume with graded pore size). Cost: same as crater-field plus one Level eval.

**SortedSediment** (material, parents: pebble-pile, graded-voronoi, stamp-scatter (density sampled at the centre)). Riverbeds and scree are sorted by size, and every ground material needs that. PebblePile has size layers but no spatial sorting; GradedVoronoi has seam-free size control but makes cells rather than stones. Not built, look unverified.

Algorithm: Level is a hybrid source in [0,1], with 0 for boulders and 1 for sand. Constant loop over layers i=0..L-1: s_i = s0*g^i in a per-layer rotated and offset frame q. ix = floor(q/s_i); h = hash(ix, seed+i); centre c = (ix + 0.5 + jit*bits(h))*s_i; radius r = s_i*lerp(rmin, rmax, bits(h)), with jit and rmax bounded so a stone fits its own cell and no neighbour window is needed. Evaluate Level once per layer at the stone centre rotated back to world, so the map never slices a stone. keep = bump(|i/L - Level(c)|, width); r = r*keep, so stones shrink out instead of popping, and hash bits < keep decide presence. dome = sqrt(Max(0, r^2 - |p-c|^2)) or a parabola. Height = Max over layers. Output enum Height, StoneValue (Select of the winner's hash), LayerIndex. Same rim slope issue as PebblePile with sqrt; the parabola profile is smoother. Any dimension. Cost ESTIMATE from PebblePile's 1.5-2 ns per layer plus 1.1 ns for a Perlin Level: about 20-25 ns at 8 layers in 2D.

Gap: density and size that follow a map: planets, riverbeds. Risk: own-cell cap on top size stays. **Smallest test:** Add a Level hybrid to the crater proto with stamp-scatter's cascade fade; ramp test for pop.

**CraterGullies** (terrain, parents: crater-field x erosion-filter). Crater walls in the relief are smooth; real crater rims are dissected by radial gullies. The erosion filter already proves the steer-by-gradient kernel; the crater profile is closed form so its gradient is free, no finite differences.

Algorithm: Per lane: evaluate CraterField levels as today but accumulate (h, dh/dx, dh/dy) analytically per level (bowl, rim and peak are polynomials of r, so grad = f'(r) * (p - c)/r, masked by the same erase rule). Slope mask m = smoothstep(s0, s1, |grad|). Then run 2 octaves of the erosion filter's 3x3 triangular stripe kernel with direction = grad/|grad| and amplitude a*m, exactly as erosion-filter does on its Perlin base, and return h - stripes. Fixed loop counts (levels, 2 octaves), one hash per lattice point, 3x3 window per octave. Cost estimate: crater (~16 ns 2D est.) + 2 x ~8 ns = ~32 ns 2D; 3D/4D by the same window rule. Tiles via the torus-angle trick the erosion family already built.

Gap: planet surfaces; Old Eroded Planet and Mars presets want the same thing. Risk: rim gradient spikes may break stripes. Also proposed as an untested preset by 2 other lenses. **Smallest test:** Run the erosion proto on the crater proto as Source; look at relief first.

**FlowCellular** (maintainer, parents: steerable-perlin x cellular-edge-distance x cell-frame). steerable-perlin showed that a per-lane hybrid direction turns an isotropic primitive into a flow-aligned one at modest cost, and cell-frame showed per-grain streaks are wanted but cost 3-4 source evals. Stretching the cellular metric by one direction eval gives elongated flow-aligned cells (wood rays, muscle fibre, flowstone, ice) with F1 / F2-F1 / exact edge outputs for about one extra source eval.

Algorithm: Evaluate hybrid Direction once at the lane position: angle theta (2D) or unit vector u (3D, from a vector-valued hybrid or a DomainWarp-style triple). Build M = R diag(1, 1/Aspect, 1/Aspect) R^T once per lane (Aspect >= 1, contraction only, so the 3^D window bound of the unchanged jitter lattice still holds). Run the ordinary cellular window search with d = |M (p - site)| for every candidate; keep the bisector pass for the exact inset under the same metric (d1j = (Fj^2 - F1^2) / (2 |M (sj - s1)|)). Outputs F1, F2-F1, EdgeDistance, CellValue. Since M is the same for all candidates in a lane and theta is continuous, F1 and F2 remain continuous; discontinuity in Direction is the user's. Cost = CellularDistance + 1 Direction eval + D^2 multiply-adds per candidate (estimate 1.2x Cellular plus the direction source).

**AndamentoMosaic** (creative, parents: flow-shingle x cellular-edge-distance x tile-domain Fan). The warped fan mosaic is gorgeous, but warping changes tile sizes. A per-lane metric keeps tile size constant and aligns tiles to a field. Honest limit: sites are jittered, so expect flow-aligned pebbles rather than true coursed rows, since rows need a stream function a pointwise node cannot integrate. Not built; the look is a prediction.

Algorithm: theta = Angle.Gen(seed, pos), one eval per lane. c, s from sincos. M(pos) = diag(1/a, 1/b) * R(theta), aspect a/b capped at 2. For each of 4x4 candidates (2D): site = cell + jitter(hash); y[i] = M * (site - pos); d2[i] = dot(y[i], y[i]); keep nearest y1, h1 via Select. Second loop over the same stored y[i]: n = y[i] - y1; e = 0.5 * (d2[i] - d2_1) * InvSqrt(dot(n,n)); edge = min(edge, e) excluding the winner by mask. out = rnd(h1) * smoothstep(Grout, Grout + Bevel, edge). M is continuous in pos when Angle is, so F1 and edge stay continuous and the walls stay closed. 3D: stretch only along the field vector, y = r - (1 - 1/a) * dot(r,v) * v, 27 candidates. Window seams at max aspect must be tested with the critic's bisection scan. Estimated AVX2 2D: 10-12 ns.

Gap: researcher lens hole 6: per-lane anisotropic cellular. Risk: window seams at high aspect; true coursed rows impossible. **Smallest test:** Per-lane metric in the edge proto, aspect 2, jump scan.

**SurfaceFlutes (3D erosion)** (voxel, parents: erosion-filter + steerable-perlin (Sheets) + surface-probe + wide-stencil FD discovery). The biggest hole for a voxel world: every terrain winner is a heightfield, and raw erosion in 3D is vertical extrusion. This puts downhill flutes on any isosurface, including overhangs and cave walls. Not built or rendered: untested idea.

Algorithm: Density S, solid above 0. Tetra jet: 4 Source taps at stencil h near the flute wavelength, exact-step divisor. g = grad S, n = g*InvSqrt(g.g), t = down - n*dot(n,down), L = |t|, surface distance s = S*InvSqrt(g.g). Thin direction b = normalize(cross(n,t)). Fixed loop over O octaves (default 2): run one steerable-perlin octave in Sheets topology with d = b, using G v = e1 v + (e0-e1)(d.v)d per corner; sign of d does not matter because d appears twice. Take a ridged value and analytic gradient from the same corner sum. Add that gradient to g scaled by the octave amplitude, then recompute t and b for the next octave: that is the erosion filter's branching rule. Output S + Strength * smoothstep(Band,0,|s|) * smoothstep(0.1,0.4,L) * sum(gain^i * v_i). The L term fades flat tops and ceilings, where t is undefined, so it stays C0 there. Cost estimate: 4*Source + 2*2.89 ns (hand kernel, 3D) + about 1 ns; about 30 ns on a 3-octave Perlin density. No per-lane early out, so the engine should run it only in surface-band chunks. 4D steerable has a timing kernel only. Risk: 3D sheet aspect is about 3.3, so flutes may read short.

**FlutedCave** (material, parents: erosion-filter (stripe kernel), tube-noise, strata-caverns). The erosion filter transforms terrain but nobody ran it on a volume in my images. Flutes running down cave walls and flowstone would make noise caves look geological. Not built, look unverified.

Algorithm: s0 = Density(p), plus D forward differences for g (4 evals in 3D). n = g*InvSqrt(dot(g,g) + eps). With gravity axis a: t = a - dot(a,n)*n; tl = |t|; b = cross(t,n)/Max(tl,eps), the across-slope axis. Constant octave loop (2): 3x3x3 cell window; for each cell, hash gives jittered point c_j; w_j = Max(0, 1 - |p-c_j|^2/R^2)^3, with R inside the window reach; psi_j = f*dot(p-c_j, b); Z += w_j*(cos psi_j, sin psi_j). stripe = Re(Z)/sqrt(|Z|^2 + eps). out = s0 + A*saturate(tl/0.3)*saturate(|g|*k)*stripe. The tl mask removes flutes on floors and ceilings, where direction is undefined. 2D reduces to the ordinary ErosionFilter path. 4D's 81 cells are not affordable, so 4D drops w and does not tile. Cost ESTIMATE from the reported stripe kernel of about 8.1 ns per octave on 9 cells: about 24 ns per octave on 27 cells, so about 50 ns plus 4 Density evals. Risk: gradient noise on rough density shreds b, so it needs a smooth input.

Gap: voxel lens hole B: every terrain winner is a heightfield. Risk: sheet aspect caps near 3.3; rough density shreds the frame. **Smallest test:** Flutes on a smooth Perlin isosurface, vol, before any cost work.

**CellDomain** (voxel, parents: cellular-edge-distance + plate-drift + nested-voronoi + tile-domain per-tile frame + NestedCracks + facet shatter). Half the striking discoveries are the same thing: evaluate a child in the frame of the owning cell, hide the jump in a grout line. NestedCracks, terrazzo, facet shatter and plate-of-plates each got their own code or a large graph. One node makes them all short graphs. It does not reproduce plate-drift's wedge gaps, because cell outlines do not rotate. Not built: untested idea.

Algorithm: 3^D window pass keeping rel[i], hash[i], F1 site and hash h. Bisector pass as cellular-edge-distance: e = min over j of dot(.5*(rel[j]+rel1), n)*InvSqrt(n.n), with Grid Jitter capped at the audited value. Frame q = R(h)*(p - site)*Scale + Offset(h), with R a table rotation in 2D or a hash-derived Householder in 3D/4D, no trig. v = Source.Gen( seed ^ h, q ), one eval with a per-lane seed. Optional tilt: v += dot(tilt(h), rel1). Output Lerp( Grout, v, smoothstep(0,W,e) ), with W a hybrid. At e = 0 both sides return Grout, so it is C0 whatever v does. Nesting is a Source that is another CellDomain; child jumps vanish under the parent grout. Cost estimate: 5.5/16/50 ns plus one Source per level (edge pass figure from the tournament), any dimension.

**ShatterLookup** (material, parents: shatter-bsp, plate-drift (Lookup mode)). Turns any node into a broken version: cracked mirror, smashed tile, fractured marble slab. PlateDrift gives Voronoi plates, but no node gives straight BSP shards with a rigid offset per leaf. Not built, look unverified.

Algorithm: Same edge pass and constant BSP loop as ShatterBSP, tracking d = Min over levels of e_l/W_l, leaf id and leaf centre c. theta = MaxRot*rnd11(mix(id,1)); shift = Drift*(rnd11(mix(id,2)), rnd11(mix(id,3))). p' = c + R(theta)*(p-c) + shift. In 3D, rotate in one plane picked by id bits using Select. v = Source(p'), exactly one eval per lane. out = lerp(GapValue, v, smoothstep(0,1,d)). Source jumps between shards, but every leaf boundary has d = 0, so out equals GapValue there and the result is continuous. Optional Throw adds a hash height per leaf for stepped relief, multiplied by the same smoothstep so it stays continuous. Works in any dimension the window affords. Cost ESTIMATE: ShatterBSP about 7 / 18 ns in 2D / 3D plus Source. Risk: with a mid-gray gap, shards read as grouted tile rather than glass.

Gap: makes nested cracks, terrazzo and facet shatter short graphs. Risk: a mid-gray gap may read as grout, not glass. **Smallest test:** Evaluate a source in the owner frame under a grout mask, nested once.

**WalkableWorms** (voxel, parents: tube-noise (Network) + strata-caverns). Tube-noise has the best cave section here and strata-caverns has the only floors you can walk on. A round worm tangle is a fall-through hazard in a voxel game. TubeNoise already computes the offset vector to the axis, so a flat floor costs almost nothing. Not built or rendered: untested idea.

Algorithm: One Perlin lattice visit as in TubeNoise: channels n0,n1,n2 with gradients g0,g1,g2 and the per-vertex value term. Apply a fixed Y squash sy (about 0.4) to the input, and multiply g.y by sy by chain rule so results are in world units. For each of the 3 fixed channel pairs: A = J J^T + Damping*I (2x2), lambda = A^-1 n, r = J^T lambda, the first-order vector from curve to sample. Keep the r with min |r| using Select. sd = SmoothMax( |r| - R, -r.y - F*R, k ), giving a round roof and a flat floor F*R below the axis. Steep axes have r perpendicular to the axis, so r.y stays near 0 and the floor does not cut: shafts stay round. Output Clamp( sd / R ). No window, no per-lane control flow. 4D uses the same algebra with a 4 component r. Cost estimate: network 5-7.5 ns 3D (tournament estimate) plus about 0.3 ns. Inherits the flat lens flakes.

**BeddingTubes** (maintainer, parents: tube-noise x strata-caverns x bedding warp (networks discovery)). tube-noise gives round worm tunnels but no stratigraphy; strata-caverns gives flat-floored galleries but is a graph recipe. Tubes constrained to bedding planes give limestone-style galleries that run laterally along layers and connect through short cross-cuts, which is the actual look of karst.

Algorithm: Two channels as in tube-noise Network mode: n0 = Perlin(seed, x, y, z) and n1 = Saw(y' / Thickness) - 0.5 where y' = y + Dip.x * x + Dip.y * z + Fold * Perlin(seed+1, x * ff, z * ff) (the bedding warp) and Saw is a sawtooth with hashed per-layer thickness from Floor(y'/Thickness). Tube distance d = sqrt(n0^2 + n1^2) / sqrt(|grad n0|^2 |grad n1|^2 - (grad n0 . grad n1)^2)^(1/2) exactly as tube-noise estimates distance to the intersection curve, with the gradients from the derivative Perlin kernel and the analytic saw gradient. Output 1 - d / Radius. Add a third channel n2 = Perlin(seed+2) and take the Min over pairs (tube-noise Network rule) for cross-cuts between layers. Cost about tube-noise Network plus one cheap analytic channel (estimate 5-8 ns 3D).

Gap: walkable floors on round tunnels. Risk: inherits lens flakes; floor cut may clip junctions. **Smallest test:** One SmoothMax term on the tube offset vector in the proto, vol at 2 seeds.

**GrainedRegions** (researcher, parents: exchange-foam x steerable-perlin (DistFade border weights)). Cell-frame gives per-grain brushed direction but with Voronoi grains; exchange-foam gives blob regions of varied size with enclaves. Steering the grain by the region's hashed angle, blended at borders by the pairwise distance weights from FoamBlend v2, gives metal grains, mineral thin-sections and brushed patchwork with soft isotropic borders, all region shapes instead of polygons.

Algorithm: 1) Evaluate K label fields s_k (exchange-foam, with the per-field offset so no lattice ties), K a fixed int. 2) Winner w = argmax s_k and runner-up by a fixed max network; border weights per label from FoamBlend v2: d_k = max_j (s_j - s_k) / |grad s_j - grad s_k| using the fields' analytic or 3-tap gradients, weight a_k = smoothstep(1 - d_k / Width). 3) Direction vector v = normalise(sum_k a_k * (cos th_k, sin th_k)) with th_k = hash angle of label k; where |sum| is near zero (opposite angles) fall back to isotropic by the same |v|-weighted anisotropy as CurlSteeredGrain. 4) Evaluate steerable-perlin octaves with direction v and Aspect; output grain, or Label, or grain + label tone. 5) Vector-blending angles means grain rotates smoothly through borders instead of popping. 3D: angle pairs per label, same blend. Cost: K label fields (about K x Perlin, with gradients K x 1.5) plus steerable octaves; K=4 default.

**GrainStripes** (creative, parents: exchange-foam x vortex-phase / lattice-phasor x cell-frame). lattice-phasor shows square cuts where orientation changes, and exchange-foam has beautiful curved walls with no lattice. Giving each foam region its own stripe direction should give a polycrystal zebra with curved grain boundaries. Not built; the look is a prediction.

Algorithm: For k in 0..K-1 (fixed int): v[k] = Source.Gen(seed + k*Stride, pos). Track top1, top2 and label idx with Max and Select. dir = table[idx], phi = table2[idx], both per node arrays computed when a param is set. Stripe mode: c = cos(tau * f * dot(dir, pos) + phi + W * top1); W bends stripes along the region's own field. Contour mode: c = cos(tau * f * G * top1 + phi), which uses no raw coordinates, so it can tile through 4D if Source does. g = smoothstep(0, Gap, top1 - top2). out = c * g. Output is 0 on both sides of every wall, so it is continuous by construction. Estimated AVX2 with K=5 Perlin: about 8 / 14 / 26 ns (critic estimate for the foam plus about 1.5 ns, unverified).

Gap: polycrystal looks with curved walls. Risk: gap at walls may read as cells. **Smallest test:** GrainStripes contour mode from the foam proto: output 0 on both sides of every wall.

**SteeredTube** (terrain, parents: tube-noise x steerable-perlin). Tube-noise worms are isotropic; lava tubes, roots and burrows follow a field (down-slope, down gravity, along bedding). Steerable-perlin proves an elliptical per-lane kernel costs little and needs no window.

Algorithm: Per lane: direction unit vector u from a hybrid Direction input (constant, source, or gradient of a source via 3 taps). Build the per-lane metric G = I + (aniso - 1) u u^T. Evaluate the two (Network: three) tube channels n_i as steerable-perlin octaves: at each of the 2^D corners the kernel offset is G (p - corner), with the per-vertex value term from tube-noise so channels do not share zeros. Distance d = sqrt(sum n_i^2) / max(|grad n|, eps) using the analytic corner gradients steerable-perlin already carries, then tube-noise's radius/network logic unchanged. Single lattice visit per channel, no window, 2D/3D/4D by the GenT path. Cost estimate: tube-noise cost x ~1.3 for the metric multiply, plus the Direction eval.

Gap: lava tubes and roots that follow a field. Risk: metric may break the distance estimate. **Smallest test:** Metric on the corner offsets of the tube proto.

**CurlSteeredGrain** (researcher, parents: steerable-perlin x domain-warp-curl (analytic potential)). Steerable's per-lane angle is its whole value, and the downslope-flutes discovery already showed a gradient-of-Perlin direction works. Taking the direction from the curl of an analytic Perlin potential gives grain that follows closed streamlines (eddies, whorls, smoke) without any Euler stepping, at the price of one perlin-with-gradient evaluation. Different from warping steerable: the kernel stays undistorted so contrast stays even.

Algorithm: 1) psi, g = perlin gradient at p * PotentialScale (analytic derivative, as perlin2h provides). 2) direction d = (-g.y, g.x) normalised with a floor: d = (-g.y, g.x) * InvSqrt(|g|^2 + eps^2); where |g| is tiny the kernel falls back to the isotropic case automatically because the steerable kernel's anisotropy matrix is G = I + (Aspect-1) d d^T weighted by |g|/sqrt(|g|^2+eps^2). 3) Evaluate the steerable lattice kernel (2x2 corners in 2D, 2^D generally) with per-lane G exactly as steerable-perlin does, Octaves times with lacunarity; direction field shared across octaves. 4) Optional Steps int: before step 1, advance p by Steps small curl steps (the DomainWarpCurl loop) so the grain also folds; Steps=0 default. 5) Envelope normalise per octave (envn=1 discovery). 3D: d = curl of a 3-component Perlin potential, kernel anisotropy about the unit curl vector. Cost estimate: one perlin gradient (about 1.5x Perlin) plus steerable octaves; not measured.

Gap: whorled grain without Euler steps. Risk: singular points need the fallback. **Smallest test:** Direction from the curl of one Perlin in the steerable proto.

**CellularScaffold** (maintainer, parents: cellular-edge-distance x tube-noise x gini-foam (trabecular iso discovery)). The gini-foam trabecular vol and the tube-noise worms show that struts along Voronoi edges are a wanted 3D look (bone, coral rock, Plateau borders) and that round sections beat ribbons. Nothing gives distance to the Voronoi edge skeleton; the exact bisector pass already has everything needed.

Algorithm: Standard 3^D cellular search keeping the three (3D: four) nearest sites s1..s3 and distances F1..F3. From the bisector pass compute exact inset to each neighbour: d1j = (Fj^2 - F1^2) / (2 |sj - s1|) for j = 2,3. Edge distance e = sqrt(d12^2 + d13^2) (3D: distance to the line where three cells meet; 2D: distance to the Voronoi vertex, so expose Mode {Edges, Vertices}). Output = 1 - Min(e / Radius, 1) scaled to [-1,1]; hybrid Radius. All terms are continuous functions of continuous F's, fixed loop, no extra hashes; cost about 1.4x CellularDistance by the critic's per-site op count (estimate). Threshold at 0 gives a connected strut network; Radius from a Level source gives bone that thins with height.

Gap: round struts along Voronoi edges: bone, coral rock. Risk: 2D output is vertex distance only. **Smallest test:** Edge distance from the stored window, vol at iso 0.

**PlateShatter** (terrain, parents: plate-drift x shatter-bsp). Plate-drift gives rigid rotated plates but their surface is flat; shatter-bsp gives T-junction cracks but on a fixed Voronoi. Cracks that turn with their plate are what breaking river ice and tempered glass look like, and the hierarchical-shatter discovery shows nesting plate-drift works but was too noisy.

Algorithm: Per lane: plate-drift's 3x3 window finds the owning plate id k, its rotation R_k and translation t_k (hashed), and the gap distance g. Transform q = R_k^T (p - c_k - t_k). In plate space run shatter-bsp with seed = hash(k): levels L (fixed int), each level a hashed line through the sub-cell centre, distance d_l clipped at the parent cut as shatter-bsp already does; crack = min_l(d_l / w_l). Output = min(g / gapWidth, crack) for a mask, or plate TiltedHeight minus crackDepth * profile(crack). All lookups are per-lane hashes, no neighbour state; window stays 3x3 (3x3x3 in 3D). Cost estimate: plate-drift (~3x Cellular) + ~0.5 ns per level.

**ShatterPlates** (maintainer, parents: plate-drift x cellular-edge-distance (Levels) x cellular-planes x height-blend). plate-drift's tilted rigid plates were its strong image and its bevel mask the weak one; CellularEdge with Levels gives exact T-junction shards; height-blend fills gaps with a second material so features interlock. Together: broken flagstone / tumbled slate with soil in the cracks, in one pass.

Algorithm: Run CellularEdge with Levels = ShatterBSP cuts to get shard id h, shard anchor a (site, or parent site plus cut index) and exact inset e. Per shard from h: lift l in [-1,1], tilt vector t with |t| <= Tilt, so plate height H = l + Dot(t, p - a), clamped to the shard by the inset band: H_plate = Lerp(soil, H, SmoothStep(e / Bevel)). Then HeightBlend(H_plate, Soil(p), HeightA = H_plate + Bias, HeightB = Soil(p), Softness) where Soil is any Source: soil fills where it is higher than the plate top, plate corners poke through. All pointwise: one cellular edge pass, one source eval, no sort. Cost about 1.5x CellularDistance + Source (estimate).

Risk: hierarchical-shatter discovery was too noisy. **Smallest test:** Cracks in the plate frame at levels 2.

**InvertedStamp (Apollonian craters)** (maintainer, parents: bubble-invert x crater-field x stamp-scatter). bubble-invert is a 1-3 ns domain modifier with a proven Lipschitz bound, and its frogspawn image shows inversion turns any cellular source into nested clusters. Fed with craters or bubbles it gives craters inside craters and vesicle clusters inside vesicles, a nesting look the own-cell stamps cannot make with a fixed size ladder.

Algorithm: Level-0 own-cell sphere per lane: c = cell centre + jitter, radius r, confined to its cell. q = p - c, rho2 = Max(q.q, (eps r)^2). If rho2 < r^2: p' = c + q * r^2 / rho2 (inversion), else p' = p (identity outside the sphere; continuous at the rim since the map is identity there). Repeat for Iterations (fixed int, 1 or 2) with the next finer own-cell lattice. Evaluate the stamp family (GradedStamp or any Source) at p'. The map's Lipschitz constant is 1/eps^Iterations as bubble-invert measured, so the output stays continuous with a known slope bound. Cost 1-3 ns per iteration plus the stamp (estimate from the bubble-invert AVX2 port).

**NestedCraters** (researcher, parents: NestedCaps local-frame discovery x crater-field). NestedCaps was the strongest surprise in lobes: children living in the owner's frame never cross a parent boundary and scale with it. Applied to craters it gives small craters that sit on a big floor and scale with that floor, ejecta rays in the owner frame, and terraced walls, none of which the absolute-lattice crater field can do.

Algorithm: 1) Level 0: 3x3 own-cell crater search as crater-field; keep the owning crater's centre c0, radius r0, hash h0 (or no owner). 2) Transform p into owner frame: q = (p - c0) / r0 rotated by an angle from h0; seed1 = h0. 3) Level 1: run the own-cell crater stamp on q with cell size ChildScale (0.2..0.4) and seed1; child depth multiplied by a fade smoothstep((1 - |q|) / Rim) so children vanish at the parent rim, which keeps continuity across owner switches exactly as NestedCaps does. Lanes with no owner evaluate level 1 on the base lattice instead (Select). 4) Repeat for Levels (fixed int), each child becoming the owner for the next. 5) Combine: parent height + child height * ChildDepth^L; rays: optional term in the owner frame, Abs(sin(k * atan-approx(q))) * falloff(|q|), continuous because it is a function of q only. 6) Output range by measured table. 3D: own-cell in 3x3x3, child frame = scaled translation only. Cost about Levels x crater-field.

Risk: Levels x crater cost; aliasing at cores. **Smallest test:** Compare the two routes on one seed in the crater proto.

**GrowingCracks** (material, parents: cellular-edge-distance, shatter-bsp, edge-fate-cells (tapered tip form)). A crack mask driven by a wear map, or animated by a moving front: parents open first, children follow, tips taper. Materials want cracks where the damage is, and VFX wants them spreading. Not built, look unverified.

Gap: cracks driven by wear; VFX. Risk: walls never move: a reveal, not growth. **Smallest test:** Damage hybrid on the merged proto; animate a moving front.

**GeodeField** (voxel, parents: bubble-pack + crater-field own-cell kernel + strata-bands). True spheres are exact distance fields, so banded shells get constant thickness. Each geode needs its own band sequence, which a Terrace on a distance output cannot give. Own-cell kernel means no window. Not built: untested idea.

**Thunderegg** (creative, parents: cellular-edge-distance x strata-bands x simplex-facet, with the poster agate discovery). Poster agate bands follow noise; real agate bands follow the cavity wall. CellularEdge gives exact wall distance cheaply, so bands should wrap each cell with a crystal core. My stock breccia preset is the neighbour, and it costs far more. Not built; the look is a prediction.

Risk: bands are hard inside a cell. **Smallest test:** Bands by exact wall distance in the edge proto.

**GlassCaustic** (creative, parents: caustic-web x tile-domain (or quasi-tile)). The caustic back-map is only used on smooth noise. Fed a bevelled tile height it should give light through glass bricks or a Penrose skylight: rounded bright rims and cusps per tile. Not built; the look is a prediction, and tile joints may need a softer profile.

Risk: tile joints may need a softer profile. **Smallest test:** Back map on a smooth-bevel tile height.

**MoonBase** (terrain, parents: crater-field x grounded-scatter x stamp-scatter). Crater relief has no ejecta; real craters are ringed by boulder fields that thin with distance from the rim. Grounded-scatter already attaches stones to a Height source; the only new part is a density that depends on the rim mask, which stamp-scatter's cascade fade keeps pop-free.

Gap: ejecta boulders. Risk: about 150-200 ns estimate. **Smallest test:** Rim mask at candidate centres in the grounded proto.

**HeightFoam** (material, parents: exchange-foam, height-blend, biome-blend (FoamBlend v2)). Up to four ground materials competing in foam-shaped regions, with borders that follow the stones and cracks instead of fading across them. ExchangeFoam has the regions and HeightBlend has the border, but the graph needs many nested nodes. Not built, look unverified.

**FoamBlend** (maintainer, parents: exchange-foam x height-blend x FoamBlend v2 (regions discovery)). exchange-foam gives the best region labels, height-blend gives the best material transition, and biome-blend failed because its borders were cell-scale scallops. Combining label margin with height-driven blending gives biome transitions where pebbles stay whole and sand fills first, from the K evals already paid.

Gap: biome borders that follow the stones. Risk: nested HeightBlends with Margin may already do it. **Smallest test:** Build the nested stock-plus-proto graph first; only then the node.

**SupplyDunes** (voxel, parents: vortex-phase dunes + barchan-field + cole-hopf-dunes). Barchan is one stamped dune at 20-22 ns measured and never merges; vortex dunes merge but are only transverse. A sand supply hybrid could run one field from isolated dunes to continuous ridges at a quarter of the cost. Whether horns form is unknown, so test this before believing it.

**SandSea** (creative, parents: barchan-field x dunes on vortex phase x steerable-perlin per-lane direction). Critics list one stamped profile and straight ripples as barchan tells. The vortex-phase dunes discovery has clean Y forks, and a wind hybrid lets the whole field bend together. Not built; the look is a prediction.

Risk: whether horns form is unknown. **Smallest test:** Clip the vortex dune by a Supply hybrid; look for crescents.

**QuasiDomain (Penrose parquet)** (creative, parents: quasi-tile x tile-domain x textile). The nested hex herringbone discovery shows tiles-inside-tiles working, and quasi-tile has the best layout in the set. Exposing each rhomb's local coordinates lets twill, boards or strokes run along its edges: a Penrose parquet floor. Not built; the look is a prediction.

Risk: 433 ns scalar locate, 3D hero only. **Smallest test:** Expose rhomb (u,v) in the quasi proto, feed twill.

**ShearFrame + InkStrokes** (creative, parents: lyapunov-stretch x flow-strokes x steerable-perlin / fiber-noise). Lyapunov streaks and the flow-strokes curl are the two best 2D images, and every steered node needs a direction field. Gradient fields have cores. Each shear has det J = 1, so J*v0 can never vanish: this direction field has no singular points in any dimension. Limit: it cannot make whorls, only bends. Not built; the look is a prediction.

Gap: a direction field with no singular points, usable by every steered node. Risk: bends only, no whorls. **Smallest test:** Output the J*v0 angle from the Lyapunov proto and feed flow-shingle's Angle.

**ChoppyOcean** (material, parents: caustic-web (back map), burgers-steepen (root of the same Lagrangian map), wave-noise-sliced (plane-wave table)). The set has the light under water but no water. One map gives height, whitecap mask and caustic from the same waves, so they line up, and Time is a hybrid input. Not built, look unverified.

Gap: no water surface anywhere; queue gap too. Risk: fixed point may change branch at high Chop. **Smallest test:** Scalar back map on 16 waves; check continuity at rising Chop; judge in motion.

**StrainLines** (material, parents: lyapunov-stretch (tangent propagation), shear-flow, cellular-edge-distance). Warped line work goes fat and thin with stretch, and that is how warped cells give themselves away. Carrying the Jacobian through the warp keeps line width constant in world units: craquelure, stretched hide, even marble veins. A graph cannot do this because nodes cannot pass a Jacobian. Not built, look unverified.

Gap: even line width through warps. Risk: first order breaks at high strain. **Smallest test:** Carry M through 3 shears in the edge proto.

**QuickShatter** (voxel, parents: Simplex-window Voronoi discovery + simplex-facet PL warp + shatter-bsp). The 3D and 4D price of cracks is the main barrier for shatter in volumes. Simplex-window uses 6/8/10 sites against 9/27/81, but its cells drift toward honeycomb in 3D. A PL warp breaks that regularity with no search. Not built or rendered: untested combination.

Gap: the 3D/4D price of cracks; depends on the Simplex-window question. Risk: near-honeycomb cells in 3D; clamped masks only. **Smallest test:** PL warp in front of the t_critic2_nested simplex root; 3D vol.

**FoamWalls** (voxel, parents: exchange-foam + FoamBlend v2 + iso-distance + cellular-edge-distance). Cracks around non-convex organic plates with constant world-space width. Voronoi cannot do non-convex; Foam Margin blurs where the top two fields run parallel. Analytic gradients avoid FoamBlend's 3N evaluations. Not built: untested idea.

Gap: constant-width cracks around non-convex plates. Risk: specks at saddles near ties. **Smallest test:** Analytic gradients per field; min over all pairs.

**PenroseShatter** (researcher, parents: quasi-tile x shatter-bsp). Shatter-bsp needs a Voronoi root only to be isotropic; a Penrose rhomb root is already isotropic, has exactly two tile shapes, and gives an aperiodic shattered paving (cracked Penrose floor, aperiodic broken glass) that neither parent makes. Also removes shatter-bsp's 3x3 Voronoi cost in 2D.

Risk: cost of quasi-tile plus levels. **Smallest test:** BSP cuts in rhomb coords in the quasi proto.

**RippleOverlay** (terrain, parents: lattice-phasor (hex kernel) x surface-probe gradient x transverse-dunes profile). Sand ripples and wind-blown snow run perpendicular to the local slope-and-wind direction; the phasor family showed steered stripes are clean on the hex kernel at 4.3 ns, and the dune profile gives the stoss/slip asymmetry. Nothing lets a graph steer stripes by its own terrain today.

Gap: stripes steered by your own terrain. Risk: walled domains above about F2.5. **Smallest test:** Hex phasor steered by a base gradient at spread .15.

**ScreeShingle** (terrain, parents: flow-shingle x surface-probe (gradient) x grounded-scatter (chisel stamp)). Flow-shingle stacks oriented overlapping stamps along a field; scree and talus are exactly that: angular stones imbricated down a slope. The field is the terrain gradient and the stamp is the chisel-rubble silhouette, both already prototyped.

Gap: imbricated talus. Risk: hard edges; 3 + 9 H taps. **Smallest test:** Shingle proto with gradient of an FBm as Angle.

**JointBlocks** (voxel, parents: fault-lines + multigrid-noise + cellular-planes + jointed strata discovery). Real cliff faces are blocks bounded by long joint sets with small offsets. Fault-lines gives offsets with no grout, Multigrid gives cheap regions and exact plane distance, neither gives blocks. No window, cost flat in dimension, and a 4D form that survives tiling better than graphs using DomainRotate. Not built: untested idea.

Gap: cliff blocks bounded by joints, flat with dimension. Risk: long straight runs (86.8 units measured on multigrid N=7). **Smallest test:** Fixed loop of families with a grout mask; warp afterwards.

**GroundedCrystals** (voxel, parents: grounded-scatter + chisel-rubble + cellular-shape needle rods + simplex-facet look). Faceted crystal outcrops rooted on terrain, with no placement pass. Crystal clusters are a staple voxel request and no graph can rotate per-instance prisms. Not built: untested idea.

Gap: crystal clusters on terrain. Risk: 60-65 ns estimate, surface band only. **Smallest test:** Swap the stamp in the grounded proto for a hex prism.

**SlabField** (terrain, parents: cellular-planes x cell-frame). Cellular-planes gives tilted plates with soft fault ramps; cell-frame gives per-cell rotated grain. Tilted sedimentary slabs whose bedding grain turns with each slab is tumbled-slate and flagstone terrain, and the two share one window pass.

Gap: tumbled slate with per-slab grain. Risk: 4-5 source evals. **Smallest test:** Tilted plane plus a grained source in the cell-frame proto.

**BurgersFoldStrata** (researcher, parents: burgers-steepen x fault-lines (strata depth coordinate)). Fault-lines gives offsets along straight traces; Burgers gives smooth ramps ending in sharp fronts. Applying the shock to a strata depth coordinate turns symmetric sinusoidal folds into asymmetric chevron and overturned folds with sharp limbs, the look of thrust belts in cross-section, which no node in the tectonic family produced.

Risk: untested; K source evals. **Smallest test:** Depth coordinate through the burgers proto, strata source.

**ContourEngrave** (creative, parents: iso-distance x strata-bands x surface-probe x lattice-phasor Pulse output). strata-bands has crowded contours and iso-distance has constant width only at one level. This gives constant world-width lines at every level, with width driven by hillshade: banknote engraving of any field. Cheap, no window, no hash. Not built; the look is a prediction.

Gap: banknote engraving of any field; constant world-width contours. Risk: specks at critical points. **Smallest test:** D+1 taps in the iso proto; width driven by hillshade.

**QuasiWeave** (researcher, parents: multigrid-noise x textile). Textile's weave is locked to two axis families and the level-set-weave discovery showed arbitrary A/B coordinates work. Multigrid already yields N line families with integer indices and fractional phases pointwise, so a 5- or 7-family over/under weave (quasiperiodic basketry, Penrose-like lattice work, kagome at N=3) falls out with no new search and no square repeat.

Risk: crossings of many families may read as a mess. **Smallest test:** Parity rule over N=5 in the multigrid proto.

**LeakStreaks** (material, parents: surface-probe, streak-scatter, flow-network (one-way direction)). Rain runs and rust trails below ledges are on every wall I texture, and the set has no gravity-driven weathering. Not built, look unverified.

Gap: material lens hole 3: no gravity-driven weathering. Risk: thin ledges missed; Up has no meaning through the torus. **Smallest test:** 12 taps on a TileDomain proto edge output.

**MeanderDelta** (creative, parents: dendry-noise x fisk-meanders). Dendry trees are straight-limbed and Fisk has meanders but no tributaries. Width-preserving Kinoshita offsets per segment give a sinuous tree where big rivers wander and twigs stay straight. Honest limit: a function graph cannot double back, so no omega loops or oxbows; only Fisk gets those. Not built; the look is a prediction. Bake node.

Gap: sinuous river trees. Risk: bake only; no omega loops possible. **Smallest test:** Offsets per segment in the dendry proto.

**FlowShockScales** (researcher, parents: burgers-steepen x flow-shingle (per-lane direction) x cellular F1 source). The imbricate-scales discovery (Burgers on a Worley source) is the best scale texture in the set but has one fixed direction for the whole field. Flow-shingle's per-lane angle field is exactly the missing ingredient: scales whose sharp lips face downstream of a flow (fish skin round a body, pine cone spirals, roof tiles round a dome).

Risk: 13x Cellular at K=13; tap line bends. **Smallest test:** Angle hybrid in the burgers proto over a Worley source.

**CliffBands** (terrain, parents: contour-scarp x strata-terrace x surface-probe (the stacked-scarp-bands discovery, made a node)). Terrace makes risers whose plan width varies with slope; the probes family showed a signed distance s/|grad s| gives risers of constant plan width, and strata showed stacked caprock bands read as cuesta country. Neither family shipped it as a node.

Gap: constant-width risers. Risk: the stock mesa preset competes; critic says the distance barely shows. **Smallest test:** Compare against Caprock Mesas at the same seed before anything else.

**HorizonProbe** (material, parents: surface-probe, spill-level (its ray fan)). Cavity and occlusion drive dirt, moss and wear on every material. Slope and hillshade exist, occlusion does not. Spill-level's fan failed at finding lakes but is the right shape for this. Not built, look unverified.

Gap: material lens hole 3: no occlusion or cavity. Risk: bake cost: 17 evals; star artifacts. **Smallest test:** Fan in the probe proto over a 3-octave FBm.

presets.name: Caprock Mesas
presets.body:
Proposed as: Mesa Country (stock) (terrain), Caprock Mesas (stock today) (material), Caprock mesas (no new node) (researcher), Caprock Mesas (stock nodes, usable today) (creative).

**Recipe:** `S = Subtract(FractalFBm(Octaves=5, Source=Perlin(Feature Scale=178)), Gradient(Multiplier X=0.00026, Y=0.0001)); out = Add(Max(S, Terrace(S, Step Count=1.8, Smoothness=0.05)), the same Gradient). Larger Gradient = cuestas and hogbacks; a Perlin in the Gradient slot = folded cliff bands`

**Gives:** Flat-capped mesas, buttes, sheer cliffs and talus slopes from four stock nodes, measured 13.2 / 27.5 / 51.2 ns AVX2 2D/3D/4D by the strata critic. Reproduces the whole StrataTerrace default.

**Status:** Rendered by the strata critic on 2 seeds; viewed by the panel. **Cost:** 13.2 / 27.5 / 51.2 ns AVX2 measured.

presets.tree:
Plain gyroid from existing nodes (period 2 world units, verified in fnlab vol + bench: AVX2 3.86 / 3.69 / 4.87 ns 2D/3D/4D):
Add(LHS=Add(LHS=RemoveDimension(Remove Dimension=Z, Source=DomainOffset(Offset Y=0.5, Source=SineWave(Feature Scale=0.3183))), RHS=RemoveDimension(Remove Dimension=X, Source=DomainOffset(Offset Y=0.5, Source=SineWave(Feature Scale=0.3183)))), RHS=RemoveDimension(Remove Dimension=Y, Source=DomainOffset(Offset X=0.5, Source=SineWave(Feature Scale=0.3183))))
SineWave is sin(x/S)*sin(y/S)[*sin(z/S)], so Feature Scale S = period/(2 pi) and the pi/2 phase is an offset of S*pi/2 = 0.5 world units. Wrap in DomainWarpGradient / DomainWarpFractalProgressive for the warped sponge.

**Recipe:** `labels = ExchangeFoam(K=5, Source=Perlin(Feature Scale=900) per field with the per-field offset on, Weighted shares via the Gumbel table); blend width = FoamBlend v2 pairwise distance (s_j - s_k)/|grad s_j - grad s_k| from 3 taps per field; detail density per biome = GradedVoronoi(Level=labels)`

**Gives:** A planet biome partition with islands, enclaves and any-to-any borders (no 4-label pinwheels), a constant world-space blend width (cv 0.05 measured for FoamBlend v2) and cell density that follows the biome. The pieces exist; only the K-field label compare needs a node.

**Status:** Foam labels and FoamBlend v2 rendered separately; the stack is not rendered. **Cost:** Exchange foam K x source. **Needs:** ExchangeFoam, GradedVoronoi.

presets.body:
Proposed as: Penrose terrace country (researcher), Penrose pavers (maintainer).

**Recipe:** `Add(QuasiTile(N=5, Output=LookupCentre, Lookup Source=FractalFBm(Octaves=3, Source=Perlin(Feature Scale=400)), Grout=0.04, Bevel=0.05, Feature Scale=70), Multiply(FractalFBm(Octaves=4, Source=Simplex(Feature Scale=30)), 0.05))`

**Recipe:** `SteerablePerlin(Octaves=4, Aspect=3, Angle = Multiply(Perlin(Feature Scale=500), 3.14159), Feature Scale=12) wrapped in FractalRidged for white strands; or the cheap version FiberNoise(Path=Streak, Layers=1, Spacing tight) inside DomainWarpFractalProgressive(Octaves=3, Warp Amplitude=40)`

preset_notes: These need no new code. They should ship as preset graphs whatever happens to the node plan.

plan.honesty: No node here has a FastSIMD port. Measured numbers are hand-written AVX2 harnesses, scalar prototypes, or stock-node graphs through fnlab, as labelled per node. Every other cost is an estimate.
plan.honesty_note: The plan wrote this before any node was ported. Since then BurgersSteepen, CausticWeb, CellFrame, CellularEdge, CellularSmooth, ChiralWallpaper, DendryNoise, DomainInvert, DomainMap, DomainTwist, DomainWarpFlow, DomainWarpShear, ErosionFilter, ExchangeFoam, FaultLines, FlowNoise, FlowShingle, GradedVoronoi, GroundedScatter, HeightBlend, LyapunovStretch, Oscillator, PeriodMember, PhasorNoise, PlateDrift, QuasiTile, RayMarch, SimplexFacet, SpanningMaze, SplineRemap, Stamp, StampLayers, StampScatter, SteerablePerlin, StencilFilter, StochasticPatch, StreakSmear, SurfaceProbe, Textile, TileDomain, TubeNoise, VortexPhase have a real FastSIMD port with a report.

decisions.title: Widen Metadata::Vector index_type from uint8_t to uint16_t
decisions.why: This plan overflows the 255-entry global pools; see the pool budget. In a release build the assert compiles out and the index wraps silently. It is a 1-line change in a public header, and sizeof(Metadata) grows. Nothing here has built it yet.
decisions.default: Do it first, as batch 0a. The alternative is trimming enums and members until the budget fits, which conflicts with the look tests.

decisions.title: Keep gradient kernels internal, or add a public GenGrad path on Generator
decisions.why: Five of six lenses name the missing gradient path as the biggest structural hole. The plan builds K1 and K2 as internal helpers only. A virtual value-plus-gradient on Generator would let ErosionFilter, SurfaceProbe and DomainWarpFlow skip finite differences on any graph, at the cost of a dispatch-table and architecture change in every node.
decisions.default: Internal for this plan. K2 is the single place a future GenGrad would plug in.

decisions.title: Accept the merges that overrule a critic call
decisions.why: HeightBlend own node (critic: Fade mode). DomainWarpFlow takes Curl (critic: separate nodes). StampLayers takes Crater, Bubble, Pebble (critics: one node or siblings; pebble separately). CellularEdge takes Foam and Plate (critic: CellularDistance and CellularValue modes). TileDomain takes TileSplit (critic: ship). DomainInvert in over MultigridNoise.
decisions.default: As planned. Each can split back into a second class in the same file.

decisions.title: Policy for nodes with no real 4D form
decisions.why: QuasiTile and DendryNoise have no 4D, ErosionFilter needs a special torus Gen, and SpanningMaze and PhasorNoise lose their property on the torus. The default fallback drops w and silently breaks GenTileable2D. The maintainer lens asks for a metadata flag rather than a silent fallback.
decisions.default: Say so in the node description for now. A metadata flag would be a small separate change.

decision_notes.D1: Since done: the scaffold merge widened it to uint16_t with registration caps.

pool_budget.index_type: Metadata::Vector<T>::index_type = uint8_t, include/FastNoise/Metadata.h line 56; assert in Metadata.cpp push_back compiles out in Release, so overflow wraps silently
pool_budget.per_node_limit: MemberLookup.index is 5 bits (Metadata.cpp): at most 32 of each member kind per node in encoded trees
pool_budget.node_id_limit: node_id is uint8_t with 255 reserved for references: 47 + 30 + tier 3 stays well under
pool_budget.encoded_tree_compat: Read in DeserialiseSmartNodeInternal: variables and hybrids are stored with their member index, and a missing generator lookup gets a dummy Constant, so appending members at the end of an existing node keeps old encoded trees loading. Not run, read only. Inserting in the middle would break them.

kernels.what: Value + analytic gradient from one lattice visit: Perlin 2D/3D/4D, Simplex 2D/3D/4D with the r^2 = 0.5 kernel. Value + gradient + Hessian Simplex 2D/3D/4D. One-lattice multi-channel Perlin with a per-vertex value term and full Jacobian.
kernels.risks: The 4D Simplex Hessian is unwritten and the caustics critic names it the main port risk. Real Simplex in 3D/4D uses radius 0.6 kernels that jump; these kernels must use r^2 = 0.5.
kernels.test: Lab-only check node: analytic gradient and Hessian against a central difference over about 1e6 points per dimension, all feature sets.

kernels.what: Finite-difference gradient of any GeneratorSource: Jet (D+1 taps) and Central (2D taps) stencils, exact-step divisor hx = (x+h)-(x-h), fourth-root step law h = hw * max(1, 4 * (|x| 2^-23 / hw)^(1/4)).
kernels.risks: The critic found the exact-step gain mostly disappears once a real Feature Scale multiplies after the step (8.8 vs 11.5% at fq 0.4). The fourth-root law is tested on Perlin only, 2 seeds, and adds 2 sqrts per lane.
kernels.test: Gradient error against K1 analytic Perlin at 1e5, 3e5 and 1e6 features, compared.

kernels.what: 3^D window pass with FastNoise's 0.43701595 disc jitter that stores rel[i], d2[i], hash[i] and keeps F1/F2 by Select. Exact bisector second pass over the same window. Symmetric pair hash mix(ha ^ hb, ha + hb). F1-relative compact weight Max(0, 1 - (d_i - d1)/S)^(2^m). Top-K Select-chain insertion.
kernels.risks: Storing 81 vectors in 4D will probably spill registers; PlateDrift's notes suggest recomputing sites from hashes in the inner loop to avoid that. Exact jitter limits from the critic's search, not proofs: 2D GJ 0.940, 3D 0.917, 4D 0.909.
kernels.test: F1/F2 against stock CellularDistance on the same seed and jitter; edge distance against the prototype brute force.

kernels.what: Polynomial atan2, the continuous octant-scaled atan (scale 1.00025877), one-reduction sincos, hash to 2D rotation, Shoemake quaternion from hash and 18-flop rotate, superellipse and superellipsoid SDF with an e=2 fast path, polynomial smooth min.
kernels.risks: Low. atan2 accuracy only needs about 1e-3 rad for the piecewise-linear profiles.
kernels.test: Worst-case error sweep against std:: functions; the octants must meet exactly for the Fan pattern.

batches.title: Infrastructure and shared kernels

serial_first.name: 0a pools and registration scaffold
serial_first.what: Widen Metadata::Vector::index_type to uint16_t and bump gMetadataVectorSize (decision D1). Add every planned node's include and FASTNOISE_REGISTER_NODE to the bottom of FastSIMD_Build.inl and FastNoise.h in registration order, each wrapped in #if __has_include(...), so later branches add only their own new files. Node ids shift while nodes are missing, which is fine in the lab because fnlab trees use names, and they settle at this order once all exist. Untested idea: if __has_include misbehaves in the FastSIMD multi-include build, fall back to an integrator adding these lines in plan order at merge.

batches.exit: All four kernels pass their lab-only checks and merge into the lab base branch.

gates: `fnlab check`: 0 FAIL, including SSE2, SSE41, AVX2 and AVX512 parity. A stock brick graph already failed AVX512 parity on 27% of samples, so do not assume it.

Straddling jump scan: bisection across lattice lines. `ContinuityProbe` at its default origin cannot see integer lattice lines: the voronoi critic moved the origin and saw GiniFoam go 7.93 to 1.00. Treat any c0ratio near 8 in `tournament.json` on a lattice node as unverified.
`fnlab sheet`, `relief` or `vol` beside the prototype's best image. Look at both and say what differs.
`fnlab bench` for the real cost, recorded here in place of the estimate. A measured `ScaleOutput` constant, and a `VariableRange` mixin where the output is a noise.
Far coordinates and `fnlab tile`, with any failure written into the node description.

nodes.expected_cost: Measured with fnlab bench, min of 3 runs, 2 stripe octaves on a 3 octave Perlin FBm, clang-cl 23. AVX2 29.56 / 42.60 / 69.92 ns, SSE41 66.74 / 91.15 / 155.40, AVX512 19.23 / 26.63 / 54.35. That FBm alone is AVX2 3.12 / 6.58 / 12.24, so 4 taps are 12.5 / 26.3 / 49.0. On plain Perlin AVX2 19.62 / 24.66 / 36.81. Stripe octaves on the FBm, AVX2 2D: 1 is 20.86, 3 is 36.05, about 8 ns each. Hand harness estimates were 25.6 / 37 / 56 with forward differences.
nodes.dims: 2D, 3D and 4D measured. 3D is a heightfield: lattice in the two axes other than Up Axis, the up axis only reaches the source. 4D serves GenTileable2D only: lattice on the angles of (x, z) and (y, w) with whole cell counts from the radii. The tile closes, but other 4D positions jump where a count changes (fnlab seams 4D: 3655 of 4000, worst 0.306), and the description says so.
nodes.range: Output stays in source units, so no ScaleOutput and no VariableRange. Delta is bounded by Strength * (1 - Gain^octaves) / (1 - Gain). Measured on a normalised FBm3 over 8 seeds: Height -0.781..0.871, Delta -0.150..0.192, mean +0.046. Mask is exactly -1..1.
notes: Remaining weaknesses: short dashes of one size at wide views, faint 6-fold imprint (|c6| .13 to .15), heightfield only.
Reimplement from the maths: the reference gist derives from CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 code. The Phacelle reference is MPL-2.0, so write that clean too.

EdgeDistance 4.31 / 14.35 / 57.76, Bevel 4.45 / 14.53 / 57.90, Cobble 4.68 / 14.90 / 58.98. Crack at 3 Levels 8.05 / 18.85 / 62.93, LeafValue at 3 Levels 6.98 / 15.50 / 51.21. EdgeMask with 3 Colours 5.59 / 16.69 / 63.38. Foam 5.55 / 16.92 / 61.57, Plate 8.60 / 29.13 / 105.11. SSE41 EdgeMask 9.22 / 31.69 / 123.39, AVX512 3.10 / 9.87 / 36.91. Stock T-junction graph: 35 / 106 / 345 ns measured.
nodes.dims: 2D, 3D and 4D, one GenT over a pack.
nodes.range: Measured, 3M samples per dimension at Grid Jitter 1: EdgeDistance max .669 / .590 / .554, so ScaleOutput over 0 to .68 / .60 / .56 with Min above that. Foam: 1 - sum w^2 / (sum w)^2 over 0 to .75, reached at 4 way vertices and clamped. Plate: scaled down by max(1, |Lift| + .75 |Tilt|), so a Lift or Tilt source crossing 0 stays continuous (review: the pure ratio jumped at the zero contour), measured p99.99 .908 / .871 / .855 at the defaults and Smoothness .06, clamped at +-1. Bevel, EdgeMask, Crack, Cobble are 0 to 1 by construction, LeafValue is a hash.
notes: The critic rejected CellularDistance return types because Size Jitter and non-Euclidean metrics would sit there invalid.

Worst real seam at GJ 1.0 is a kink, visible only in shading (149 of 12M wrong, max 0.0245, on the real generator). Real node: straddling window borders at GJ 1, 81 of 1M in 2D jump, max .054 of output range, 3D and 4D none; GJ .9 none.
PolyGauge (tier 3) lands here as one more Output if wanted.

Port differences from the prototypes: Cobble dome is 1 - (1 - t)^3, the quarter circle's infinite slope at a wall scans as a jump. Foam has no per site pressure, which is not in the member list and costs provable window safety, so walls are straight. Cuts with Colours fade within .05 of a wall, otherwise they stop dead at a merged wall and jump. nodes.dims: 2D at Families 4, 5, 7 and 3D real, each matched tile for tile against a double precision forward construction. NO 4D (about 1120 candidates by estimate): 4D ignores w. GenTileable2D wraps with no seam (fnlab tile ratio 0.47) but shows a warped slice through the rhombohedra with no rhombs, and rows v and -v are equal on 100.0% of pixels, so it mirrors top to bottom. The description says so.
nodes.range: Native ranges by construction, no fitted constant. Value outputs are +-1, EdgeDistance is 0 to half the widest tile thickness (0.5 at Four, 0.4755 at Five, 0.4875 at Seven, 0.4253 in 3D), Bevel reaches 1 at the highest stone. Measured over 1M samples per dimension on 2 seeds: all of them -1.0000 to 1.0000 except EdgeDistance tops of 0.9945 to 0.9961 in 2D and 0.9714 in 3D, which random samples only approach at tile centres. CentreLookup passes Lookup through.
notes: Candidate bound re-proved by an independent double-precision forward construction: exactly one rhomb per point, 0 hits outside {floor t, ceil t}.

The prototype's float32 ceil gave bad samples of .06% at 1e3 tile edges, 1.8% at 1e5, 13.9% at 1e6. The port writes each tile relative to its crossing, which cancels the large terms, and gets ceil( t ) - t from wrapping 32 bit fixed point. A test compares tile identity to a double precision reference: tile wrong by more than 8 float steps on 0 of 120000 samples up to 3e4 tile edges, .0033% at 1e5, .1% at 1e6, 30% at 3e6, where float32 t breaks the candidate bound. Past 1e6 the description warns.

Thick / thin area ratio 2.6273 against phi^2 2.6180, lowest corner index only 1 or 2 at Families Five, so true Penrose. Singular gamma: 40 seeds including 0, +-1, INT_MAX and INT_MIN gave no sample off by more than 8 float steps.

Sharing line products between combinations was tried: 2% at Five, nothing at Seven, reverted. A runtime branch around the coordinate selects made AVX512 3D CentreLookup 66-143 ns and unstable, a template bool made it 50-54.

Continuous with a very steep slope, 677 per unit in the prototype, which is why c0ratio read 2. The real node uses softness / sqrt( det^2 + softness^2 ), no crease and half the slope (fnlab check max slope 30.5 to 14.9 per feature in 2D), and fnlab check reads a step ratio of 7.8. fnlab seams still flags Feature Scale 40 (1 of 4000 in 3D and 4D, Free about 50); the flagged step shrinks with the window, so it is slope and not a jump. A texture, not a heightfield.
Corr/IoU against the ray histogram is not a quality judge: a Newton polish beat Steps 3 on the metric and looked worse. Judge by eye.

nodes.dims: 2D, 3D and 4D are real forms. 2D (g_y, -g_x), 4D (g_y, -g_x, g_w, -g_z) on one potential, measured seamless through GenTileable2D. 3D Curl with no Potential is grad phi x grad psi from two channels of one K1 lattice visit, peak speed 4.8 x rms against 2.3 x in 2D, so it tangles sooner. 3D Curl with a Potential is g x axis with the axis cycling Z, X, Y per step, one potential per step and no dependence on seed, net displacement about 0.58 x path at 3 steps.
nodes.range: Warp: output is the Source's, Path Average is a weighted mean of Source samples. No ScaleOutput. The measured constants are the speed scales instead, 0.7485 / 0.858 / 0.942 and 0.912 for the 3D cross, so Warp Amplitude is the rms path length on Perlin (measured 0.99 to 1.02 over 3 seeds in every dimension), peak 2.3 x in 2D and 4D, 4.8 x in 3D Curl.
notes: Prototype amplitudes map as Warp Amplitude = 0.75 x A x Feature Scale, the prototype rms speed is 0.75 (mean displacement 0.693 against 0.92 here). L in the flow prototype maps to 1.6 x L x Feature Scale. Gradient mode descends at positive amplitude, so A=-3.33 is 2.5 x Feature Scale.

Measured limits, Steps 4 and 12 on Perlin: no jump found up to about 1 x Feature Scale, thin folds get as sharp as jumps from 2 x, feature sets and entry points disagree from 6 x. Connected fBm: about 1 x the finest octave is clean, 5 x fails parity.

DISAGREEMENT: the eddies critic wanted Curl and Flow as separate nodes. Merged because both are the same step loop and differ only in where the gradient comes from. Split if the two paths read badly in the editor.
The Jupiter look comes from the hand-built potential, not the node. It needs a preset, and scalar cost with that potential is 2526 ns per the terrain lens.

tier3.name: FeistelWarp

tier3.name: SplatKernel

tier3.name: CellularHexLattice
tier3.queue_rank_reason: Honeycomb, BCC and A4* candidate tables save up to 2.5x in 4D at low jitter (J4 top pick). Hex 2D alone justifies a Lattice enum.
tier3.why: Superseded for now by the Simplex-window Voronoi question in round 2, which attacks the same 3D/4D window cost harder (6/8/10 sites).

tier3.name: RegionSpectrumFractal
tier3.queue_rank_reason: Octaves evaluated once and reweighted per Voronoi region: cheap biome spectra at FBm plus one coarse Cellular. Check the kink at Voronoi vertices.
tier3.why: Unverified kink at Voronoi vertices and no panel demand.

tier3.name: LocalFrame
tier3.queue_rank_reason: Binned scale and rotation crossfade removes origin shear when scale varies by mask, 2x source. Earlier proto beats naive scaling; watch the ghosting band.
tier3.why: Ghosting band is unresolved. GradedVoronoi covers the cell case; revisit with the LOD gap.

tier3.name: CombineOps
tier3.queue_rank_reason: Chamfer, stairs and groove combiners under 1 ns. Fillet radii are only true on distance-like inputs, so pair with iso-distance.
tier3.why: Fillet radii are only true on distance-like inputs, so it waits for SurfaceProbe SignedDistance to prove useful in graphs.

tier3.name: DomainTile
tier3.queue_rank_reason: Wrap and crossfade for any graph including 3D. Check ghosting in the band and the 16x worst case in 4D.
tier3.why: Ghosting in the band and a 16x worst case in 4D. Try the Period member first.

tier3.name: MultipoleNoise
tier3.queue_rank_reason: Disputed: J3 top pick for changing zero-set topology, while the others expect near-Perlin. A kernel swap in a Perlin proto settles it quickly.
tier3.why: Disputed. J3 expected new topology, others near-Perlin. A kernel swap in a Perlin proto settles it, which makes it a round 2 test, not a node.

tier3.name: FractalSpectrum
tier3.queue_rank_reason: Hybrid per-octave weights at constant variance: a strong graph control that is still FBm visually. Only normalisation needs testing.
tier3.why: Still FBm visually, per the queue.

tier3.name: ContrastFade
tier3.queue_rank_reason: Variance-preserving lerp with one InvSqrt that fixes washed-out fades. Likely a Fade option rather than a new node.
tier3.why: Likely a Fade option, not a node. Small, but no look evidence.

tier3.name: CdfRemap
tier3.queue_rank_reason: Threshold X means X percent coverage. Start with the analytic Gaussian stage, since Measured mode holds stale state across subtree edits.
tier3.why: Measured mode holds stale state across subtree edits. Only the analytic Gaussian stage would be safe.

side_findings.text: verifier: leak found and fixed. FastNoise_C.cpp fnDeleteNodeRef only decrements the reference count (Internal::BumpNodeRefences) and never runs the destructor or frees, so every tree built through the C API leaks; confirmed natively on base.dll through ctypes (370 B per 3-node tree, 89 B per lone Simplex) and in master and v1.1.1, so it is a repo bug, not a WASM one. Through fnwasm.js a slider leaked about 275 B per rebuild per worker and defaultDsl() 2.4 KB per call. Fix: fnwasm_shim.cpp gains fnwasmDeleteNodeRef (holds the node in a temporary SmartNode while the C API reference is dropped, so the last release destroys it), and Core in fnwasm.js makes core.x a plain copy of the exports with fnDeleteNodeRef pointing at it, so every caller gets the releasing version. Both .wasm files rebuilt (713558 and 719178 bytes). After the fix 2000 varying rebuilds, failed builds, encode, enc: reloads and defaultDsl churn move the heap top by 0 bytes; the cached-node path holds exactly one extra 64 KB SmartNode pool, flat from 10k to 60k rebuilds.
side_findings.title: C API node leak (fnDeleteNodeRef)
