items: '2^D corner lattice and 3x3 splats are visually indistinguishable at F1.5': false. stripes_kernels and new seeds 42 and 9001 show rectangular cuts on the lattice and an organic field on the splats.

'At usable F~1.5, or whenever the direction is steered or fixed, it is invisible': false. Tile borders appear in all 12 panels of the corner grid including spread .25, and steered lattice has short straight seams on seeds 42 and 9001. foldCV stays .215 when steered.

'Orientation domains have straight borders on cell edges': the fold shows the excess energy as a cross through the cell centre, so the seams sit on cell mid lines, where the quintic weight hands over.

'FFT axis stat does not single the lattice out' is true but was used as comfort. The stat is blind: corner 5.24, hex 5.60, though only the corner sheet shows a visible cross. Ensemble field axis ratio is 1.03-1.08 for all kernels, while energy fold and Bragg peaks do separate them (104, 87, 30, 5.4).

Scalar ratios not reproduced: lattice 4.64x measured 6.50-7.11x; splat 7.09x measured 9.20x; ripple 3.34x measured 5.8-6.1x; vortex 3.21x measured 4.11-4.31x; dunes 9.07x measured 16.33x with the same params. The same dune binary measured 6.64x with no params set, so std::map lookups appear to matter a lot; do not rank kernels by this harness.
'Lattice est ~3.5 ns AVX2, 3x3 ~8 ns': direct AVX2 measured 5.10 and 11.64 ns, so the estimates were low and 3x3 costs 2.3x the corner kernel, not 1.5x.

'Coherent + pjit .6 gives isolated dislocations, no explicit cuts needed': the corner kernel shows a large closed loop and squared steps on seed 1337, and squared jogs on seeds 42 and 9001. Vortex phase gives the clean forks instead. The explicit cut form remains untested.
'Dune defect sweep goes cleanly from ridges to junctions to dashes': false. Defect .5 has horizontal gashes and defect 1 is a rectilinear gash network following the lattice.
'Transverse-dunes is an Output mode of lattice-phasor': works, but the vortex phase is better at equal spacing. Plain ridges are also a stock 8 node graph at 6.04 ns.
'4x4 window is the most organic': it is dotty, has an FFT cross, and has a flat grey hole with hard shards in the XZ slice.
'Ripple: the 3x3 window caps R at 1': only at jitter 1. R1.125 j.75 and R1.25 j.5 fill the field at c0 7.99-8.03, per the rule R <= 1.5 - jitter/2 the prototyper itself recorded for splats.

'Vortex scroll sheets at fr14: tightly folded pastry, no analogue': thick slabs at fr14. The folded look needs fr 30, and stock PingPong of |A+iB| at strength 9.5 is the same family at 4.57/7.53 ns AVX2.

'Vortex 4D works by construction': true for seams, not the look. The stock graph tile test has seam ratio 1.00 but few broad bands, because the plane carrier does not hold its frequency on the torus. Tested on the stock graph, not a real node.
'B defaults to A at seed+1': same lattice forces cores at lattice points, 62.5% of low |z| samples against 6.2% uniform, and straight cuts on seed 42. It needs an offset.
'Phase-vortex: keep as Wave=Triangle': that wave only greys the carrier in the q by wave grid, so there is nothing to keep.
'3D isosurface is gyroid-like': the volume is an irregular sponge, not gyroid-regular, and corner, splat and BCC kernels look alike at w6.

The depth-table scores (corr, IoU) rank the candidates by look. Not reliably: a Picard-then-Newton back map I added scored .926 / .62 at D=1.1 seed 42, above web/3 at .921 / .53, yet the image shows speckled double edges and debris at junctions. The 1.5 px blur and 10% IoU reward wider ribbons, so the metric can be gamed and only separates candidates far apart.

CausticMesh is a candidate node. It is a bake tool at best: 2166 ns scalar measured here (42.8x perlin2), true jumps at mesh fold edges, polygon facets in hillshade, 2D and plane-3D only; a true 3D or 4D form would need a window^d of simplices.

fold-caustic as written has a reason to exist. Its default form (A=0.8, single sheet, independent Perlin noises) is separate loops around blobs on a mottled floor with axis streaks; only the back-mapped Simplex form earns a place, and that is an enum on CausticWeb, not a node.
Erosion AVX2 25-40 ns at 5 stripe octaves, 3-5 ns per stripe octave (estimates): measured 44.9 ns analytic and 50.3 ns forward difference at 5 octaves, about 8.1 ns per stripe octave.
Fractal-derivative only 3 percent over plain ridged: a scalar artefact. AVX2 harness: uber 9.19 ns, swiss 11.52 ns, ridged 6.52 ns, so 1.41x and 1.77x.
Fractal-derivative is 'a look ridged plus graphs cannot make': false for Uber. Real FractalRidged Weighted=1 gives the same crests and bowls at 6.58 ns.
'No mode produces gullies': too strong. Swiss on its own base gives long parallel downhill flutes on steep walls at warp .15-.3, though they do not branch.
Slope-aligned slightly cheaper than plain simplex FBm: scalar early-out artefact. AVX2 without early out: 7.99 ns vs 6.67 ns, 1.20x.
Erosion hillshade 'converging into smooth valleys, flats stay smooth from the slope mask': the relief shows valley floors as rough as the flanks. Only an added altitude mask makes them smooth.
'The base must be smooth': true only with a narrow stencil. A .2 forward-difference stencil takes fbm5 c0 3.48 to 7.14 and ridged4 c0 1.25 to 6.54.
5 stripe octaves as the recommended default: 2 octaves nearly match it at half the cost once the altitude fade is on.
Same-base comparison at equal str: amplitudes differ up to 5.7x (rms delta uber .021 vs erosion 2 oct .119).
3x3 polynomial 'identical' to the 4x4 window taken as a clean result: both square lattices carry an unreported + weave, |c4| .23-.29 at the first octave.
Fractal-derivative vol 'solid 3D lobes': at iso 0 it is almost solid with a few holes, because the mean is about +.3 to +.4.
Slope-aligned 3D 'streaky surfaces': the vol shows pockmarked surfaces with dots.
Aniso-simplex-steered c0ratio 8.0: measured 6.38 with max slope 56 at seed 42.
Erosion '3D heightfield form works' as a 3D noise: raw vol is vertical extrusions. It works only as h minus y density.

dendry-noise: 'the wide panel keeps branching everywhere, with regional thick and thin zones' understates it; at 96 cells (seed 42, window 24) the baseline is half white blob, half thin scribble because width tracks the drift field. Fixed by per-segment normalisation (wmode=1).
fern-fold: 'reading as rivers up close' failed; at seed 7 window 16 and seed 42 window 48 the drainage layout reads as lightning/frost at every scale.

catchment-rivers: scalar_vs_perlin 72.5 does not describe the listed params; with cmode=2 (as listed and as used for every terrain image) I measured 7243 ns, 144.7x Perlin. 3739 ns (75.9x) only with cmode=3.
stochastic descent: 'hubs mostly dissolve into confluences' is generous; seed 7 dendry still shows several star junctions and diamond crossings. 'Reduced, not gone' holds.

A naive local width normalisation that reads the sample's window seams (17 true jumps, worst 0.359): the prototyper's cap-by-window argument covers geometry but not any per-sample modulation, which a port must keep per segment.

Prototyper: 3D edge distance exact at the default ring 0.396, so no jitter change is needed. My search finds failures above r* 0.3629-0.3637 (GJ 0.917), worst error 0.0358. The real generator showed 0 of 1.5M, so this is true only as a sampling result.

Prototyper: 2D max error 0.005 at the default ring. Worst case is 0.0327 by search and 0.0245 on the real generator over 12M independent samples. t_edge_audit does reproduce 0.0053, but it samples 4 seeds on a contiguous block.

Prototyper: Edge Drop and Crease vertex jumps are unsolved and a continuous drop needs all window pairs. Site colours with F_other need one compare per stored site and give c0 8.00 with 0 jumps above 0.2 in 3M 2D and 800k 3D samples (kd 0.2 or more, GridJitter 0.90).
Prototyper: Voronoi-root recursive cut matches ShatterBSP almost pixel for pixel. The comparison shows the same style, but the interior cuts do not coincide.

Prototyper: Order-2 kite mosaic is something no existing value mode produces. Add of CellularValue index 0 and 1 gives the same kind of partition (25 / 78 / 255 ns AVX2), with different walls and correlated tones.
Prototyper evidence: the lacunarity grid predates the strip-pick fix (file 01:44:33, fix logged 01:47:16). The hatching conclusion still holds on a re-render at seed 4242.

Catalogue and earlier critic: T-junctions cannot come from a graph, and Min of two F2-F1 only crosses. A per-cell DomainOffset makes the child network stop at the parent wall. Three levels pass check with 0 FAIL at 35 / 106 / 345 ns.

Earlier critic: nothing in the existing nodes gives bricks with a per-tile id. A graph makes a running-bond wall with tone and mortar at 16 / 46 / 148 ns, though it fails AVX512 parity on 27% of samples.

Earlier critic: recursive-cut-noise should ship as ContourCut. Thin closed rings appear around lattice vertices at seeds 31337 and 4242, and the 32-unit view is a scribble rather than a crack network.

TPMS FFT axis stat 'at window 16 ... 10 two octaves': my window-16 sheets read 16.05 (seed 7, prior critic image) and 19.14 (seed 42) for a=6.6 wf=.157 oct=2; the two-octave warp does not weaken the cross versus one octave.

The caves comparison table's 'Gyroid, warped' rows (a=4 wf=.1 and a=3 wf=.1 oct2) are a visible honeycomb crystal in the prototyper's own cave sheet, so the 100% connectivity / CV .306 figures describe a crystal lattice, not the organic a=6.6 sponge the text recommends, which was never in the table.

'A smooth sponge with no visible repeat in a 12 unit window' for a=6.6 wf=.157: window-12 vol views at seeds 3, 7 and 42 show domains of locally parallel channels (polycrystal). No exact repeat, but orientation order is plainly visible.
TPMS '3D with one-lattice warp is 2.55x' describes oct=1; the recommended oct=2 preset measures 5.83x perlin2 scalar (298 ns) in my run, and the AVX2 estimate of about 9 ns is the low end.

TubeNoise estimated 4D AVX2 7-12 ns: scalar 4D is 10.3x perlin2 (527 ns) with 16 lattice corners and 2-3 channels of Jacobian, so my estimate is 20-40 ns (estimate, not measured); GenTileable2D will be slow.

Plain gyroid has no cheap existing-node form (implied by 'TPMSNoise ... no lattice' as a new primitive): a verified 11-node graph of SineWave + DomainOffset + RemoveDimension + Add renders an exact gyroid at 3.69 ns AVX2 3D, and DomainWarpGradient on it gives the warped sponge.

Truchet is not a connected network (55 components, largest 3.5%): measurement bug, NETCONN ran at static init before gMatchInit and flood filled parallel x cylinders. Re-measured 99.1-99.3% in 6^3 on seeds 99 and 2024, 100.00% in the 11^3 core at 21-22% void. Only thin tubes are disconnected (rmax <= 0.17: 9%).

Bond is the only member connected in view and cheap: real Add(a^2, b^2) of two Perlin is 99.99-100.00% in the core at 11% void, 9.29 ns AVX2, no warp. Real F3-F1 is 99.99% at 11% void, 12.2-12.7 ns. Bond plus warp is 12.92 ns. Bond wins only below about 5% void or in its unwarped rectilinear look.

Bond 99.1-99.6% in one component: on unseen seeds 97.7-98.5% in 6^3. That number mostly measures box cuts; the 11^3 core is 100.00%, so the claim is low on the true figure and high on its own measure.
Connected by construction: bond is statistical (p=0.4 95.3% in the core with 13 sealed pockets). My mode 3 spine rule, which is connected by construction, did worse in view than p=0.6.
Two octaves (0.3@1.2 + 1.2@0.2) remove all straight lines: seed 99 still reads as a grid at windows 8 and 14, k=1 peak/median 209-266.

Warp amounts as stated transfer to the real graph: real DomainWarpGradient is hermite value noise (RMS 0.39 x amp vs 0.22 x for proto Perlin). On a real lattice with real warp nodes, 0.66 cells FS 5 cells leaves peak 78566 and a clear grid.

Warping did not break connectivity: with the real warp replica, core 98.16-99.93% at 1 cell, 96.21-99.87% at 1.25 cells, thin tubes 86.65% at 1 cell (voxel limited), and sealed pockets appear (31-46 at 1 cell).

A hybrid Bond Chance is the obvious next step: sampled at the point it gives c0ratio 1.03, max slope 1851 (tubes cut with a jump). Face centre sampling is continuous but costs 2n source evals. A low frequency mask in a graph on top does the job instead.
4D is the same loop over 8 faces: run through a 4D torus as GenTileable2D does, it is isolated dots, and a flat 3D slice is fragments. No tiling and no w animation.
Spanning bond-graph p=0.5 98.1%: 95.3-96.6% in 6^3 on seeds 99 and 2024.

Strata is a look nothing else produces: the existing-node graph gives the same floors, domes, plans and shafts on my seeds at 32.06 ns (33.92 with y warp and dip), though 40 nodes and with blind shaft ends.

Strata does not need a warp: a y-only warp keeps floors flat, varies layer thickness and removes the ruler; a y-only dip tilts the beds. Clearly better image, connectivity unchanged (99.98-100.00% in the core).
Strata defaults 76.7% and pillar setting 52.8%: 51.1% and 35.3% in 6^3 on seed 99.

Scalar ratios: bond 2.52x was the tree default; 7.13x perlin2 under the harness with the recommended params. Strata 18.92x, not 9.77x. These run through the parameter map, so they overstate; the measured AVX2 ratio for bond is 4.2x Perlin 3D.

lyapunov-stretch: 'rising strain removes the straight bands' - straight lines go but a herringbone/weave hatch remains in the wide view at seed 21 (axis 25, woven basket at window 48) and in every variant tried (golden table, gain 1.0/1.05, warm 2/3, 12 steps: axis 16 to 42); seed 1337 is the kindest seed

shear-flow: 'Periodic3 at 9 to 21 steps gives curling smoke, c0ratio 3.6' - at seed 7 with 21 steps c0ratio is 1.5 and max slope 733 (aliasing filaments); 9 steps gives c0ratio 6.0 with clean curls, so only 9 steps is usable

domain-warp-sine: 'Parabola 8 steps is the cheapest good warp' - on a stripe source at window 64 it is a regular textile with a wallpaper wide view; it is only good on FBm-like sources, and its 3.3 ns figure is an unverified estimate

shear-flow: the report presents 3D as working ('lamellar sheets') - the volume at seed 7 and the gallery vol are torn planar sheets from the 1D kernel, a visible 3D weakness that needs the noise2 option

family: 'chains match or beat progressive warps' - the only measured numbers are the real nodes (progressive Gradient 3 = 3.06 ns 2D); the chain costs are hand kernel estimates I could not reproduce, so the 2D cost comparison is unverified and on the estimates the chain is 2x dearer in 2D
DomainWarpFlow is the only thing in the family that makes real ink marbling and needs 8-16 steps: 4 analytic curl sub-steps give nearly the same picture as 12, seen on bands and Worley, seed 2024.
Existing warps never fold a ribbon over itself: same-seed real DomainWarpSimplex and DomainWarpGradient chains fold into plates with spiral eyes.

The independent-vector warp does not pinch: real DomainWarpGradient FS34 at matched displacement makes closed rings and islands on bands, and real Simplex and SuperSimplex make star junctions on Worley.

Curl keeps line density and cell size even everywhere: only partly. Cell area CV is lower than real warps, but a single step at displacement 0.71 folds 42.8% of pixels and has det spread 5.81. Evenness of that kind needs sub-steps.

Curl is much cheaper than the independent warp (147 vs 219 ns): this harness bias is large, the same warp reads 155-217 ns depending on how many keys are passed. At equal key count it is 180-189 vs 221-226 ns, about 1.2x.

Facet shatter: no existing node or graph can do it. Real FD curl of Euclidean F1 reproduces it closely at 12 nodes and 18.12 ns (wider breaks rather than thin tears), and a per-cell shift gives a straight-shard variant at 4 nodes and 21.10 ns.

Fluted cones are not available from existing warps: half true. Independent fractal warps give blobby cells, but a real 16-node FD curl graph at 21.21 ns gives the same star pits and fluted relief, so it is a recipe, not a reason for a node.

Normalise plus decaying step is required for descent and unnormalised speed overshoots into chaos: plain descent is clean at a step of 0.19 features, shows stripes at 0.25, grain at 0.38 and static from 0.5.
Sink is a kernel worth keeping: its foam is the same glass-crumple family as a progressive gradient warp, rounder and less lattice aligned, so Gradient mode covers it closely enough.

VortexCells is a fair Jupiter candidate and belongs in the curl node: on bands it reads as stamped, as the report admits, but its better use is layered fBm curls, and exact disc rotation does not come from a potential.
QuasiTile scalar_vs_perlin 5.54: that is the branchy hit test; with the recommended params (best=1 margin selection) the harness measures 433 ns = 8.22x perlin2 and 3.75x worley2

QuasiTile est_avx2 15-25 ns for 2D N=5 is optimistic as a single range: scaling worley2 scalar to CellularDistance AVX2 gives about 15 ns but the prototyper's own 10:1 rule gives about 43 ns; it is 15-45 ns, estimate only

DomainQuasicrystal 'MultigridNoise produces the same looks directly' understates the case: the octagonal Checkerboard ornament is already a two-node graph of existing nodes (AddDimension x2 with Gradient positions), verified by rendering it with fnlab on base.dll
MultigridNoise Parity and LatticeDistance at N=4 are reachable from existing nodes by the same 4D cut (at 4D source cost); only N=5 and N=7 are truly new
SubstitutionTiling 'promising': seed 3 wide window shows the same structural direction bias and long streaks, Robinson stop=0 is periodic; this is showcase material, not a candidate node
Grounded stones are half buried: at default sink .35 the exposed fraction is .915 over 333 stones on 3 new seeds. Half buried needs sink=1 (.504).

Grounded flagstones and the tilt option were proven: the prototyper's mean radius rest rule floated its own flagstones, 11.1% at tilt=1 and 39.9% at tilt=0. The support-distance rule from the earlier critic pass gives 0%.

Thinning wherever overlap exceeds K is the caveat of K-limited selection: this mostly comes from the rank-subtract formula. The cascade fade at the same source evals takes mass kept at K=2 from .63 to .80 at mean overlap 4.91. Only exact K+1 way ties must vanish (algebraic argument).
K=4 is clean with solid domes: true only at the prototyper's low density. RMS error to the 9 stamp reference with its fade at K=4 is .70 of std at mean overlap 4.91, though mass kept is .98.
Document K >= pi*R^2*Density: 2D only. Measured mean overlap at R=1.5 is 14.1 in 3D and 25 in 4D, so K=4 cannot meet the rule there.
Range -0.94..0.94 for stamp-scatter: Perlin source only. Stripes reach +-1.40 and craters -2.35 to .60, so a port needs a per-source scale.
Sizes within a pebble layer must stay fairly uniform: not inherent. A per-layer cell size from a golden sequence (sizej=0.3) mixes sizes with one constant per layer.
CraterField scalar speed 505.9 ns 2D / 10.16x perlin: measured 708 ns and 714 ns (14.4x perlin2) at the stated 12-level parameter set with base=0.05, in two critic passes.

CraterField: 'the best graph attempt gave only rimless overlapping dimples': a one-layer existing-node graph (bowl clamped to a flat floor plus Abs ring rim, gated by thresholded CellularValue) gives sparse, rimmed, flat-floored craters at a measured 23.6/65/208 ns AVX2. It still lacks multi-scale, erasure and unclipped shapes, so the node stands, but the baseline is better than reported.

BubblePack: 'only very faint rows remain in the wide view': seed 11 window 20 showed plain rows and columns (axis 36.6) because level 0 had rotation angle 0; after adding rot0=0.5 faint diagonal bands of large discs still show at seed 3 window 20 (axis 8.9). The lattice is reduced, not removed.
CumulusNoise FFT 'axis about 24': seed 5 window 12 measures axis 40.9 with a dense even cell lattice in the wide view; the value depends strongly on seed and window.

NestedCracks 'no simple graph could nest them': Min of three scaled F2-F1 layers reproduces the hierarchical-plate height view closely; the only distinctive NestedCracks feature is the dark wedge grooves, which are also its max-slope-164 flaw.

c0ratio as seam evidence: lab_proto ContinuityProbe at its default origin (0.37, 0.61) never samples across an integer lattice line. Moving the origin to (0.3795, 0.6195): GiniFoam press 0.3 7.93 to 1.00, big capsule walls 8.0 to 1.0, Planes S 0.6 8.01 to 1.06, Hierarchy coast 8.0 to 1.0. Graded and Nested stay 8.

GradedVoronoi 'floor k at ~1.15', 'practical floor 1.2', 'theory bound 1.144': crack jumps above 0.01 at k 1.0 (0.1487%, max 0.218), 1.15 (0.0070%, max 0.096) and 1.2 (0.0023%, max 0.081), none from 1.3 up, 300000 samples. The bound is the largest in-window F2 (1.390 seen). Floor at 1.4.

GradedVoronoi 'vol (out=3) gives graded spherical cavities' and 'F1 output is a graded bubble field': a penalty floor lifted F1 by up to k/2 between integer levels, and the old 3D panel is a mostly solid block with two strips of cavities. Fixed with flr=1.
GiniFoam 'clean at jit 1 for press<=0.3': 0.0267 jumps per unit^2, max 1.69, over 6 seeds. press 0 at jit 1 still gives 0.0023 max 0.29. Clean needs jit 0.8 and press <= 0.1.
CellularPlanes 'cap Smoothness at 0.4' as sufficient: at jitter 1, S 0.4 gives 0.0031 max 0.132 and S 0.15 already 0.0003 max 0.071. 0 up to S 0.4 needs jitter 0.8.
CellularShape big-capsule error 'wrong but continuous': it jumps, 0.033-0.042 per unit^2, max 1.71, c0ratio 1.00-1.16 with a straddling probe.
CellularShape 'small capsule no ledges, clean': walls at size 0.2 len 0.3 jit 1 still jump 0.0009, max 0.53. 0 at jitter 0.8.
CellularShape Dmax = 1.063 - Rmax for all shapes: not a bound for non-Euclidean SDFs. Boxes jump 0.0014 max 0.39, hexagons 0.0001 max 0.062. Per-shape bound (dfix=1) gives 0.
CellularHierarchy 'Coast 8.00': at default cw 0.8 it jumps 0.1128 per unit^2, max 1.79, 3D slice 0.0285 max 0.89. Near clean only at cw 0.25 and jitter 0.8.
t_voronoi_common.h 'jitter matches FastNoise' and the 1.5 - 0.437*Jitter cap for 3D and 4D: Cellular.inl uses 0.396144 in 3D and 0.366025 in 4D.

NestedVoronoi and CellularPlanes as keeper nodes: stock graphs reproduce the look. Nested value 39.01 / 124.51 / 424.80 ns, crack 21.31 / 66.45 / 232.55 ns, hard planes 20.75 / 68.38 / 256.22 ns AVX2. What the graphs lack is per-parent frames (Nested) and the soft S range (Planes).

simplex-facet: 'with PL warp .5/.5 relief reads as folded rock' - at seed 7, window 12 it reads as crumpled paper with many small crinkled facets, busier than the bare lattice and the cellular mesh; the lattice is hidden but the look is not clean low poly

cellular-facet-mesh: 'nothing lines up' - seed 7 gives a few long sliver triangles and a 2D axis metric of 47.7 (prototyper sheet 10.9); in 3D the Kuhn split is openly visible as an axis-aligned grid in the flat-mode XZ slice

biome-blend: '3x3 window shows no squareness' is true but misleading - the textured render shows a honeycomb cell mosaic wherever the control is near a biome threshold, a clear lattice imprint not mentioned in the report

biome-blend width: 'constant against the control' holds only as a median; the two-level border at seed 7 is visibly scalloped and the wide view shows lumpy outlines, so for a user the width is not constant
FoamBlend v2 discovery: presented as the clean width winner, but at seed 7 the two-level blobs have pointed cusps and the FFT shows ringing; not a drop-in replacement

Exact-step divisor gives 0.2% at 1e5 and moves the usable range from 1e4 to 1e6 features: true only at frequency 1, since far_test.cpp has no Feature Scale stage. At 1e5 features, h 0.02, exact vs naive is 8.8 vs 11.5% at fq 0.4, 8.5 vs 12.7% at fq 1/7, 3.5 vs 3.5% at fq 0.01. At fq 0.4 the Laplacian is not helped at all: 2.72 vs 2.39 relative error.
2% at 1e6 with h 0.05, floor then needs only 2 ulps: its own far test shows 1.9% with no floor (neighbouring smaller h values are NaN) and 25.8% with the k=2 floor.

Second differences need about 16 ulps: this floor grows past the feature size, giving Laplacian error 55.2% at 3e5 and 96% at 1e6 features (fq 0.4). A root-4 law at C=4 gives 15.8 to 33.6% and 20.6 to 75.6% at the same points (h 0.05 and 0.02).
'At 1e5 features' on the iso and crest far images: far=100000 is world units at fq 0.4, so about 4e4 features.

3-tap jet Laplacian shows a hexagonal null pattern and central does not: false. Central on Simplex shows the same six nulls, including the prototyper's own image. Jet on Perlin shows an axis cross. It belongs to the Simplex kernel, not the stencil.

'All are masks a graph cannot make today': false. Slope built from real nodes renders the same mask, check 0 FAIL, 26.62 ns AVX2 at 5 octaves. Band from real nodes: same look, 0 FAIL, 44.49 ns. Hillshade is close to a 2 node emboss.

Band width visibly constant along the whole coastline on 5 octaves: ground truth spread p90/p10 is 3.28 (3.81 at h 0.03), naive 4.77, and at w 0.2 it is 4.02 vs 4.20. Near constant only at 1 octave (1.07), decent at 3 (1.89).
Doubling the step to 0.06 changes no width: median true distance at the band edge goes from 0.082 to 0.068, band area from 23.5 to 21.3%. At h 0.1 it is 0.062 and missed core is 6.0%.

Gradient Floor 0.1 as a working default: absolute units. At Feature Scale 100 it gives median width 2.94 w, 34% false band, 57.5% area instead of 19%. The prototype was only ever tested at feature size about 2.5.
Crest-lines works with a=0.5, b=3, c=1: output is blank at Feature Scale 100 (min -1, max -1, std 0). The thresholds are absolute on Hessian values, which scale as frequency squared.

Terrace output improves on the value terrace: on seeds 42 and 7 at 3 octaves the plain value terrace looks crisper with flatter treads and the distance risers look smeared. That is my eye; I did not measure riser width.
Canyon cuts an incision of constant width with sheer walls: at 1 octave it reads as blue flats with thin crease lines, at 3 octaves as blobby noise, at 5 octaves pillars.
Crest-lines is 'nothing like Ridged or F2-F1': a thin warped masked F2-F1 reads as a similar crack network at 8.38 ns, though with straighter lines and 120 degree joints.
Crest 3D is fragmented plates, not useful: mostly the 4 step power iteration. A closed-form solve drops z-continuity max from 0.50 to 0.031 and 1.02 to 0.080, and gives a connected membrane.
Crest c0 6.74 is seed dependent: 4.8 on seed 42 for the same 'both' output.
Contour-scarp c0 4.94: 4.31 with the stated params; the sheet was made with default params.
Surface-probe scalar 5.82x with stencil=1: that figure is about the jet (5.71x). Central is 6.88x at 1 octave and 30.37x at 5.
3D continuity is measured on simplex3g (r2 0.5), not the real 3D Simplex (r2 0.6). A real-node slope on Simplex has 3D worst ratio 1.23 against 4.02 on SuperSimplex.

The exact-step divisor 'keeps the band identical' at far coordinates as if it were the cause: the naive divisor gives the same band there, mean difference 0.84 to 0.95 of 255, no pixel off by more than 12.

StrataTerrace: 'what stock Terrace and the two-Terrace graphs did not give is flat caps, cliffs and plain slopes in one stack'. Add(Max(S, Terrace(S)), Plane) in stock nodes gives exactly that on seeds 1337 and 7; the alternating caprock profile is Max( s, Terrace( s, 2T ) ).
StrataTerrace: hashed thickness jitter and the talus power are part of the look. Relief with tjit=0,tpow=1 is visually indistinguishable from the default.
StrataBands: 'the node with jitter and contrast off reads as zebra stripes at matched density'. The proto with jit=0,ajit=0,lat=0 on stretched Perlin still reads as wood and is close to the default.
GrowthAge: 'Vol at iso 0.58 is a timber block whose grain grooves agree across faces, with a knot on top'. At iso 0.58 with the default params the isosurface is a stack of thin splintery sheets.

GrowthAge: c0ratio 3.14 with max slope 351 through Timber at 10 rings. The default check measures c0ratio 1.71 and max slope 651 per unit (the thinnest jittered ring), so the rings alias harder than reported.
StrataTerrace 3D: overhanging caps are new. density + PingPong(Gradient along the strata axis) in stock nodes also undercuts ledges, though the proto's mushroom caps are cleaner.

'mode=5,K=13,N=4 is nearly pinhole free': failed. On the prototyper's own counter it is worse than bisection in all 4 cases run: 25/43 vs 12/28, 134/842 vs 33/287, 172/382 vs 73/177, 34/134 vs 10/76 (islands/px). It is better only on wrong-root area, 0.84% vs 3.71% at t=1.5 on seed 1337.
'The entropy root removes pinholes (K21 leaves 2 px)': true only on seed 1337 at t=1.5. Seed 90210 gives 6 islands/52 px against bisection's 10/76, and t=3 gives 49/163.

The pinhole counts understate bisection. The counter only sees islands of 40 px or less, so 28 px of pinholes sit alongside 3.71% of pixels on the wrong root and 42 thick islands against a converged reference.

'Asymmetric sawtooth that no existing node or graph produces': partly false. A stock Modulus of a tilted plane plus Perlin, added to Perlin, gives one-sided ramps and cliffs at 4.59/7.75/12.60 ns AVX2. What it cannot do is make shocks that start, end, merge and vary in height.

'Breaking time 0.32 for 3 octaves': measured .273-.304 over 3 seeds. The 1 and 5 octave figures hold. The prototyper's list also stops at 5 octaves: it keeps falling to .181-.188 at oct 8 for gain .5, and only saturates below gain x lacunarity 1, for example gain .35 at about .30-.32.

'Steepen the coarse octave and add fine detail raw is the intended graph': it keeps some silhouette, but in relief the fronts largely drown under detail. Gain .35 with all octaves steepened looks clearly better, at 86.5x vs 23.5x perlin2 scalar.
'Banding argues against even a viscous option': failed. Banding came from sliding point-sampled taps. An exact segment integral over locked taps gives c0ratio 7.97-7.99 and no ripples.
'Zone .15-.35 turns scarps into drag folds': the image shows the fault trace gone and the layers simply folding. Real drag needs a residual jump, which is what the new zres parameter adds.
'Throw gives fault-block terrain with tilted blocks': the code adds only a height step per slab, with no per-block tilt, and the image reads as rugged hills with thin scarps.
'Faint per-family parallel lattice in wide views': not reproduced. I could not see it or in my own window 32 renders. The visible limit is 6 orientations.

The idea's claim that graphs cannot make slip discontinuities or cross-cutting offsets: false. A stock DomainRotate, DomainOffset, Terrace chain does both. The node's case rests on usability, dip, tips and 4D, not on the look.

'3x3 window audited: 0-10 px': seed flattering. Seed 90210 gives 13 of 65536 at default settings and 63 at drift .3 rot .8 gap .15, with max diff .85. These are tiny clipped pieces, so the window is still fine with drift clamped.
'Unlike F2-F1 the gap width varies': a stock F2-F1 with a per plate threshold also gives uneven gaps and a close mask silhouette. The real difference is rotation, per-plate texture and tilted slabs.
'Full 3D plate cost ~80-100 ns': scalar measured 10.4x worley3 implies about 125 ns against the 12 ns handbook figure. This is an estimate, not a SIMD measurement.

'A tangential flip across a closed loop reads as rotation' as the reason shear faults fail: incomplete. A rigid offset across closed loops has no rotation, stays clean, and still reads as lenses. Closed curved traces fail on their own.

'Self mode is in kind the same as DomainWarpGradient or a curl warp': the DomainWarpGradient, Progressive and Independent graphs I rendered have no such hairline creases. It is still not worth a node, because shear-flow covers that ground.

TileDomain 'the speed command reads 2.98x-5.13x': the fan cobbles recipe with its fbm source reads 12.79x Perlin in the speed command (fan alone with out=EdgeDistance reads 5.12x); the 3.06x headline is the parquet config only.

Textile knit 'reads as chunky stockinette': at seed 5, window 16, it reads as twisted-rope columns and vertical ribbing, and the wide view is plain vertical stripes; thinner yarn turns it into chain-link, not knit.

FiberNoise fur cost is understated in the summary: the fur recipe (path=0, K=6, field angle) measures 26.1x Perlin in the speed command; the report quotes only the resolved 17.7x and a 14.5x speed figure for K=2.
LevelSetWeave headline c0ratio 7.96 does not belong to its recipe params: src=4,k=1.2,cell=0.3,mode=1 measures 2.99 (round-profile rim); 7.96-8.05 is reached only with prof=1 or the Textile mode.

HeightBlend '1.64x to 1.71x less cost': with real nodes in fnlab AVX2 the saving is larger, about 2.1x in 2D (21.4 vs 10.0 ns) and 1.8-2.1x in 3D/4D; and the GeneratorCache remark, which the prototyper only read from code, is now measured: wrapping every source in GeneratorCache gives 21.9 ns vs 21.4 ns, no saving.

'A graph cannot build it' is false. FractalFBm with Gain=Remap(same-seed Simplex) gives top/bottom roughness 19.5 against Hetero's 14.1, correlation 0.991, at 8.56 ns against 7.23 AVX2 2D. FBm g.84 WS1 gives 8.8 at 7.28 ns with no graph. Hetero via PowFloat(e, FBm) gives correlation 0.994 and a nearly matching roughness curve.
'FBm Weighted only mildly smooths its lows' holds only at gain .5 WS .8 (ratio 2.5), which was the only setting compared. The same node at gain 1 WS 1 reaches 12.4.

'Glassy flat lowland floor' overstates it. Hetero's lowlands are smooth bowls of the first octave. Actual flats need a floor such as MaxSmooth, and the real-node recipe with a floor looks better than Hetero.
'No analytic range' is false for Hetero. The bound gives 4.48 / 6.01 / 6.59 / 14.08 against measured 4.31 / 5.27 / 5.42 / 10.77.
Range-table defaults are not bounds. At seed 5, p-model inter 1.5 reaches 6.77 against 6.31, Hetero 6 octaves reaches 5.45, and Hybrid g.84 spans -1.46..6.05 against -1.63..5.99.

The range table is 2D only. With off .7 on the lab simplex3g, Hetero has 0.00% of samples below zero and max about 3.4 in 3D, so the prototype's defaults do not carry over. Real 3D Simplex was not measured.
'Flat voids of all sizes' is false at gain .5. Measured area with a zero factor: inter 1.5 only octave 0 (14.2%); inter 2.5 octave 0 (28.3%) and octave 1 (6.9%); all others 0%.

Cascade-mesas as a look 'neither FBm, ridged nor the other modes give' is not a reason for a node. A real graph of clamped Remap, PowFloat and Divide reads as the same genre at seed 99, though it costs 22.55 ns AVX2 2D with the subtree duplicated.
'Merge percolation into a Weight option' is unnecessary. The Mask is three clamped Remaps in two Multiply nodes at 5.62 ns AVX2 2D.
The RidgedMulti comparison image pits it against FBm Weighted (mode 6), not FractalRidged, so it does not show what was claimed. The conclusion survives: real FractalRidged g.7 WS1 is close.

Root-vein 'needs about 100 px or more per primary spacing' applied to the old defaults. With the new defaults speck at 64 px is 4.86% against 11.28%, and it stays readable. Branches crossing the parent and the closed web were treated as inherent, but both are fixable with side and gap.

Scalar ratios are weak cost evidence in these prototypes. Root-vein going from 10 to 7 evals only moved 644 to 516 ns, so 560 vs 558 ns says little by itself. The real-node bench is what supports the cost statements.

wave-noise-sliced: 'Real N=8 ... no lattice in the wide view' and 'N=8 tilt .5 is the new default'. At seed 7, window 24-32, N=8 shows the blobs lined up in straight chains along the 8 wave directions in both 2D and the XZ slice; N=16 is needed, which moves the cost to 12.5-15 ns by the prototyper's own table.

wave-noise-sliced: 'Ridged ... 3D thin membrane foam, the best 3D result of the family'. FractalRidged(Octaves=1, Source=Simplex) at iso .5 rendered with fnlab gives the same membrane foam and the same 2D closed-loop net. It is an existing graph.

wave-noise-sliced: the Wired wide panel 'one faint horizontal line' is wave 0 being exactly axis aligned (angle -90 degrees); at seed 7 window 32 it is a long bright row across the whole field. A half-step offset of the direction table removes it.
wave-noise cost answer: 'the default is 5.1-8.6x Perlin in 2D'. That default is the N=8 configuration with visible direction chains; the clean configuration is about 9-11x.

cyclic-noise: 'the final form ... removes the rows (r .072)'. The rows are gone, but at seed 7 window 32 the whole field is sheared along one diagonal at decorS 6, 9 and 14 alike, so seeds still share a fabric direction fixed by the slice axes.

cyclic-noise: 'reads as different from warp graphs'. Different from the two graphs the prototyper rendered, but the existing Warp Fractal Progressive panel on the existing-nodes sheet is the same wispy-marbling family without the shear bias; the gap is smaller than reported.
spanning-maze: 'hidden by any warp'. The shown warp 0.3 f0.5 leaves plain row and column banding at window 24 (FFT axis 52).

spanning-maze: the topology guarantee is only safe for near-injective warps. Warp 0.6 f0.5 gives 34 corridor and 62 wall enclosed pieces, warp 1.0 gives 864 and 497, warp 0.3 f1.0 gives 25 corridor. The prototyper tested only warp 0 and 0.3 at f0.5, where its numbers do hold.

spanning-maze: '4D is the same code path' holds for the rule (0 cycles in 4D) but gives no tile. The GenTileable2D torus slice is window-pane fragments with 161 enclosed corridor pieces, largest 1.6%. Any 2D slice of the 3D form has the same problem.
barchan-field: est_avx2 6-8 ns. Measured 20-22 ns with ripple, 16.3 ns without, using an AVX2 port that agrees with scalar (worst difference 0.00005).
barchan-field: Sand Supply as a hybrid with binary existence seams, c0ratio 1.02 and max slope 614. Fading each dune by sat((supply-rnd)/w) restores c0ratio 8.06.
barchan-field: 'crescent fins' is largely the terrain colour ramp. The same params in a sand ramp with a side sun read as barchans. The flat plain complaint was correct.
light-cone-ca: scalar_vs_perlin 3.06 misleads. AVX2 gens=4 is 29.6 ns measured, 33x AVX2 Perlin at 0.90 ns.
light-cone-ca: 'real but modest difference' came from a 3-octave FBm baseline. One octave of SuperSimplex x20 clamped (2.79 ns) nearly erases it.
light-cone-ca: pyramid est 60-100 ns looks 2-3x low. My estimate is ~205 ns, scalar 1577 ns divided by the measured 7.7 scalar/AVX2 ratio.
light-cone-ca: 'no specks after 3-4 gens'. Faint gray single-cell dots remain at gens 4. Minor.

Template forest 'looked much the same as unique trees': at window 4 the one-template forest repeats visibly (same silhouette rotated in several cells). The 1.79x speed-up reproduces only in the AVX2 sketch (156.9 to 87.8 ns); the scalar prototype shows none (3189 vs 3180 ns).

Newton 'real fronds and lobed borders': seed dependent. Seed 3 at the same params has fronds in only a few small zones and seed 11 at window 16 is a speckled mosaic; sheet axis stays 14 to 19 after the offsets, so a mild lattice alignment remains.

Knot tube 'c0ratio 8.11': with the hero params the check returns a constant -1 field (c0ratio 0.00, std 0, seed sensitivity 0); the continuity figure comes from other params and the checks are not meaningful for a single centred object.
Knot '2D is a whirlpool of scales': true at the centre only. At window 16 it is one spiral whose scales grow to screen size away from the centre; it is not a texture.
Coral 2D twig mode 'useful as a mask': one equal-size tree per cell shows as a lattice of glyphs in the wide view (axis 8.06).
Family answer 'all three are proved on look; none is killed': newton-basins does not survive a different seed or the wide view, and its only non-graph content (lace) is a minority of the area.
fisk: est AVX2 20-28 ns (G=1) and 55-80 ns (G=3) is about 3x low. Measured 73-77 and 220-230 ns with a port at parity (worst 0.00115). The borrowed 47x scalar ratio is about 14x for this code.
fisk: G1 everywhere is false at defaults. Breakpoint kinks p50 9.9, p90 23.2, p99 36.6, max 62.2 deg, caused by jv=0.15. jv=0 gives exactly 0.
fisk: tangent-continuous rivers is false at oxbows. Chute corners p50 120, min 100, max 154 deg; they read as straight canal segments on seeds 7, 42, 2024 and were not listed as an artifact.
fisk: goosenecks with narrow necks overstates it. 0.0% of doubling-back bends have a loop over 2x the neck; median neck gap 0.57 Lc against channel half width 0.11.
fisk: warp=0.4 does not break the parallel belts. It takes warp 2.5 at frequency 0.05 plus per-river bend length.
fisk: dead flat trench relief was partly the view. hscale 90 on a -1..0.3 range; hscale 18-22 with a low relief Add reads as a floodplain.
chiral: warp cost |G/T| x modes sinusoids is wrong. After merging, 4 or 6 wave vectors for every group. Measured p6m 4.7 ns against 12-24, p3 and p6 4.7 against 6-12, p4 2.06 against 4-8.
chiral: fold about 1 ns is true only for hex (0.98). Rect and square measure 0.15-0.18 ns.
chiral: each enum entry is exactly its group fails at chi=0 (14 of 17 collapse) and at modes=1 (pg->pm, pgg->pmg at seed 21). The proposed Modes 1-4 range must be 2-4.
chiral: passes the source range through is false. Per-seed range is narrow and seed dependent, e.g. -0.18..0.15 at seed 99 k=1 and -0.67..0.42 at seed 7 k=1. Auto-ranged images hide this.
chiral: the prototyper's group test ran at rounds=4 and tested mirrors only about the origin. It holds when retested at rounds=2 with a full search, so the result stands but that test was weak.
bubble: the 3D vol shown (stripe slabs) undersells it; a cellular source gives nested sphere clusters. Other bubble claims held.

holes_round2: Motion: nothing was judged in motion. Render z-slice strips for CausticWeb, DomainWarpFlow, ripple-noise, and any Time hybrid.
Clouds: a cheap 3D cumulus-like primitive. Wispy density as well as cauliflower.
Water surface beyond ChoppyOcean: Gerstner or spectrum-targeted sums.
Filtering and LOD: a hybrid Filter Width on hard-edged nodes, octave fade by footprint.
Deposition and slope limiting: the erosion filter carves but never fills.
Rivers at building-block cost: all three tree nodes are above 50x Perlin scalar.
Sphere-native lattices, and a real latitude utility.
Organic surfaces: bark plates, skin pores, leather, rosettes.
Column awareness: dependency-aware 2D prepass on grid generation (architecture question).
Value plus gradient as a public output, and id plus distance from one lattice pass (architecture question).
From queue.md: Generic Reseed, Lazy selection, per-octave Time control, Surface-relative 3D helpers, Long-range structure, Vector-field algebra, Spectrum-targeted noise, 4D-native designs.
notes.proto_index_note: ns2 and ns3 are WASM ns/sample of Eval2 and Eval3 at the idea params, one thread in Node. has3d: Eval3 changes with z. eval3Varies shows each coordinate, an Eval3 ignoring y is an extrusion.
